title: Myles Garrett on Aaron Donald: A difficult decision, don't want to push him
summary: Garrett thinks a pairing with Donald would lead to "great things."
full_text: ' Myles Garrett's arrival in Los Angeles sparked talk of Aaron Donald coming back to play for the Rams in 2026, but Garrett isn't going to try to sell Donald on returning to the NFL after two years of retirement. Rams head coach Sean McVay said earlier this week that he has no news of an " imminent decision " from Donald about whether he'll join Garrett on the Rams' defensive line. Garrett spoke to reporters from Rams training camp on Wednesday about the difficulty of "getting back to that tempo" after so much time away from the game, but said he believes Donald would be able to do it "for however many games he chooses to play." Garrett did not make it sound like he plans to tell Donald that or anything else because he believes the ultimate decision has to come from Donald himself. “I’d love to learn from him," Garrett said. "I’ve watched his tape. Everyone who’s been a rusher from anywhere across the line, they have a lot of respect for him. I don't want to push him in one way or another. If he's here, I'm going to be excited to be his teammate, his partner in crime. And I think we can do great things, but it's a difficult thing coming back, and I know he has a family. He has a lot of decisions to make. Last thing he needs is me to push him in one direction or another. I’m gonna support him either way and I look forward to seeing whatever happens." Donald has been on a workout regimen to help him determine if he's physically up to the task or returning to the NFL trenches and it's not clear when any decision about his plans will come. That uncertainty seems fine with the Rams as getting Donald back would be a finishing touch to a roster that's already in strong shape thanks in part to Garrett's presence.
author: Josh Alper

title: Will Anderson: I had two high-ankle sprains on the MetLife turf, real grass is better
summary: Anderson has missed games due to injuries twice in his NFL career. Both times, the injuries were suffered at MetLife Stadium.
full_text: ' In his NFL career, Texans defensive end Will Anderson has only missed games due to injuries twice: In 2023, when he suffered a high-ankle sprain against the Jets on the turf at MetLife Stadium, and in 2024, when he suffered another high-ankle sprain against the Jets on the turf at MetLife Stadium. He doesn't think that's a coincidence. Asked about the use of real grass in the World Cup, both at MetLife and at the Texans' NRG Stadium, Anderson said it's the superior playing surface. “Yes, most definitely. I would most definitely say grass. Grass 100 percent," Anderson said. "I think it's just the natural feel of grass, your feet not getting stuck in the ground like in turf. I had two high ankle sprains up in MetLife because of the turf. I think grass is just a better option.” Still, Anderson said he hasn't talked to the Texans about using a grass field in Houston for NFL games. “Not really. At the end of the day, it's up to them. They'll figure it out. You just control what you can control. Go out there and play and do your job," Anderson said. The two times in his career that Anderson couldn't do his job, artificial turf was the reason.
author: Michael David Smith

title: De'Von Achane: If teams aren't taking the Dolphins seriously, they'll have a long day
summary: "We're kind of used to that," Achane said of being overlooked. "We don't pay no mind to that."
full_text: Miami running back De'Von Achane is aware that the Dolphins are not viewed as contenders this year, and he's happy to be on a team that opponents are overlooking. Achane said he and his teammates will be ready to make other teams regret looking past them. "We're kind of used to that," Achane said. "We don't pay no mind to that. If teams feel that way about us, that means when they play us, they're gonna be not taking us seriously. And if you're doing that, then you're gonna have a long day for yourself." Achane, who said he has a goal of leading the league in rushing, signed a four-year, $64 million contract this offseason. That was a significant investment from the Dolphins, who are a rebuilding team but think Achane is a big part of their future. As for this season, if Achane likes having people overlook his team, the good news is that a lot of people are: The betting odds say the Dolphins are the least likely to make the playoffs of any team in the AFC.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Jamal Adams on joining the Vikings: "The sky's the limit"
summary: Veteran defender Jamal Adams joined the Vikings not long before the opening of training camp.
full_text: Veteran defender Jamal Adams joined the Vikings not long before the opening of training camp. On Wednesday, he spoke to Minnesota reporters for the first time. Adams said he was attracted to Minnesota by the presence of G.M. Nolan Teasley and defensive coordinator Brian Flores. Adams spent time with Teasley in Seattle, and he has always respected Flores from afar. "There's certain DCs in the league that you pray that you could play for him one day, and, you know, he fits me, man, and we fit each other," Adams said, via Darren Wolfson of KSTP. Now that Adams is in Minnesota, where can his career go in his tenth NFL season? "I mean, the sky's the limit, man. I just have to get back healthy," Adams said. Adams explained the difficulty in fully recovering the quad tendon tear he suffered in Week 1 of the 2022 season. "You know, when you tear your tendon, it takes time," Adams said. "It takes years to really get it back to yourself. You might heal, but you're not back to yourself, mentally and physically. So I just had to get back healthy and, clearly, I just — I know what I can do. I know what I can bring to the table, just got to be out there, you know, fully locked and loaded." He said the effort to overcome the injury made it hard for him to perform at a high level, even though he was able to return to action in 2023. "I wasn't confident," Adams said. "I knew my knee wasn't, you know, fully back yet. But I knew I was on contract. I had to get out there and go out there and sacrifice. I wanted to play with my guys. I went out there, did what I could, but my knee just never could give it to me each and every week, as far as practicing. I'm a practice player. I love to practice. I couldn't practice full speed, so when you don't practice full speed, it's hard to kind of go to the game and transition to full speed. So it took time, but I definitely had a lot of doubt, man, and went through a lot of adversity, but I came out on top, and it made me stronger." For now, he's learning the terminology of the Minnesota defense. And he believes he can eventually be extremely flexible as to where he lines up, even if he's officially listed as a linebacker. "I can play linebacker, safety, corner, nose tackle, D-end, kicker," Adams said. "It don't even matter. Whatever you want me to play, I play. You want me to walk the dog? I'll walk the dog." His approach is basic. As he said, it's "see ball, get ball." When he was healthy, he was one of the best at doing that. Nearly four years removed from the injury, who knows what'll happen when he's added to a defense that can take full advantage of a player who can do a lot of different things?
author: Mike Florio

title: 49ers should have promptly disclosed that Kyle Shanahan was in an accident
summary: The 2026 offseason has featured multiple P.R. failures by NFL teams.
full_text: The 2026 offseason has featured multiple P.R. failures by NFL teams. The first was the handling of the Mike Vrabel-Dianna Russini situation by the Patriots. The latest happened when the 49ers failed to promptly disclose that coach Kyle Shanahan had been in a car accident, holding the information for 11 days. There was no reason to delay acknowledging the fact that an accident had happened. The accident is different from the injuries. The 49ers could have announced that Shanahan was involved in an accident, that he suffered non-life-threatening injuries, and that further information would be disclosed at the appropriate time. He's not a private citizen. He's a public figure. He's the head coach of one of the 32 NFL teams. Basic transparency is a must. Really, what was the point of hiding the fact that the accident happened? The details of the injuries or the events leading to the incident could have waited. It would have been fair and appropriate for the 49ers to disclose that the accident happened. Beyond the fact that this is part of the life NFL head coaches have chosen, thousands of people bet millions of dollars on sports. At this time of year, gamblers wager on teams to make the playoffs, win a certain number of games, make the playoffs, win the division, advance to the Super Bowl, and/or win the Super Bowl. The fact that an NFL head coach was in a car accident should not have been treated like a state secret in a climate where every bit of information is potentially relevant to the decisions made by bettors. The absence of transparency in these matters creates inside information that can be misused by those who bet. Certain basic information must be disclosed promptly — especially if people within the team and/or the league knew about it. Clearly, plenty of people knew about the Shanahan accident. The 49ers organization knew. Media figures, like Chris Simms, knew. ESPN obviously knew; it coordinated with the 49ers in the belated rollout of the information about the accident and the injuries. Many have suggested this week that Shanahan is entitled to privacy. While true as to the injuries, it's false as to the accident. That's relevant information to those who follow the 49ers specifically and the NFL generally, and to those who may be inclined to place NFL-related wagers. There was nothing to gain by hiding the fact that an accident happened. In the end, it simply created the impression that the 49ers possibly had something to hide.
author: Mike Florio

title: Lamar Jackson on landing at 69 on player's top 100 list: "I don't care about rankings"
summary: With training camps open, list season has mercifully ended.
full_text: '''' With training camps open, list season has mercifully ended. One of the most significant developments in this year's collection of slow-time one-through-whatever efforts to differentiate players was the ridiculous placement of Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson in the NFL Network players-only list of the top 100 players in the league. Jackson finished at No. 69, down 67 spots from 2025 . Jackson was asked about the placement on the NFLN list during his first press conference of training camp on Wednesday. "It is what it is," Jackson said. "You know, I play football. I don't care about rankings." That's the right attitude. The rankings don't mean anything. They're something for the media to write and talk about and for the fans to react to. Still, it's an opportunity to fashion a legitimate chip on the shoulder for the season to come. But Jackson doesn't seem to be motivated by actual or perceived slights. He goes about his business. And, in relation to the rest of the league, there's no way 68 other players go about their business better than him.
author: Mike Florio

title: The Gabe Jacas injury waiver is unusual
summary: The Patriots and linebacker Gabe Jacas took a long time to work out a rookie contract for reasons unrelated to the standard terms of his rookie deal.
full_text: The Patriots and linebacker Gabe Jacas took a long time to work out a rookie contract for reasons unrelated to the standard terms of his rookie deal. The problem was that Jacas has a pre-existing injury for which the team wanted financial protection. As explained by Ben Volin of the Boston Globe , the Jacas contract has an injury waiver regarding his left knee . The fact that he's on the non-football injury list suggests that his left knee injury has kept him from passing a pre-training camp physical. Per Volin, the first three years of Jacas's contract are fully guaranteed, along with roughly 17.5 percent of the fourth year. The injury waiver covers the 2027 and 2028 league years. It means that the injury guarantee doesn't cover the left knee in those two seasons. As a source with extensive knowledge regarding contract negotiations and injury waivers explained it to PFT, the unusual insertion of an injury waiver into a slotted rookie deal points to three possible explanations: (1) failing to disclose a medical condition at the Scouting Combine; (2) suffering an injury after the Scouting Combine and before the draft; or (3) sustaining an injury away from the team facility after the player was drafted. For Jacas, there weren't many alternatives to accepting the injury waiver. He could have refused to sign the contract including the injury waiver, sat out the year, and re-entered the draft. But what would that have gotten him? He most likely wouldn't have been drafted any higher in 2027, and he would have gone a year without playing football — and without getting paid. There's also a question of whether, if he suffered the injury while working out on his own after the Combine or after the draft, the Patriots should not have insisted on the injury waiver, since he was doing what he needed to do to stay in shape for football season. If, alternatively, Jacas suffered the injury in some other way, it becomes more reasonable to take the position that the guarantees for 2027 and 2028 don't apply to the damaged knee. Whatever the explanation, it's a rare situation. Teams draft players on an as-is basis. If they know or had reason to know about a player's injury history, that becomes a factor as to when he's picked. And if the Patriots had been insisting on an injury waiver for a condition that they knew or should have known about before picking him, Jacas, his agent, and the NFL Players Association should be making a stink about it. They aren't. Which points to one of the three explanations listed above. And which forced Jacas to either agree to the waiver and sign the deal he was offered, or to not play this year and roll the dice in the 2027 draft.
author: Mike Florio

title: Quinnen Williams wants to be in Dallas "for the long haul"
summary: The Cowboys gave up two high draft picks to get Quinnen Williams from the Jets.
full_text: The Cowboys gave up two high draft picks to get Quinnen Williams from the Jets. The defensive lineman still has two years left on the four-year, $96 million deal he signed in 2023, but the Cowboys didn't give up what they gave up for 2 1/2 seasons of Williams. Cowboys executive vice president Stephen Jones said Tuesday that the team wants to begin contract extension talks with Williams' representation during training camp. "He's at the top of our list," Jones said. After 6 1/2 seasons in New York, Williams has found a home in Dallas. He would like nothing better than to make it his final stop. "I definitely want to be here for the long haul," Williams said Wednesday, via Joseph Hoyt of the Dallas Morning News . "I definitely would love being here for the long haul, but I want to win, and that's really the only thing I'm focused on is winning and getting this defense into the groove where we can win football games for this team." His price likely went up after Eagles defensive tackle Jalen Carter recently signed a four-year, $152 million deal following Jeffery Simmons' three-year, $105.8 million extension with the Titans. "It's pretty cool to see the guys get paid," Williams said. Williams didn't know that the Cowboys had preliminary talks with his agent this offseason. He reiterated that he is focused only on helping the Cowboys win.
author: Charean Williams

title: Former Chargers LB Billy Ray Smith dies at 64
summary: Former Chargers linebacker Billy Ray Smith Jr. died Wednesday, his family announced.
full_text: '' Former Chargers linebacker Billy Ray Smith Jr. died Wednesday, his family announced. He was 64. "It is with profound sadness that we share the loss of our beloved Billy Ray Smith Jr., who passed away peacefully surrounded by family," the family said in a statement. "Billy Ray faced his long journey with dementia caused by CTE with unmatched bravery, dignity, and strength. "Billy Ray brought so much joy, light, and laughter to the world as a devoted father, husband, son, and loyal friend. On the NFL gridiron for a decade with the Chargers, and decades that followed in sports broadcasting, Billy Ray earned deep respect from teammates, colleagues, and fans, who he cherished in return. "He leaves an irreplaceable void in our lives. His undeniable legacy will live forever in our hearts, and we thank our incredible community for the outpouring of love and support." The Chargers made Smith the fifth overall pick in 1983 out of the University of Arkansas, where he was a two-time unanimous All-American. He finished eighth in Defensive Rookie of the Year voting. He played all 10 seasons of his NFL career with the Chargers, totaling 26.5 sacks, 15 interceptions and 13 forced fumbles in 126 games. Smith was a member of the Chargers' 50th Anniversary Team. After his retirement, Smith became a sports broadcaster on TV, radio and online.
author: Charean Williams

title: Taysom Hill bids farewell to New Orleans, though his future is unclear
summary: Hill spent nine seasons with the Saints, playing quarterback, wide receiver and tight end.
full_text: ' Free agent Taysom Hill doesn't know where his future is, but he knows it's not in New Orleans. After nine seasons with the Saints, the quarterback/tight end/wide receiver bid the team and the city farewell. "For the last nine years, New Orleans has been so much more than the city where I played," Hill said in a statement. "It's where my family built a life, where our oldest son was born, and where we formed relationships and made memories that will stay with us forever. "I've taken time this offseason to think carefully about what comes next for my family and me. I still don't have a clear answer about what the future holds, but I know that returning to New Orleans is not in the cards. As training camp begins, I didn't want my silence to be misinterpreted, and as hard as it is to put into words, I wanted to express my gratitude." Hill, who will turn 36 in August, has been most closely linked with the Broncos if his career continues. He played for Broncos head coach Sean Payton for five seasons. In his career, Hill has 2,551 rushing yards, 1,034 receiving yards and 2,426 passing yards. He's the first player in the Super Bowl era to have more than 1,000 yards as a receiver, runner and passer.
author: Charean Williams

title: Kellen Moore confirms Bryan Bresee's knee injury "doesn't look great"
summary: Not long after defensive tackle Bryan Bresee went down with a knee injury came word that the Saints feared a torn ACL.
full_text: Not long after defensive tackle Bryan Bresee went down with a knee injury came word that the Saints feared a torn ACL. Saints coach Kellen Moore appeared on WWL Radio on Wednesday afternoon and confirmed that the initial diagnosis didn't deliver good news. "No one kind of ran into each other; no one fell on anyone," Moore said. "It was just kind of a goofy deal where obviously something unfortunately happened and so it took a little bit, I think, for him to realize what it felt like. It felt like a little bit of something and then once they checked it out, obviously we’ll continue to finalize all that, but it doesn’t look great .” If the MRI confirms Bresee tore his ACL, his season will end on injured reserve. The Saints have Davon Godchaux, Nathan Shepherd, rookie Christen Miller, Vernon Broughton and John Ridgeway, among others, at the position. "That’s the cycle of the NFL and in an unfortunate but opportunistic way," Moore said. "Guys unfortunately go through things and they don’t become available, and it’s the opportunity for someone else to step up and take advantage. . . . And so if Bryan is out for a while, certainly, we’re going to expect a lot of these other guys to take the next step.” The Saints exercised Bresee's fifth-year option this offseason, so he is under contract for next season. New Orleans made Bresee a first-round pick in 2023, and he has totaled 86 tackles, 19 tackles for loss, 14.5 sacks, and two forced fumbles in 49 career games. He started all 15 games he played in 2025.
author: Charean Williams

title: Seahawks sign undrafted rookie WR Kyre Duplessis
summary: The Seahawks signed wide receiver Kyre Duplessis on Wednesday, the team announced.
full_text: The Seahawks signed wide receiver Kyre Duplessis on Wednesday, the team announced. The Seahawks had an open roster spot after waiving Kenny McIntosh on Monday. Duplessis was an undrafted free agent who briefly was on the Lions' 90-player roster. He played at Delaware in 2025, recording 60 catches for 824 yards and five touchdowns. Duplessis spent four seasons at Coastal Carolina before transferring to Delaware. He made 23 receptions for 348 yards for the Chanticleers.
author: Charean Williams

title: Maxx Crosby: I have a little more reason to go out there and whoop ass
summary: Maxx Crosby has a chip on his shoulder, but the Raiders pass rusher says it's always there "no matter what."
full_text: Maxx Crosby has a chip on his shoulder, but the Raiders pass rusher says it's always there "no matter what." He was a two-star recruit with only an offer from Eastern Michigan, and he didn't get drafted until the fourth round in 2019. Crosby admits, though, that the chip might be a bit bigger than in past seasons. The Ravens agreed to trade for him before reneging because of long-term concerns about Crosby's surgically repaired left knee. He missed two games last season to undergo surgery to repair a torn meniscus. “Of course, there’s added motivation ,” Crosby said, via Sam Warren of TheAthletic.com. “It’s beautiful at the same time. I love being doubted. I love being told I can’t do something because I’ll go to the end of the world to make it happen.” Crosby fully participated in the Raiders' opening training camp practice after spending the offseason program rehabbing. Thus, Wednesday marked his first practice since December. “It’s a blessing, man,” Crosby said. “I love this game. I heard all the noise and all those things, but everyone knows that when my back’s against the wall, that’s when I’m at my best. I love the pressure. That’s what I live and thrive on. It’s just added points and gives me a little more reason to go out there and whoop ass.”
author: Charean Williams

title: Alvin Kamara doesn't have a chip on his shoulder, but he is motivated
summary: Running back Alvin Kamara agreed to a reported $5.5 million pay cut to stay in New Orleans, because "this is where I wanted to be."
full_text: '' Running back Alvin Kamara agreed to a reported $5.5 million pay cut to stay in New Orleans, because "this is where I wanted to be." But at 31, headed into his 10th season and no longer the lead back, Kamara has every reason to have a chip on his shoulder even if he insists he doesn't have one. " I’m motivated every year ," Kamara said Wednesday, via Matthew Paras of nola.com. "A chip? No. Pissed? Maybe." Former teammate Terron Armstead had suggested "pissed off" was the best way to describe Kamara's emotions. Kamara played 11 games in 2025, with 131 carries for a career-low 471 yards and a career-low one touchdown. That prompted the Saints to sign Travis Etienne in the offseason. The Saints, though, know who Kamara is and what he can do, and the five-time Pro Bowler will have a role. “Credit to Alvin, he always does a great job during the offseason of really training himself and putting himself to be in a position ready to go,” coach Kellen Moore said. “You certainly see that when he’s out there on the field. We feel great about the situation.”
author: Charean Williams

title: Sean Payton on Jonathon Cooper: We're staying the course with league protocol
summary: Broncos linebacker Jonathon Cooper didn't take part in the team's minicamp after being arrested twice on domestic violence charges, but he is back with the team and participated in their first practice of training camp on Wednesday.
full_text: Broncos linebacker Jonathon Cooper didn’t take part in the team's minicamp after being arrested twice on domestic violence charges, but he is back with the team and participated in their first practice of training camp on Wednesday. Head coach Sean Payton said on Wednesday that he, General Manager George Paton and team owner Greg Penner all met with Cooper after the arrests and that Cooper completed a counseling program that the team made part of his path to returning. Payton said he is "proud" of the work that Cooper has done since the arrest and that the team will "see where it goes." “We’re staying the course with league protocol, we're staying the course with club protocol, relative to what we’re advised to do,” Payton said, via Denver Sports 104.3. “He’s been fantastic working away from the building, and we’ll continue to do that, and monitor it. We’re supportive, and very much aware of the seriousness of these types of things.” Cooper faces an August 31 arraignment on multiple charges, including second-degree count assault by strangulation. In addition to his legal case, Cooper faces potential league discipline under the Personal Conduct Policy.
author: Josh Alper

title: Packers make three moves, including activating OG Aaron Banks
summary: The Packers made three moves on Wednesday.
full_text: The Packers made three moves on Wednesday. They activated left guard Aaron Banks and defensive tackle Nazir Stackhouse from the active/physically unable to perform list. The team also placed wide receiver Brenden Rice on the non-football injury list. Banks' stay on PUP did not last long as he passed his physical. He appeared in 15 games last season, starting 14, despite dealing with a back injury in training camp and ankle problems and a stinger last season. The Packers claimed Rice off waivers from the Raiders in May. The son of Hall of Famer Jerry Rice joined Las Vegas' practice squad late last season after also spending time on the practice squads of the Seahawks and Patriots. He was with the Chargers in training camp last summer.
author: Charean Williams

title: Todd Bowles: There's always distractions, these happen to be two of our biggest players
summary: The Buccaneers entered training camp with a pair of contract impasses taking center stage.
full_text: ' The Buccaneers entered training camp with a pair of contract impasses taking center stage. Quarterback Baker Mayfield is expected to play out the season on the final year of his deal after failing to come to agreement on an extension this offseason and defensive tackle Vita Vea requested a trade after trying to land a new contract of his own. At a press conference, Bowles was asked about keeping the focus on football as the negotiations play out publicly and said he isn't worried about players taking their eyes off the ball. "Well, there [are] players every year [that] you're going to have them [with]. These happen to be two of our biggest players," Bowles said, via a transcript from the team. "We haven't had two of our biggest in a while, but we've had players every year. It just hasn't been of that magnitude. But, it's always about football. There [are] always going to be distractions just like there are on game day. There are going to be sudden changes and there are going to be sudden changes on the field. We have a very professional and mature group with a lot of leadership there, starting with Baker. So, he makes sure that's separate. He makes sure the team knows that's separate. Like I said, we're not going to make this training camp about what he signed or what he didn't sign or it being his contract year. We're just going to play ball." Bowles said questions about whether there's a chance of continued contract talks with Mayfield should be addressed to General Manager Jason Licht. Mayfield may have an opportunity to address that first while Bowles keeps his attention on making sure the team is ready to go for Week 1.
author: Josh Alper

title: Harold Fannin fully cleared after offseason groin surgery
summary: Browns tight end Harold Fannin Jr. missed all of the offseason program with an undisclosed injury.
full_text: Browns tight end Harold Fannin Jr. missed all of the offseason program with an undisclosed injury. Fannin said Wednesday, via Ashley Bastock of cleveland.com, that he required surgery to repair the groin injury he sustained in Week 17. His rehab lasted 6-8 weeks, with doctors clearing him two weeks ago. Fannin is full go at training camp. He reported early to try to catch up on learning Todd Monken's offense. In 16 games, with 13 starts, in 2025, Fannin caught 72 passes for 731 yards and six touchdowns. He also scored a rushing touchdown.
author: Charean Williams

title: Kirk Cousins on Raiders QBs: We're all supporting one another and working together
summary: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak was clear with reporters on Tuesday that Kirk Cousins is Las Vegas’ starter, with No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza a part of the group pushing the signal-caller.
full_text: '' Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak was clear with reporters on Tuesday that Kirk Cousins is Las Vegas’ starter, with No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza a part of the group pushing the signal-caller. But Mendoza himself framed that picture a little differently recently, saying that he’s competing with and not against Cousins . What does that mean to the veteran QB? Well, for Cousins, “pushing” and “competing with” are effectively synonyms. “I think that's pro football,” Cousins said, via transcript from the team, when asked about being pushed by the QBs behind him on the depth chart. “I think every day we go out there, we all try to work together and raise the standard every day for one another. I think every position group, we're all competing. I just think that's the world we've lived in even going back to college. They're going to put as many good players in a room as they can and see who can come out as the guy who is taking the spot to play. “We're all supporting one another and working together. That's just the journey we've always been on, and it's pretty much the norm.” On “competing with” Mendoza, Cousins added he feels like that’s “always trying to ask good questions, help one another, challenge one another, and raise the standard. Have fun competing because competition is fun. Have fun doing that together. And I think that's what it will always be.” Cousins noted that when he got into the league, he had Rex Grossman in his QBs room in Washington and asked him questions “maybe to the point of being annoying.” But they built a good rapport that “made a big difference for me in my career.” Cousins is in Las Vegas to play, but there is still a way he can help fill Mendoza in on many of the nuances of playing QB in the league by being a mentor. “I think it's just a great daily conversation in the meeting room, certainly on the practice field, but even in the downtimes in the cafeteria,” Cousins said when asked about Mendoza and mentorship. “The conversation can drift from football to other things, and we can all learn from each other. So, I enjoy being in here with the guys. When I'm at home in the summer, I get a lot of time with my family, which is nice too. But it's also fun to hang out with a bunch of young 25-year-olds with a lot of energy, and they make me laugh. I was laughing almost till I cried yesterday at lunch. The guys are so funny. So, I didn't have that the last six weeks in the summer break. So, it's good to get back with everybody. Cousins appeared in 10 games with eight starts for the Falcons last year, completing 61.7 percent of his passes for 1,721 yards with 10 touchdowns and five interceptions.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Kyler Murray leads off 11-on-11 work at Vikings camp
summary: Murray is competing with J.J. McCarthy for the starting quarterback job.
full_text: The Vikings kicked off training camp on Wednesday and that also served as the kickoff for the final stage of their quarterback competition. Head coach Kevin O'Connell said on Tuesday that Kyler Murray and J.J. McCarthy will both work with the first team as he makes his decision about who will be under center for Week 1. That approach means there will be plenty of attention paid to who gets what repetitions and the first day saw Murray in the lead spot. Jori Epstein of Yahoo Sports reports that Murray was the first man up when the Vikings moved into 11-on-11 work and that he hit wide receiver Jordan Addison for a 30-yard gain. "I’m not really too focused on the long-term vision of it," Murray said before practice. "I’m focused on the process and that’s day to day, coming out here with this walkthrough and then practice later. . . . Prove to the coaches and guys what I’m capable of." McCarthy will get his chances to prove the same point as well and all of the developments on the field in Minnesota will be closely followed until O'Connell makes his call.
author: Josh Alper

title: Lions place OL Giovanni Manu on active/NFI
summary: The Lions placed offensive lineman Giovanni Manu on the active/non-football injury list, the team announced Wednesday.
full_text: The Lions placed offensive lineman Giovanni Manu on the active/non-football injury list, the team announced Wednesday. Manu is competing for a roster spot after the Lions signed veteran Larry Borom and drafted Blake Miller in the first round. The Lions drafted Manu in the third round in 2024, but he played only four games with one start in his first two seasons. Manu didn't play his rookie season and spent part of last season on injured reserve with a knee injury. Time is running out on his tenure in Detroit despite being a second-day draft pick only two years ago.
author: Charean Williams

title: Brandon Beane on Keon Coleman: You feel a guy who has really matured
summary: Bills receiver Keon Coleman became a lightning rod when team owner Terry Pegula referenced him during his January press conference just after firing former head coach Sean McDermott.
full_text: '' Bills receiver Keon Coleman became a lightning rod when team owner Terry Pegula referenced him during his January press conference just after firing former head coach Sean McDermott. But Coleman, who is entering his third season, has handled everything well, as he begins training camp. General Manager Brandon Beane was asked about Coleman in his press conference on Wednesday and said that Coleman as exhibited signs of turning over a new leaf. “If you know Keon through two years, right, and this is Year 3, if you know him the way I know him and the way a lot of his teammates know him, you feel a guy who’s really matured — like the light has come on, he understands some of the things he could’ve done better along the way,” Beane said. "I think back to when I was 21, 22, there’s things that I [feel like], gosh I probably should’ve done that a little bit better. So I like to remind everyone — was his first two years perfect? No. But, if you just talk to him and are around him, you feel a guy growing into his own, comfortable in his skin, and just like, I know that I can’t do the same things that I did the first two years and expect to have success on the field or in the locker room with my teammates. “And his teammates see it. He dropped the first ball today, and I saw like three guys come over and dap him up. Josh [Allen] comes right back to him the next play — a much harder play — and he makes it.” That play captured much of what Beane has liked about Coleman’s 2026 offseason. “I’m very proud of where Keon is,” Beane said. “He could’ve taken the negativity from the press conference thing, the season, the benchings — whatever has happened to him, he has had a positive outlook on things. And I think not only myself, I think everybody in this organization is excited. “He’s still got to go out there and do it. And nothing is given. But I think he’s done everything he could control up to this point.” Coleman, who turned 23 in May, caught 38 passes for 404 yards with four touchdowns in 13 games with six starts last year. He had 29 receptions for 556 yards with four TDs as a rookie in 2024.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Bears activate Montez Sweat from NFI list
summary: The Bears will have one of their best defensive players back on the practice field Thursday.
full_text: The Bears will have one of their best defensive players back on the practice field Thursday. They announced that they have activated defensive end Montez Sweat from the non-football injury list. He went on the list on Tuesday, so he only missed the opening practice of training camp. Sweat started every game for the Bears last season. He had 53 tackles, 10 sacks, three forced fumbles and a fumble recovery in the regular season. Sweat added five tackles, a sack and a forced fumble in the playoffs. Linebacker T.J. Edwards remains on the non-football injury list. Six players, including cornerback Kyler Gordon, are on the physically unable to perform list.
author: Josh Alper

title: Buccaneers sign DT Travis Shaw
summary: Safety Ifeatu Melifonwu wasn't the only defensive player to join the Buccaneers on Wednesday.
full_text: ' Safety Ifeatu Melifonwu wasn't the only defensive player to join the Buccaneers on Wednesday. The team confirmed Melifonwu's signing and also announced that they have signed defensive tackle Travis Shaw to their 90-man roster. Shaw played at North Carolina and Texas before going undrafted this year. He signed with the Patriots after the draft, but was waived earlier this month. The move comes as the Bucs practice without defensive tackle Vita Vea. Vea has requested a trade, but head coach Todd Bowles said that he is on the sideline due to tweaking his back during a conditioning test this week. The Bucs waived defensive lineman Haggai Ndubuisi on Wednesday as well. Ndubuisi signed with the team in April.
author: Josh Alper

title: Malik Nabers participates in practice, but Joe Schoen offers no guarantee about Week 1
summary: Malik Nabers participated in individual drills during the Giants' first practice of the summer.
full_text: '' Malik Nabers participated in individual drills during the Giants' first practice of the summer. The wide receiver backed up what General Manager Joe Schoen said earlier Wednesday about Nabers now running, cutting and sprinting. Schoen, though, softened his stance on Nabers' availability for Week 1, declining to guarantee Nabers will play the season opener. "We've got a really good plan for him," Schoen said, via a transcript from the team. "The medical staff has a really good plan for him, and we're going to always say listen to the patients. So, we're going to see how he reacts. . . . So, as long as everything goes as planned, we'll listen to Malik and his body and again, hopefully he'll be ready, and we'll see how it plays out. But no predictions right now, just because we have a long way to go, still a lot of camp." Nabers tore the ACL and meniscus in his right knee on Sept. 28 against the Chargers. He underwent surgery Oct. 28 but required a second surgery this offseason to remove scar tissue after experiencing stiffness.
author: Charean Williams

title: Panthers sign WR Casey Washington
summary: The Panthers saw a wide receiver go down with an injury at Wednesday's practice and they added another player to the position group later in the day.
full_text: The Panthers saw a wide receiver go down with an injury at Wednesday's practice and they added another player to the position group later in the day. Casey Washington is the new addition to the depth chart. The Panthers announced the move hourse after third-round pick Chris Brazzell was carted off with what's reported to be a torn LCL. Washington was a 2024 sixth-round pick by the Falcons and he was released by Atlanta last month. He had seven catches for 108 yards in 15 appearances for the Falcons over the last two years. The Panthers placed wide receiver and special teamer Dan Chisena on injured reserve in a corresponding move.
author: Josh Alper

title: Tucker Kraft expects to come off active/PUP "very soon"
summary: Packers General Manager Brian Gutekunst said earlier Wednesday that tight end Tucker Kraft will return "sooner rather than later."
full_text: Packers General Manager Brian Gutekunst said earlier Wednesday that tight end Tucker Kraft will return " sooner rather than later ." Kraft, who is on the active/physically unable to perform list, echoed that later Wednesday. Kraft said he expects to begin practicing " very soon ," Ryan Wood of PackersNews.com reports. Kraft tore the ACL in his right knee in a Nov. 2 game against the Panthers. He underwent surgery later that month. The season opener on Sept. 13 is still 46 days away, which is why Gutekunst says Kraft's participation in Week 1 is "very much a possibility." Kraft caught 32 passes for 489 yards and six touchdowns in the eight games last season before his injury.
author: Charean Williams

title: Andy Reid: Mia Bieniemy is out of ICU, making progress
summary: Chiefs head coach Andy Reid shared a positive update on the condition of offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy's wife Mia on Wednesday.
full_text: Chiefs head coach Andy Reid shared a positive update on the condition of offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy's wife Mia on Wednesday. Mia Bieniemy was shot multiple times at the family's home in Virginia on Sunday and was admitted to the intensive care unit at a local hospital as a result of her injuries. The couple's son was arrested and charged with multiple crimes as a result of the shooting. "She's doing great ," Reid said, via Nate Taylor of ESPN.com. "She's doing better and great from where she was. [She's] out of the ICU unit and making progress, so we're happy about that." Eric Bieniemy has been away from the team since the incident and Reid said it's not known when he might return. "Eric's a big part of this," Reid said. "We love having him here, but it's important that he takes care of business and everybody knows that. Eric will be back soon enough to jump in there and do his thing, but he's got to take care of that first." Passing game coordinator Joe Bleymaier is handling the offensive coordinator duties in Bieniemy's absence.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jonathan Taylor on his contract: I have faith things are moving in the right direction
summary: The Lions and Falcons are each dealing with apparent hold-ins by their respective star running backs.
full_text: The Lions and Falcons are each dealing with apparent hold-ins by their respective star running backs. While Jonathan Taylor is not on his first pro deal, he is in a contract year. But he's not taking the same approach with the Colts. Taylor was on the field practicing with the team on Wednesday and said after the session that he feels like an extension is on its way. “ I have faith ,” Taylor said, via Nathan Brown of the Indianapolis Star . “There have been some good conversations, but I have faith between my agent and the front office. “Like I‘ve said already, I would love to be a Colt for life, and I have faith that things are moving in the right direction.” Taylor signed a three-year, $42 million extension with Indianapolis midway through the 2023 season. He’s No. 1 in franchise history with 69 rushing touchdowns and No. 2 in rushing yards, needing 1,629 to take over the No. 1 spot from Hall of Famer Edgerrin James.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Howie Roseman: No hesitation about extending Jalen Carter
summary: The Eagles made Jalen Carter the highest-paid defensive tackle in the league this week and that deal was a lead topic of conversation at a Wednesday press conference from the team's training camp.
full_text: The Eagles made Jalen Carter the highest-paid defensive tackle in the league this week and that deal was a lead topic of conversation at a Wednesday press conference from the team's training camp. One of the questions posed to General Manager Howie Roseman had to do with a report that the team was hesitant to extend the 2023 first-round pick. Carter pleaded no contest to street racing charges stemming from a crash that occurred before he was drafted and he was benched for part of a game in 2024 after being late for a meeting. Carter's conditioning was questioned by defensive coordinator Vic Fangio ahead of last season and Carter was ejected in Week 1 for spitting on Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott. Roseman said he had not seen that report, but that the team went into the offseason hoping to get a deal done with Carter and said that there were no off-field issues that raised a red flag about committing to him for the long term. "I don't know what off-field concerns," Roseman said, via a transcript from the team. "Since Jalen's been here, he's put his head down, he's worked hard, and he's made huge impact plays for this organization, for this team. Last year, he wasn't 100 percent. He tried to fight through that and play through that. We understand that. Like anyone, when you're 25 years old, you're still growing as a person and as a player. I saw Zack Baun yesterday and he made a great comment. He said to me, 'When I signed my contract, someone told me you don't pay me for what I did, you're paying me for what I'm going to do.' And that's why we do these deals. We don't do anything based on retroactive performance; we're doing things based on future performance. We were trying to sign Jalen in March, understood it was unique because of where the market was and where he thought and [Agent] Drew [Rosenhaus] thought it was going, but it was always positive and we were always trying to get him extended." Carter missed six games last season with shoulder injuries, but none of the issues that have cropped up outweighed what he's shown the Eagles on the field over the last three years. Roseman is banking on that continuing to be the case and the bet is a big one for the Eagles.
author: Josh Alper

title: Familiar faces in new places: Refresher on all the biggest NFL offseason moves in 2026
summary: What free agency lacked in superstar talent, the trade market more than made up for with multiple blockbuster trades
full_text:
NFL teams are in the throes of training camp, which in most cases means all of their major offseason personnel moves are complete. The vast majority of impactful free agent signings and trades occurred at the start of the league year in March, but another wave hit in June when the biggest signings of the summer hit the transaction wire. That was when the Los Angeles Rams acquired Myles Garrett in an all-timer of a deal and the New England Patriots traded for A.J. Brown , reshaping the league's wide receiver landscape.
During the busiest periods of the free agency cycle, it can be a chore to keep up with all the meaningful signings. News flies in by the minute in what is a dizzying time of year. Before preseason games arrive and the regular season gets underway, we are here to help you regain your bearings with a refresher on all the biggest moves.
Or perhaps you are just now tuning back into the NFL after taking the offseason off. Either way, the summary below will provide you with the personnel information you need in order to be properly informed ahead of kickoff.
Here are all the most important signings and trades from the offseason.
Tagovailoa and Murray are locked into two true quarterback competitions with Michael Penix Jr . and J.J. McCarthy , respectively. While both are the presumptive frontrunners to emerge as Week 1 starters, any missteps could lead their teams to hand the keys back to the younger options and attempt to develop them rather than rely on the highly affordable veterans. It also remains to be seen just how long Cousins will hold onto the job in Las Vegas with No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza waiting for his first opportunity. Willis and Smith are the likeliest to hold onto their roles over the course of the season.
There is a strong argument to be made that the Rams pulled off one of the five biggest trades in NFL history with their acquisition of Garrett. Landing the player who just set the league's single-season sack record a year ago and who, by the end of his career, might be considered the greatest to ever suit up at the edge rusher spot was the ultimate statement that Los Angeles is pushing all its chips forward in 2026. The Rams also killed two birds with one stone in acquiring McDuffie and Watson, as their arrivals not only elevate the back end of what should be an impenetrable defense but also hamper a fellow Super Bowl contender. Both of them were every-week starters for the Chiefs .
Nobody allowed more yards on the ground last year than the Bengals . That should change in 2026. Giving up the No. 10 pick for Lawrence was a more than worthwhile investment in the defensive line, and pairing him with Allen takes Cincinnati from the least-feared run-stopping unit to potentially one of the best -- at least with regard to the defensive tackle spot. Losing Trey Hendrickson hurts the pass rush, but the other signings should help neutralize that star departure. In total, a defense that held the Bengals back from maximizing their offensive superstars is suddenly much less of a liability, which could open the door for a breakthrough season.
Priority No. 1 in proving that last season's run to the Super Bowl was more than just a product of good schedule luck was to load up on weapons around MVP runner-up Drake Maye . Trading for Brown, and only having to give up one first-round pick to do so, gives Maye the No. 1 target he needs in the wake of Stefon Diggs ' departure. It was one of the biggest blockbusters of the offseason. Just as impactful might be the Vera-Tucker signing. If he stays healthy (which is certainly an "if"), he will help upgrade the left side of the offensive line that far too often let Maye down in 2025.
Verse and Waddle were parts of two offseason blockbusters. The rest of the most significant trades also show just how valuable the wide receiver and edge rusher positions are in today's NFL. Not only do the stars at these spots command the most money in free agency, but they are now also garnering the largest return packages on the trade market. Waddle, for instance, moved from Miami in exchange for a first-round pick, third-round pick and a fourth-round swap.
Other notable trades: Texans receive RB David Montgomery , Lions receive IOL Juice Scruggs , 49ers receive DT Osa Odighizuwa , Saints receive EDGE Tyree Wilson , Bears receive C Garrett Bradbury , Packers receive LB Zaire Franklin
First-year coach Joe Brady is not the only new face who could help the Bills get over the hump and finally reach the Super Bowl. Josh Allen now has a dangerous go-to target for the first time since 2023. The timing of Moore's arrival could not be better with Allen now firmly in his prime. Defensively, Buffalo surrendered the fewest passing yards of any team in the NFL last season. The newcomers on that side of the ball go more towards keeping the pass defense elite than improving a run-stopping scheme that had serious shortcomings.
Perhaps the most surprising development of the entire offseason was that the Ravens backed out of their agreed-upon trade with the Raiders that would have sent Crosby to Baltimore. They settled on a terrific backup plan in signing Hendrickson, and in fact, it might have been a higher-value deal than the one they nixed. Hendrickson is not nearly as well-rounded as Crosby but is just as dominant in pass rushing, and the Ravens got him at a lower average annual value and did not have to part ways with any first-round picks.
Other notable edge rusher moves: Panthers sign Jaelan Phillips , Commanders sign Odafe Oweh , Colts sign Arden Key
The Jets were the most active team in the early days of free agency with their flurry of defensive signings. Before that, the Sweat and Fitzpatrick trades set the stage for their spending spree. These are not necessarily ceiling-raisers, considering the Jets set the bar remarkably low last year, but at the very least, they should produce some kind of improvement from a campaign that saw New York force exactly zero interceptions and rank fourth-worst against the run. The only way to go is up, and the influx of talent should put the Jets on that path. Aaron Glenn needs that to come to fruition, or else he could be looking for work next year.
The Seahawks elected not to give Walker a second contract even after fueling their Super Bowl run. Once the price tag became clear, it is not hard to see why Seattle was content to let him walk. The Chiefs made him the highest-paid free agent in NFL history with a three-year, $43.3 million deal, and if his asking price to stay in Seattle was in that same realm, it might have been tough to justify spending so much on a ballcarrier who missed time with injuries in each of his first three seasons. That is not to say Kansas City made a poor investment, though. The Chiefs have been in the midst of a rushing drought for years and last season finished bottom-five in numerous categories. Walker joining the offense should take some pressure off Patrick Mahomes as he works his way back from a torn ACL.
Other notable running back moves: Saints sign Travis Etienne Jr., Buccaneers sign Kenneth Gainwell , Cardinals sign Tyler Allgeier , Steelers sign Rico Dowdle , Lions sign Isiah Pacheco , Falcons sign Brian Robinson Jr .
In addition to signing Cousins, the Raiders went after other plug-and-play pieces that should help elevate the roster around their eventual starting quarterback in Mendoza. Most of the reinforcements come on the defensive side of the ball and ought to bolster a group that already features a top-flight edge rusher. But the most direct aid to Mendoza is Linderbaum, whom the Raiders made the top-earning center in league history. His presence on the interior should also clear running lanes for Ashton Jeanty in what Las Vegas undoubtedly hopes is a more productive second year.
If it worked before, it can work again. That seems to be Saleh's thought process as he reunites with Johnson, Thomas and Franklin-Myers, all of whom played…
