title: Bengals training camp Day 2 news and discussion
summary: Competition breeds success. The Cincinnati Bengals are hoping to see plenty of that this training camp after the defense has undergone a significant upgrade to help one of the league’s best offenses not need to play near perfectly every week. That competition will also bring out some serious tension. Afterall, guys are fighting for spots […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OHIO - JANUARY 04: Jalen Davis #35 of the Cincinnati Bengals celebrates a tackle during the second quarter of the game against the Cleveland Browns at Paycor Stadium on January 04, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Dylan Buell/Getty Images) | Getty Images Competition breeds success. The Cincinnati Bengals are hoping to see plenty of that this training camp after the defense has undergone a significant upgrade to help one of the league’s best offenses not need to play near perfectly every week. That competition will also bring out some serious tension. Afterall, guys are fighting for spots on the depth chart or on the roster entirely. There is a lifetime opportunity on the line for some players. While the Joe Burrows and Ja’Marr Chases of the team don’t need to worry about their spot on the roster. The reality is a good chunk of these players will not be around in Week 1, and for some of them they will never touch an NFL practice field for the rest of their life. Maybe Jalen Davis went a little overboard jumping onto Mike Gesicki’s back, but it is that kind of mindset and intensity this defense needs to foster if it wants to turn things around this upcoming season. Bengals News Training Camp Report | Scoping out Bengals’ Intense First Practice: ‘A Lot Of Alphas Out There’ “We didn’t have any false starts today. That’s number one, I think. Getting back into it, usually those come with the twos who haven’t heard the cadence very much, (or) gone against live defenses, and we didn’t have any today, so that’s positive. We’ve got to continue that. There shouldn’t be any, but we also had a couple motion errors, one by me, and a couple others by receivers. So we’ve got to clean that up. But overall, a productive day.” Dexter Lawrence is already showing why he was so coveted as a New York Giant. He has turned into one of the guys so naturally. His presence and how he talks about teammates just shows he is a natural born leader. Five Observations from Day 1 of Bengals Training Camp “Somebody has to challenge the King of the Jungle as they say,” Lawrence said. “Somebody has to keep him on edge in order for him to get better and grow. That competitive spirit won’t stop. And with a guy like that, I know he’s going to bring it. It’s going to be fun.” A fun exchange from Dexter Lawrence and Joe Burrow is hopefully going to be setting the tone for both of these super star players as Lawrence heads into his first season with Cincinnati. Joe Burrow, DJ Turner and Jalen Davis Break Silence on Bengals Practice Fight Everybody clarified once practice ended that the situation was only the result of competition, with no hostility present in the locker room afterwards. Turner compared the scuffle to brothers fighting. Turner would also say that Joe Burrow throwing in his direction was fun, and continued by saying practice should be harder for everyone. Turner had the most level headed response to the fight. It being like brothers fighting. Realistically, Turner and Davis have been practicing with Chase and Gesicki for years now. Tempers are going to flare, but respect is the biggest thing at the end of the day. Bengals’ first-round D-lineman carted off with injury at training camp The status of one of the key figures on the Cincinnati Bengals’ reconfigured defensive line is in question after a training camp injury on Wednesday, July 29. Defensive end Shemar Stewart was carted off from practice after suffering an apparent leg injury. This could be a real blow to depth on the defensive line. Stewart may not have made a Year 2 leap into being some monster pass rusher, but he certainly could have been a valuable rotational lineman at the very least. If he is out an extended period the team may want to look at who is available. After tempers flared on Day 1 what are you hoping to see? More intensity from both sides or a bit of a cool off? Tell us what you’re thinking in the comments!

summary: This offseason, the Cincinnati Bengals front office had one major job: Revamp the defensive side of the ball. Coming to the Queen City from Seattle, Mafe has seen a team […]
full_text: This offseason, the Cincinnati Bengals front office had one major job: Revamp the defensive side of the ball. They seemed to have done just that on paper as they landed players like Dexter Lawrence, Bryan Cook, and Super Bowl-winning defensive end Boye Mafe. Coming to the Queen City from Seattle, Mafe has seen a team transform quickly as the Seahawks won another title last season. Now suiting up for the Bengals, he sees some similarities between his time in the PNW and his time in Cincy so far. He recently joined The Insiders on the NFL Network last week and had this to say about Al Golden’s defense: “When I was in Seattle, when we first had Mike (McDonald) there, there was always a learning curve. Guys are learning a new defense. There’s gonna be a learning curve,” Mafe said. “Coming into spring, I’m seeing that guys are comfortable with the defense. I’m seeing that guys are understanding everything. They’re seeing the vision. They’re seeing how he (Golden) wants to run the defense, and what he wants it to look like. “It’s starting to become his vision of what the defense should look like.” "It's starting to become his vision" 👓 @Bengals Boye Mafe on DC Al Golden pic.twitter.com/bD5COWcHeh — NFL Network (@nflnetwork) July 24, 2026 Bengals fans should love hearing that as the team searches for a defensive pulse this year to keep up with their potent offense. If all of these new additions can click, it could mean another deep run in the playoffs for Zac Taylor’s squad. However, we will have to wait and see if those pieces are actually fitting together before we all start booking our flights and hotels in Los Angeles.

title: Dexter Lawrence says Bengals have “a lot of alphas,” calls the chippiness at practice “perfect”
summary: Dexter Lawrence’s first practice with the Cincinnati Bengals was an emotional one. After a fight broke out between the offense and defense, with Ja’Marr Chase in the middle of it, the big defensive tackle diffused the situation by chalking it up to “just the competitive spirits of everybody.” “There are a lot of alphas out […]
full_text: Jul 29, 2026; Cincinnati, OH, USA; Cincinnati Bengals defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence II (97) walks on the field during training camp at Kettering Health Practice Fields. Mandatory Credit: Katie Stratman-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Dexter Lawrence’s first practice with the Cincinnati Bengals was an emotional one. After a fight broke out between the offense and defense, with Ja’Marr Chase in the middle of it, the big defensive tackle diffused the situation by chalking it up to “just the competitive spirits of everybody.” “There are a lot of alphas out there, and there’s a lot of guys that want it,” Lawrence said. “We have one common goal, and we’re going to do whatever we can to reach it.” While Chase got entangled with Jalen Davis and DJ Turner, Lawrence had his own incident with a Bengals veteran on the offense. Bengals.com reporter Geoff Hobson pointed out that Ted Karras said he yelled at Lawrence, who laughed and said, “Yeah, we were bickering. We were bickering. But that’s the competitive spirit. It’s going to get intense. But honestly, fighting in practice is not going to help us get better. We both are pros and know how to push each other and compete.” Lawrence called Karras “probably the most competitive guy I’ve ever been against, for real, in practice.” And he said the veteran center helps others keep their edge on account of his professional approach. “I love him. He’s probably the most competitive guy I’ve ever been against in practice, for real.” Dexter Lawrence II on facing Ted Karras in practice pic.twitter.com/7Cy9J3IVSz — Mike Petraglia (@Trags) July 29, 2026 Hobson then asked Lawrence if he thinks it got “a little bit more chippy than it should have,” and the former New York Giant said, “No, it’s perfect. Perfect. Perfect.” Sounds like there’s a fine line between being competitive and letting things get out of hand, and Lawrence, a smart veteran, knows what this defense needs to take a big step forward.

title: Bengals training camp Day 1 news and discussion
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals’ training camp opens today (Wednesday, July 29)! It’s the unofficial/official start to the 2026 season. Training camp will launch us into the preseason, and the preseason brings us to Week 1. The Bengals took some big swings this offseason, including trading the No. 10 overall selection in the draft to the Giants […]
full_text: CINCNNATI, OH - AUGUST 01: Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase (1) during the Cincinnati Bengals training camp at Kettering Health Practice Fields on August 1, 2024 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Ian Johnson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Cincinnati Bengals’ training camp opens today (Wednesday, July 29)! It’s the unofficial/official start to the 2026 season. Training camp will launch us into the preseason, and the preseason brings us to Week 1. The Bengals took some big swings this offseason, including trading the No. 10 overall selection in the draft to the Giants for Dexter Lawrence. With the talent level on the offense, a stable offensive line and a defense that looks very different on paper, there is a high level of excitement in the city despite the fact they’ve missed the playoffs for three consecutive seasons. Here are some storylines as the Bengals get back into fighting shape: Paul Dehner Jr. reported back on the Bengals’ annual media luncheon. Yes, optimism rolls in as thick as the July humidity at the start of training camp every year, but undeniably, this year felt different than most and certainly a significant departure from the last three seasons filled with contract squabbles and Burrow rehabs. With the news that the Eagles extended defensive tackle Jalen Carter to a massive extension, Yahoo Sports’ Duncan Day says the Bengals got a sweetheart of a deal with Lawrence. Carter, who is a few years younger, is making an average of $10 million more annually. PFF’s 2026 Cincinnati Bengals season preview is out. Were it not for an injury that sidelined Joe Burrow from Weeks 3-12 last season, the Cincinnati Bengals could have made a serious playoff run despite their struggles on defense. While they are running it back with the same head coach and coordinators, they made significant additions on defense this offseason, and expectations are high for the 2026 season. While Bengals owner Mike Brown didn’t take questions from the media during their annual luncheon on Monday like he usually does, The Cincinnati Enquirer’s Jason Williams notes his presence is still very much felt in the building . The Baltimore Ravens have signed another former Bengal. Offensive lineman Hakeem Adeniji , who started in the Super Bowl for Cincinnati at right guard, has signed with the Ravens. Since playing in front of Burrow, he has signed one-year deals with the Vikings, Browns and Cowboys before returning once again to the AFC North. With camp starting today , there are plenty of storylines to pay attention to. What battles are you keeping a close eye on, and which bubble players or outside shots do you have a soft spot for? title: ESPN ranks Bengals ‘under-25 team’ 20th in the NFL
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals front office has been working to fill roster holes with younger pieces as it moves into the next chapter of the Joe Burrow era. The Bengals have drafted multiple pieces that have seen significant playing time very quickly, which naturally brings some growing pains for the roster. But going into 2026, the […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals front office has been working to fill roster holes with younger pieces as it moves into the next chapter of the Joe Burrow era. The Bengals have drafted multiple pieces that have seen significant playing time very quickly, which naturally brings some growing pains for the roster. But going into 2026, the young section of the roster is taking steps forward, and ESPN now has the Bengals ‘under-25 team’ ranked No. 20. ESPN’s Aaron Schatz wrote, “The Bengals climbed up a bit in these rankings despite graduating most of their secondary. The youth that remains begins with the offensive line, as right tackle Mims and left guard Dylan Fairchild are both 23. So is guard Jalen Rivers, who started seven games last season because of injuries on the line. And fourth-round center Connor Lew will be 21 in August. The other position with a lot of youth is edge rusher: Myles Murphy is 24, Shemar Stewart is 22, and 2026 second-round pick Cashius Howell is 23. Behind those players, you’ll find linebacker Barrett Carter, who started 12 games as a rookie and doesn’t turn 24 until October, and 22-year-old third-round rookie cornerback Tacario Davis.” Schatz has starting right tackle Amarius Mims listed as the Bengals’ ‘blue chip’ piece for their under-25 team, which makes sense considering his stellar play the past two seasons. Again, it is safe to say the young pieces of the Bengals’ roster are improving and will carry a crucial load this upcoming season if Burrow and company hope to snap a 3-year playoff drought.

title: Cowboys news: Recapping Day 1 of training camp
summary: Observations from the first Dallas Cowboys training camp practice in Oxnard – Nick Harris, Fort Worth Star-Telegram The first day of training camp is in the books. Jaydon Blue Takes Advantage Of Phil Mafah Fumble The backup running back role is up for grabs going into training camp, and Wednesday served as the first opportunity […]
full_text: Observations from the first Dallas Cowboys training camp practice in Oxnard – Nick Harris, Fort Worth Star-Telegram The first day of training camp is in the books. Jaydon Blue Takes Advantage Of Phil Mafah Fumble The backup running back role is up for grabs going into training camp, and Wednesday served as the first opportunity for the players behind Javonte Williams on the depth chart to make an impression. After Williams started with the first-team, Mafah was the first one to rotate in. He saw a few handoffs before a Rashan Gary punchout saw him drop the ball only for rookie Caleb Downs to recover. Just like your coach in middle school would do if a player turned the ball over in practice, Mafah was subbed out. Jaydon Blue rotated in and immediately ran for a 45-yard touchdown that probably would have stood if the pads were on. It was a big play to set the tone for what is to come this training camp at the position. Deeper in the room, Israel Abanikanda and Dominic Richardson both popped big runs with the third-team unit. George Pickens Generates Crowd Excitement The crowd on-hand at the River Ridge Playing Fields in Oxnard wasn’t packed by any means in the middle of a weekday, but there were a good amount of youth groups and Cowboys fans on-hand. The ones who did make the trip to see the Cowboys were treated with some excitement in the form of George Pickens during the team period. In one of the first plays of full 11-on-11 work, Dak Prescott found Pickens on the right side for a quick completion. Had it been in full pads, he most likely would’ve immediately been wrapped up by DaRon Bland, but he squeaked out and ran all the way down the field before falling on his back across the end zone. The crowd loved it, and they cheered on Pickens while he ran back into the huddle. After the practice, he spent a good amount of time signing autographs with fans as well. For a player that has had a public eye on his contract situation this offseason, Pickens has been front-and-center with his mentality and approach in Oxnard so far. It took one practice for the Dallas Cowboys to make telling Caleb Downs reveal at training camp – Mauricio Rodriguez, AtoZ Sports Caleb Downs was all over the field on the first day of camp. It took one Dallas Cowboys practice to reveal something surprising about first-round rookie Caleb Downs. The Cowboys held their first open practice of training camp in Oxnard, California, and the early defensive alignment was very revealing. That starts with the first-round rookie’s usage. Cowboys use Downs everywhere in first practice For months, the Cowboys had Caleb Downs penciled in as the starting nickel cornerback. That may still be the case come September. But based on what reporters saw on the field during Day 1 of camp, Dallas appears willing to deploy Downs all over the defense, not just in the slot. According to Joseph Hoyt from the Dallas Morning News, Downs did start the practice session at nickel. However, Hoyt offered a revealing observation that caught my attention: “In the last three plays I have seen, Cowboys rookie Caleb Downs line up near the edge in the box and play deep middle third,” Hoyt wrote on social media . “They wanted a versatile defensive back and they plan to use downs accordingly.” Safety P. J. Locke exits Cowboys’ first training camp practice with non-contact knee injury – Joseph Hoyt, Dallas Morning News It appears to not be serious. OXNARD, Calif. — Cowboys safety P.J. Locke was helped off the field during Wednesday’s training camp practice with a knee injury, a person familiar with the situation told The Dallas Morning News. Locke limped off the field with roughly half an hour left in the team’s first training camp practice. He was back pedaling during a play and appeared to injure his left knee when he planted on it. It was a non-contact injury. Locke walked alongside Jim Maurer, the team’s head trainer, off the field. He didn’t return. Tyler Guyton on competition, 2026 challenges: ‘I want to be a better player’ – Patrik Walker, DallasCowboys.com The former first-round pick is ready to take the next step. OXNARD, Calif. — Tyler Guyton is no stranger to competition. The Austin native has been battling for position ever since he picked up a football as a child, and upwards through his time at TCU and, ultimately, the University of Oklahoma. He’d weather all of those storms to become a first-round pick for the Dallas Cowboys in 2024, and now comes yet another round of competition to test his mettle — from two entirely different directions. “I mean, it’s the same as every day: coming to work and getting better, to try and get one percent better every day,” Guyton said following the first practice of 2026 training camp. Outwardly, he’s working to stave off offensive lineman Nate Thomas, but his biggest opponent is himself and his health. If he wins against the latter, Guyton will likely win against the former. Ability isn’t the question — availability is. Guyton has shown he can make strides when he’s on the field, but he’s suffered injury in both of his first two seasons that has cost him significant time and, as such, a significant opportunity at gaining experience. He’s made changes to both his diet and training regimen to improve durability, also noting that he’s “put on “grown man strength” for this coming season while balancing it with being technically sound against literally the most freakishly athletic pass rushers on the planet. From there, well, here’s how Guyton sees it through his point-of-view: “I [want to get] more technically sound, more confident in the playbook and the scheme and, overall, just a better player,” he said. “It’s a process, of course, and we have to take it day by day, one foot in front of the other. But, at the end of the day, I’m trying to get to a certain point where I feel good about going to the season.” Daily discussion question: What was your biggest takeaway from the first practice of camp?

title: Biggest question for the Cowboys after start of training camp
summary: The long wait is finally over. The Dallas Cowboys have not only reported to Oxnard, California for training camp, but have now officially kicked things off with their first practice Wednesday afternoon. And for all of us starving for some clarity on some unanswered questions about this year’s team, Day 1 of training camp didn’t […]
full_text: The long wait is finally over. The Dallas Cowboys have not only reported to Oxnard, California for training camp, but have now officially kicked things off with their first practice Wednesday afternoon. And for all of us starving for some clarity on some unanswered questions about this year’s team, Day 1 of training camp didn’t disappoint. Among some of the things we learned from Day 1 in training camp is Caleb Downs will play an important, versatile role as a rookie, the RB2 competition is heating up, how the secondary might line up, and Tyler Booker looks primed for a big year. The biggest remaining unanswered question though revolves around Quinnen Williams. The Dallas Cowboys paid a hefty price to acquire Quinnen Williams from the New York Jets a season ago and he’s expected to be the foundational centerpiece Dallas’ defense continues to build around. He was just named to the leadership council in this year, and as we recently learned is at the top of the Cowboys list for a contract extension. Stephen Jones made it very clear in Tuesday’s press conference they are not only open, but want, Quinnen Williams for the long haul. In fact, they’ve apparently already reached out to his agent. Cowboys EVP Stephen Jones said DT Quinnen Williams is at the top of the list of players they want to get signed long term. “Absolutely. We’re very open to that. We want Quinnen here for the long haul.” They’ve already had talks with his agent. — Jon Machota (@jonmachota) July 28, 2026 Even though Williams claims he’s more focused on training camp, his first with the Cowboys, and building the defense than he is in extension talk, there seems to be mutual interest between both parties. Addressing the media after practice Wednesday, he even confirmed he wanted to be with the Cowboys “for the long haul”. Cowboys DT Quinnen Williams said Dallas is “for sure” where he wants to be long term. “I definitely want to be here for the long haul. I want to win.” pic.twitter.com/4UnJE0pj4D — Jon Machota (@jonmachota) July 29, 2026 Of the players next in line to earn a potential long-term extension from the Cowboys, Williams should be at the top of the list. He is not only one of the best interior defensive lineman in the entire league, but someone they can continue to build around for years to come. But, what makes this so interesting is the bombshell Jerry Jones dropped yesterday hinting a “substantive” trade could possibly be in the works in the not-too-distant future. Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said he talked with an owner of another team yesterday about a “substantive” deal. He says he sees value in bargaining future assets to improve this team. pic.twitter.com/9HO0vZTw1C — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) July 28, 2026 If the Cowboys are once again circling back to Maxx Crosby to potentially acquire him via trade like many believe, the Cowboys would have to do some serious salary-cap finagling to extend Williams and absorb Crosby’s contract as well. That’s not even mentioning anyone else they could be considering locking up long-term at the end of the 2026 season. As training camp continues to progress and we continue to learn more and more about the Dallas Cowboys, the Quinnen Williams’ long-term contract situation will remain a big unanswered question. Thankfully, there’s no need to worry about his on the field production or how he’ll fit in Christian Parker’s new 3-4 defense. His contract situation though is interesting.

title: Cowboys 2026 roster rundown: LB Curtis Robinson
summary: Curtis Robinson had a mostly unheralded arrival in Dallas, overshadowed by the aftermath of the 2026 draft, rookie free agent news, and the Cowboys’ trade for his teammate Dee Winters just days earlier. But with much-needed experience at a thin position, Robinson has a great shot at making the roster and playing meaningful snaps this […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - JANUARY 17: Curtis Robinson #59 of the San Francisco 49ers stands on the sidelines during the national anthem prior to an NFL divisional playoff football game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on January 17, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Curtis Robinson had a mostly unheralded arrival in Dallas, overshadowed by the aftermath of the 2026 draft, rookie free agent news, and the Cowboys’ trade for his teammate Dee Winters just days earlier. But with much-needed experience at a thin position, Robinson has a great shot at making the roster and playing meaningful snaps this season. Background Years in NFL: 5 Acquired by: Free agency (2026) After going undrafted in 2021, Robinson signed with the Broncos. He started the season on their practice squad but got called up for three games, playing mostly on special teams but also getting time at linebacker. After being released by Denver in late November, he was quickly added to the 49ers’ practice squad and was activated for three games to close the year, getting all of his snaps on special teams. From 2022-2024, Robinson kept hanging around San Francisco for his special teams work. He only played three games in each of those seasons, sometimes due to an injury or just from the three-game limit of being called up from the practice squad. Robinson might’ve seen more action in 2024 as a member of the 53-man roster, but a late-September ACL injury cut his season short. He returned in 2025 to a more active role. Robinson appeared in 14 games, starting three, and saw regular time on defense while also being a key special teamer. The three starts put him alongside Winters, who the Cowboys traded for on Friday evening of the draft. Two days after the draft ended, it was announced that Robinson had signed with Dallas as a free agent. One more notable thing about Robinson: for the last two years, he was the 49ers’ nominee for the Walter Payton NFL Man of the Year Award. Contract Status Years Left: 1 2026 Cap Hit: $1.08 million If Robinson just makes the roster, let alone plays a significant role in the LB rotation, it will be at a steal with his minimal, non-guaranteed contract. 2026 Projections Role: Backup LB Roster Chance: 60% Unlike some positions in this year’s training camp, inside linebacker isn’t overflowing with candidates. You have three sure things in Winters, DeMarvion Overshown, and rookie Jaishawn Barham. But then there are just four more guys vying for the last roster spots: Robinson, Shemar James, Justin Barron, and UDFA Langston Patterson. Unless there are any veteran free agents added over the next few weeks, there’s not a lot in Robinson’s way. He brings the most overall experience to the party, albeit with limited defensive reps. In fact, James’ 554 snaps at linebacker as a rookie are nearly double the 335 that Robinson’s played in his entire career. But five years of going through camps, practices, meetings, and supporting teammates in other ways, plus plenty of time spent with a new key member of the group in Winters, still gives Robinson value. Given his minimal contract, Robinson may be nothing more than veteran insurance against injury, which is especially important until Overshown proves he can stay on the field. As long as Barham and James show competence as younger players, Robinson may not stick around. Some other roster candidates like OLB Marist Liufau and S Markquese Bell have the potential to be emergency depth at ILB, which could allow Dallas to go short there. Still, after a year where he ascended in role and responsibility in San Francisco, Robinson should not be ignored among this year’s LB contenders. He brings a different sort of value to the locker room, and has already proven to be a reliable special teams player over the last five seasons. full_text: Wide receiver Butch Johnson of the Dallas Cowboys runs upfieldsi against the St. Louis Cardinals. (Photo by Bill Smith/Getty Images) *** Local Caption *** It is Day 46 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like how big the game was for the organization, how memorable the game was, games that had unusual events take place, games that are a part of NFL lore, Cowboys firsts, and games where the Cowboys just plain dominated. Variety is the spice of life and we have all different kind of Cowboys games to review. At the bottom, we’ll link each day of the countdown so you can go back and check out any you missed. Strap yourselves in for Day 46 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff, when we revisit a Thanksgiving game that felt bigger than a normal regular-season matchup. The Cowboys hosted the St. Louis Cardinals in Week 12 of the 1976 season, and this was a true NFC East power game. This was the kind of game that carried playoff pressure before the playoffs even arrived. Thursday, November 25, 1976 — 3:30 p.m. ET Texas Stadium, Irving, Texas Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 19, St. Louis Cardinals 14 The Cardinals had already beaten Dallas earlier that season, winning 21-17 in St. Louis. At this time, the Cardinals and Cowboys were in the same division. That made the Thanksgiving rematch even more important. A St. Louis sweep would have thrown the division race wide open and put real heat on the Cowboys over the final two weeks. Dallas struck first with the kind of opening statement it needed. Roger Staubach finished a first-quarter drive with a two-yard touchdown pass to Scott Laidlaw, and Efren Herrera’s extra point made it 7-0. That score mattered because the Cardinals were built to play from in front under Don Coryell. The Cardinals answered in the second quarter through the ground game. Steve Jones scored from five yards out, Jim Bakken added the extra point, and the game was tied 7-7. That was the only time St. Louis fully broke through until late. The box score shows the Cardinals moved the ball all day with 377 total yards, 249 passing yards and 24 first downs, but the Cowboys kept forcing them to play the long game. Dallas reclaimed control before halftime through Staubach’s legs. He scored on a four-yard run, Herrera added the kick, and the Cowboys went into the break up 14-7. That touchdown was a perfect snapshot of Staubach in this era. He did not have a big passing day, only 83 yards with two interceptions, but he still found a way to affect the game as a runner, finishing as Dallas’ leading rusher with 54 yards and a touchdown on seven carries. The third quarter stayed scoreless, which was a win for Dallas. St. Louis had the more productive offense statistically, but the Cowboys kept getting the stops that mattered. The Cardinals could move the chains, but Dallas kept the end zone protected long enough to make every possession feel heavier. The fourth quarter became a field-position fight. Herrera drilled a 42-yard field goal to stretch the Cowboys’ lead to 17-7, and Dallas later added two more points when special teams produced a blocked punt safety. That made it 19-7, and those five fourth-quarter points ended up being the winning margin after a cardinals touchdown. It was classic 1970s Cowboys football with a solid defense, special teams magic, field position and just enough Staubach. This game belongs on the countdown because it was a classic example of 1970s Cowboys football under Thanksgiving pressure, division stakes, and a result built on defense, special teams, and Staubach doing just enough. It was not the cleanest win of the season, but it was one of the most important. #Cowboys vs #Cardinals 1976 Week 12 Thanksgiving Game Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 19, St. Louis Cardinals 14 #DallasCowboys #NFL (📽️: @nfl ) pic.twitter.com/GHmX5vAv4n — Mike Poland (@kenfigkowboy) July 28, 2026 Interesting Facts About the Game Dallas won despite being outgained. St. Louis had 24 first downs to Dallas’ 16, but the Cardinals committed two turnovers and could not turn enough of their yardage into points. title: Brian Schottenheimer calls Christian Parker “maybe the hardest working coach”
summary: The Dallas Cowboys held their annual pre-training camp opening press conference on Tuesday, with Jerry Jones, Brian Schottenheimer, and Stephen Jones taking to the podium like usual. For the first time in a long time, these heads of state for America’s Team coming to the podium marked something significant before any of the three even […]
full_text: Jul 28, 2026; Oxnard, CA, USA; Dallas Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer at training camp opening press conference at River Ridge Playing Fields. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Dallas Cowboys held their annual pre-training camp opening press conference on Tuesday, with Jerry Jones, Brian Schottenheimer, and Stephen Jones taking to the podium like usual. For the first time in a long time, these heads of state for America’s Team coming to the podium marked something significant before any of the three even said a word – the Cowboys have made it to the true ramp up for 2026 without any significant off the field drama, major contract disputes, or just Cowboys drama for the sake of drama. The Cowboys’ quiet offseason is hopefully just the start of a recipe for success in the regular season and beyond, but it became clear that the team’s secret sauce they believe in is, in fact, the coaching across the board. Jerry seemed to understand that at this point in his ownership tenure the last thing any diehard fan wants to hear him talk about is his ability to select coaches. What fans have wanted to see is not only the right coaches in place, which the Cowboys will have to now prove once real practices begin Wednesday, but Jones and the rest of the front office giving whatever coaches are in place the freedom and space to hone in on the details of actually doing their jobs. The Cowboys are doing that right now at a level that should excite fans considerably, and coach Schottenheimer started to get into this later on during opening remarks. The same rookie head coach that said the reason the Cowboys would be contenders with him at the helm was in part because of how hard he works before the 2025 season, said that his new rookie defensive coordinator Christian Parker is “maybe the hardest working coach I’ve ever been around”. Parker’s experience working with Vic Fangio, the way the Cowboys have supported him from the jump by getting players that fit the scheme, and how much he’s impressed Schottenheimer, and the Cowboys attention to detail around coaching feels even fresher than even their previously-stated lack of drama. Parker’s expertise across the defense is of course in the secondary, where Dallas actually spent free agency money on a safety this offseason. The list of things the Cowboys defense struggled with last season is infinitely long, but right at the top of the list has to be communication as a unit. This was a buzz word used throughout the press conference, not just as something Parker is going to emphasize with a track record of already doing so at both the Broncos and Eagles, but an overall goal for the team. Improvements in this area even just a little bit paired with the type of high-scoring Cowboys offenses that has consistently been in place recently, and the Cowboys should certainly be dreaming of winning a lot of football games in 2026. By the end of the presser, even Jones came around on this idea, stating he expects to be “significantly” improved on defense this year, and using that word twice for emphasis. Even through the pain of the 7-9-1 season a year ago anchored by awful defense, there were moments where the newness of an unknown coach in Schottenheimer scheming up an offense along with Klayton Adams as OC that kept defenses guessing were fun. Getting to go into year two of this offensive coaching with no distractions on that side of the ball, plus a new defensive coordinator already meeting or exceeding all expectations, and a host of new position coaches on defense to be excited about as well, is a level of overall coaching optimism that has everyone excited. It feels ever so slightly tired or redundant already to say that it’s a nice thing the Cowboys are getting to focus on football at the start of training camp, but not enough has been said about how a focus on the on-field play needs to come with quality coaching directly in that same space, but the Cowboys may have found this in a way that will make them a harder opponent for their upcoming schedule than ever before. The Cowboys seemingly have the right coaches that know how to be all-in on doing the number one thing they should be doing – actually coaching and improving their players. The Jones’ do deserve their credit for allowing this culture under Schottenheimer to grow, but now the real fun begins of seeing these coaches get to work building the roster, deploying new players in new spots, finding depth, and building a team that can compete in all phases – with the self-proclaimed hard-working Schottenheimer in charge of the offense, and the hardest working coach he’s ever seen, Christian Parker, all over the defense.

Player Profile Malcolm Roach | Defensive Tackle | Denver Broncos Height: 6′ 3″ Weight: 290 pounds Age: 24 years old Experience: 7th season College: Texas 2025 stats: 41 tackles, 2 TFL, 5 QB hits, 4 sacks Contract 2026 outlook with the Broncos We’ll likely see Roach taking on more snaps this season with the loss of John Franklin-Myers. Roach has shown he’s an impact player, and it is time to see if he can do that with a heavier snap count.

title: Sean Payton believes this year’s Broncos squad can win the Super Bowl
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country. The Super Bowl is the ultimate goal for every team in the National Football League. For some teams it’s a realistic objective. However, there are franchises where it’s simply just a talking point fantasy. Last season, the Denver Broncos fell short of that lofty ambition. This season, redemptions are in their […]
full_text: CENTENNIAL , CO - JULY 29: Head coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos speaks after practice at Broncos Park in Centennial, Colorado on Wednesday, July 29, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country. The Super Bowl is the ultimate goal for every team in the National Football League. For some teams it’s a realistic objective. However, there are franchises where it’s simply just a talking point fantasy. Last season, the Denver Broncos fell short of that lofty ambition. This season, redemptions are in their sights, and the expectations are truly a mile high. A few days ago, shutdown corner Patrick Surtain II emphasized they have the coaching staff and players to hoist the Lombardi Trophy. Yesterday, Head Coach Sean Payton took the podium to field questions from all sorts of topics. When asked about whether or not this year’s Broncos squad can win it all, Payton didn’t hesitate. He had a checklist of four criteria that gives him confidence as they prepare for the upcoming season. “Yeah, this is one of them. I think you have to play good defense to be one of those teams. You have to get good quarterback play. You have to be good on the offensive and defensive lines. You have to be well coached. I think we’re all of the above,” stated Payton. The Broncos were one of the best defensive teams in NFL in 2025. For the second year in a row, they league in sacks. Additionally, they allowed the third fewest points and were widely regarded as the best on third downs. Every starter outside John Fraklin-Myers is set to return this year. That continuity should help them help be one of the top units in 2026. With respect to quarterback play, we saw Bo Nix take great strides in his second season. Had he not gotten injured in Denver’s thrilling victory over the Buffalo Bills in the AFC Divisional Championship game, the outcome of their season could have been much different. This year, Nix has a shot to cement himself as one of the game’s best quarterbacks. The Broncos added several playmakers into the fold via trade and the NFL Draft, which should bolster Nix’s play and the offense’s overall productivity this coming season. When it comes to the offensive and defensive fronts, those are Denver’s foundational building blocks. According to Payton, those groups help set the tone in games and have been a huge reason for their success. Several years ago, that couldn’t be said. Nevertheless, heir diligence and resource allocation in those areas the past few seasons have paid off—especially on the offensive line. “I think that room permeates the building in general, and I think that was an important goal of ours that first year. I think the depth and experience in that room, we have the veteran players that have been together,” remarked Payton. “Then with the influx of each year, some real good young players. I think it’s hard to find in free agency, and I think we’ve done a good job even in the later rounds or in college free agency.” Last but not least, the Broncos have assembled a phenomenal coaching staff. Quality players matter but having the right coaches to develop and set them up for success is equally as important. The Broncos have come a long way in a short period of time. A lot of that is because of Payton and his staff who have changed the team’s culture and infused the franchise with a winning mindset. Belief is a powerful too. Can the Broncos forge that mentality to reach the ultimate goal in ‘26? I can’t wait to find out. As always, thank you for reading. Here is today’s slate of articles for Horse Tracks .

title: Is defensive line the most important position group in Denver?
summary: The Denver Broncos got back to it in training camp this week with the first acclimation practice happening today. Of the stories that emerged from that event, there was one quote that I felt was worth talking about more. We have a survey running on what position group is most vital to the team’s success […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - JANUARY 25: Malcolm Roach #97 of the Denver Broncos celebrates during the AFC Championship Playoff game between the New England Patriots and the Denver Broncos at Empower Field At Mile High on January 25, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Kara Durrette/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos got back to it in training camp this week with the first acclimation practice happening today. Of the stories that emerged from that event, there was one quote that I felt was worth talking about more. We have a survey running on what position group is most vital to the team’s success this year and while I see the offense is winning there, I do wonder if defensive line isn’t actually the most important question the team needs to solve before September. The reason for that is the departure of John Franklin-Myers to the Tennessee Titans in free agency. He was a big part of the Broncos’ interior pass rush last season and will be a guy that won’t be easily replaced along the front. Head Coach Sean Payton was asked about the competition at that former JFM position and he noted that there were two to three players who could compete. “I think there are two or three players,” Payton said. “Certainly we believe in rotation. It’s easier to evaluate once we start putting pads on.” Rotation was strongly held last season too. It was how Vance Joseph kept the defensive front fresh and terrorizing opposing quarterbacks for a league-high 68 sacks. JFM was only on the field for 46% of snaps last season, so you’d have to assume a guy like Eyioma Uwazurike might be in line for a big chunk of that coverage. Though keep an eye out for the younger talent in Sai’vion Jones and Tyler Onyedim. Even with the loss of JFM, Payton still believe this team is a Super Bowl caliber roster and that belief is spearheaded by the defense. “Yeah, this is one of them. I think you have to play good defense to be one of those teams. You have to get good quarterback play. You have to be good on the offensive and defensive lines. You have to be well coached. I think we’re all of the above.” Defensive wins championships. If Denver’s can continue to be the NFL’s strongest pressure group then that would give them an edge in any high pressure situation. summary: We’re officially back! The Denver Broncos returned to the practice field today for their first of two acclimation/ramp up practices before training camp officially kicks off on Friday. This was a lighter non-padded practice allowing the players to work themselves back into action before things get going later in the week. Also, due to fans […]
full_text: CENTENNIAL , CO - JULY 29: Nik Bonitto (15), Dondrea Tillman (92), Jonah Elliss (52) and Johnny Walker Jr. (59) of the Denver Broncos work out during practice at the Broncos Park in Centennial, Colorado on Wednesday, July 29, 2026. Ramping up 📶 pic.twitter.com/t5yDocpTOL — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) July 29, 2026 In today’s camp report, we have Bo Nix returning to the practice field and doing team drills for the first time since his injury. We also have Jonathon Cooper present AND practicing fully, comments and quotes from head coach Sean Payton on the matter, Payton saying wide receiver Jaylen Waddle can walk on water, injury updates, news and notes, quotes, and more! Bo Nix practices fully As expected, Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix was a full participant during today’s acclimation practice. According to reports, Nix looked sharp out there, didn’t show any signs that he was still dealing with his ankle injury, and took part in team drills for the first time since he suffered a broken ankle vs. the Bills in the Divisional Round. Again, this was expected, but seeing Nix out there practicing fully should put any remaining concerns about his health and ankle to rest moving forward. Sean Payton on Bo Nix: "I'm pleased with the shape he's in… The timeline, injury wise, is falling into place." 🙌 pic.twitter.com/IdR6SJXuba — DNVR Broncos (@DNVR_Broncos) July 29, 2026 Payton was asked about Nix and if he can take that “next step” in year three with the Broncos. He snapped back at the question a little bit by saying the next stuff is “cliche” and noted that he’s coming off a 14-game win season and a good season overall. He did add he thinks that he will continue to improve and that there are areas on the team that can improve to help him be better as well. “The next step is kind of cliché. He just finished winning 14 games and having a really good season. Do I think he’s going to continue to improve? Yes. I’m pleased with the shape he’s in. The timeline relative to everything we’ve discussed injury-wise is falling into place. It’s good to have him back out there in the team periods. I think there are certain areas for us offensively that can help with the quarterback, a consistent run game throughout the year. There are some things that we can do to help him, so we’re off and getting started.” The expectations are pretty high for Bo Nix in year three, and if he plays like he did late season for the Broncos, we are going to be in very good shape this season. Nix is healthy, has Jaylen Waddle, and an improving team around him, and the sky is the limit for the Broncos franchise quarterback. Jonathon Cooper is present and practiced fully Probably the biggest storyline for the Broncos heading into training camp was about edge rusher Jonathon Cooper, his ongoing legal case, and his future with the team. It was reported yesterday that Cooper did indeed report to camp with the rest of the Broncos veterans, and today he was a full participant during today’s opening practice . Despite that, Cooper’s future is clouded by a potential court case down the road and has an arraignment hearing scheduled for August 31st. That falls in between the end of the preseason for the Broncos and the start of the regular season, so things remain up in the air for the Broncos team leader and starting edge rusher. Sean Payton gives an update on Jonathon Cooper: Says Cooper’s been “fantastic” working away from the building and they are monitoring the situation closely pic.twitter.com/IeJuFh8uWs — DNVR Broncos (@DNVR_Broncos) July 29, 2026 Payton was asked about the Cooper situation, and he told reporters that they are staying the course with the league, as he said prior, and doing what they have been advised to do. However, he stated that Cooper has been fantastic working away from the building. “We’re staying the course with the league. We’re staying the course with league protocol, club protocol relative to what we’re advised to do. He’s been fantastic working away from the building, and we’ll continue to do that and monitor it. We’re supportive, and yet very much aware of the seriousness of these types of things. Pretty much what I said in the spring, there’s a schedule and a course to this, and that’s what we have to follow.” As we know, Cooper completed a counseling and wellness program last month, which he likely needed to do before returning to the team. Payton commented on that and said that “we’re proud of the work he did last month” and that he is fully supportive of him right now. “We’re proud of the work he did these last, call it month and a half. It wasn’t easy, and it’ll continue to be a challenge. We’ll see where it goes. [I am] fully supportive of him right now as we gather all the information and then we go from there.” These comments by Payton are much more positive than the ones right after his second arrest. His future with the team seemed in doubt, but with him completing the counseling and now returning to the practice field and participating fully, it certainly seems like he will be part of the team’s future. Cooper is still going through the legal process, but when Payton was asked if he read about Cooper’s charges, Payton said he had, but did not want to comment until the process is completed. He added he believes the situation should be finalized “sooner rather than later”. So, it’s possible some sort of settlement could be in the works, but we shall see. Regardless of the outcome, Cooper is still likely looking at some sort of punishment from the league, which could include a suspension. So, we will have to cross that bridge when we get to it. In the short term, it sure seems like Cooper’s standing with the team is in a much better place than we all assumed heading into camp. Sean Payton says WR Jaylen Waddle can ‘Walk on water’ The Broncos’ biggest offseason addition was when they made a blockbuster trade with the Miami Dolphins to acquire explosive wide receiver Jaylen Waddle. Head coach Sean Payton has been very upfront and complimentary of Waddle since trading for him, and that continued today when he said Jaylen Waddle could “walk on water”. Sean Payton has made it clear many times he likes big receivers. So why did he fall in love with Jaylen Waddle? “There are certain prototypes at the position and then there’s that one that if they can walk on water, then — and he’s one of those guys relative to how he runs, how… pic.twitter.com/GMjlSEzHtm — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) July 29, 2026 Payton was asked what stood out about Jaylen Waddle, and he had a bit of a biblical response to the question. He told reporters that there are certain prototypes at every position, but then there are the handful that can “walk on water,” and Waddle is one of those players due to how he runs, stops, and his competitive instincts. “There are certain prototypes at every position, and then there is that one where if they can walk on water… He’s one of those players relative to how he runs, how he stops and his competitive instincts. There is a clear vision for him. I think the knowledge we had with all the other pieces relative to a trade like that was important.” Waddle has been getting rave reviews all spring from coaches, players, and media, and that continued today. According to reports, Waddle looked smooth, quick, and unguardable at times out there, and his speed really stands out. Today was also the first time he was able to practice fully with…

title: Jaylen Waddle 5 questions: Is he the missing piece for Denver’s offense?
summary: Excitement is in the air. After the best season in nearly a decade, a roster that returns pretty much intact, and expectations of a Super Bowl, you see why. What adds to all of this is that Bo Nix finally got his offensive weapon in Jaylen Waddle. The most exciting thing about Broncos training camp […]
full_text: CENTENNIAL , CO - JUNE 4: Jaylen Waddle (17) of the Denver Broncos speaks to members of the media during OTAs at the Broncos Park in Centennial, Colorado on Thursday, June 4, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images Excitement is in the air. After the best season in nearly a decade, a roster that returns pretty much intact, and expectations of a Super Bowl, you see why. What adds to all of this is that Bo Nix finally got his offensive weapon in Jaylen Waddle. The most exciting thing about Broncos training camp starting is Waddle. It’ll also be their first look at what the offense could look like with Waddle in the mix, the type of rapport he and his quarterback have, and Nix back on the field for the first time since he fractured his ankle in the win over the Buffalo Bills. To help Broncos Country get an idea of what to expect from Waddle in Denver, the impact he could have on the offense, and the hole he leaves behind for the Miami Dolphins, we go behind enemy lines with Kevin Nogle from The Phinsider to get the answers. MHR: How much of a loss is Waddle to the Dolphins? How will they look to replace him? Kevin : The Dolphins offense is going to be completely different than what we have seen over the past few years, with the team turning from the finesse, speed-based team that Mike McDaniel wanted into a more power-focused team under new head coach Jeff Haffley. Waddle absolutely could have been a big part of the rebuild for the team, giving quarterback Malik Willis a dynamic threat on the outside, that this is not going to be a quick-fix rebuild for the Dolphins and adding multiple draft picks for Waddle made a lot of sense. Waddle was a huge part of the Dolphins’ offense, but he was always in the shadow of Tyreek Hill. Waddle’s best years were his first two seasons, when he caught 104 passes in his rookie season and tallied 1,356 yards on a league-high 18.1 yards per reception average his second year. Miami’s offense went through Hill, then to Waddle, who always seemed on the verge of breaking out as a true number one receiver, but never fully made that leap. My guess for how the Dolphins replace Waddle (and Hill) is that they will be looking for their true No. 1 receiver in 2027. Malik Washington has a chance to step up after being the third option the last couple of seasons. Free agents Jalen Tolbert, Tutu Atwell, and Terrace Marshall could factor into the passing game. Rookies Caleb Douglas (third round), Chris Bell (third round), and Kevin Coleman, Jr., (fifth round) were all drafted to rebuild the group and could fight their way into the top spot this summer and into the season. Miami’s plan right now has to be to find the best options possible for this year, then evaluate their needs for next year after the season. MHR: What makes Waddle a good receiver? Where are some areas he needs to improve? Kevin : Waddle’s strength is his speed. When he has the ball in his hands, he can run away from just about everyone on the field. His best performances seemed to come when he was targeted on in-breaking routes or slants over the middle, allowing him to get up to full speed, see the entire field, and make the right move to add yards after the catch. He has a good catch radius, allowing him to make catches away from his body and remain at speed. He can also be very precise in his route running, which worked really well in the McDaniel offense, which stressed quarterback Tua Tagovailoa placing the ball in an exact spot with trust that the receiver would be there. As for weaknesses, Waddle is not the most durable receiver in the league. He has missed a game or two each of the last few seasons, and he will end up on the sideline for stretches in games. He relies on his speed to get off the line of scrimmage and create separation, but if a cornerback is able to get his hands on him early, Waddle does not have the size to fight through effective jams. MHR: How will Waddle respond to Sean Payton and his coaching? Could Waddle get even better? Kevin : I think Waddle is Sean Payton’s missing joker. He’s not Reggie Bush or Alvin Kamara, coming out of the backfield, and he is nowhere near Jimmy Graham’s size, but I think Payton sees the potential of moving Waddle around to create mismatches that he wants out of the joker role. Miami used motion and strange alignments under McDaniel, primarily focusing on Hill but with Waddle as well, and I think that experience will allow Waddle to adapt quickly to what Payton wants. There is definitely still potential for Waddle to get better. Everything says he should be a number one receiver, but he just has not gotten there yet. Part of that was obviously Hill, but part of it was Waddle getting in his own way sometimes – whether it was injuries or just not seeming to fully commit. A change of scenery and Payton’s past success should lead to Waddle taking that next step. MHR: What should Broncos fans expect from Waddle in his first season in Denver? Kevin : I think he will be a great compliment to Courtland Sutton, adding more speed to the Broncos’ offense. Waddle playing the two to Sutton as the one, especially early in the season, would make the most sense to a Dolphins fan looking at the Broncos’ depth chart, but I would not be surprised if Waddle has more receptions than Sutton by the end of the season. Waddle is going to have some absolute highlight plays, especially if he is able to get the ball and use his speed to gash opposing defenses. But there will be some times where he simply disappears for chunks of a game. MHR: How much better does Waddle make Bo Nix and the Broncos offense? And is this a good fit? Kevin : I think it is a great fit. The Broncos need that piece to push them over the top, and Waddle could be it. He is going to become a favorite for Nix, who will be able to trust a short throw over the middle could break for a long gain simply because Waddle is the receiver. I think where you will see Waddle’s stats jump is moving away from the Dolphins’ tendency to throw passes at or behind the line of scrimmage – McDaniel loved the screen pass – and letting Waddle get out a little deeper. Payton will find the right way to create the mismatches that get Waddle away from jams and utilize his speed to maximize his effectiveness. I understand the reason Waddle was traded, and I know it makes sense in a long-term vision for Miami, but I do not have to like the idea of him in Broncos orange instead of Dolphins aqua.

Yesterday, the veterans made their way to the team’s new facility to join their rookie counterparts to begin this year’s training camp. Today and Thursday, the team will participate in ramp-up practice sessions. On Friday’s, the first official training camp practice will be open to fans across Broncos Country. In front of reporters at the new state-of-the-art training facility, Broncos Park Powered by CommonSpirit, both offensive guard Quinn Meinerz and shutdown cornerback Patrick Surtain II addressed the media. They lauded the new facility, praised the current ownership group for their efforts, and also offered their opinions on a variety of other topics. One of the first things that caught their attention was the revamped locker room. It’s a big change from what they were accustomed to in the past. However, sometimes change is necessary, and the recent revamp had both star players over the moon. “I couldn’t stop smiling. It was incredible. I feel like it has more of a social atmosphere to it. It’s kind of like a big room with an underlaid couch, TVs, so I’m excited to see the flow of it,” stated Meinerz. “The storage I have in my locker is going to be nice. I’m kind of organizing that right now, seeing how the new flow’s going to be.” This locker room though 👏 pic.twitter.com/ed95rRj6en — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) July 28, 2026 “It’s been a long time coming. The locker room is crazy. It’s quite unique, too. It just gives a different feel, a different vibe. It’s like we’re leaving that in the past and we’re entering a new state, a new year,” added Surtain. With a new season on the horizon, the Broncos are back in business. There is no more waiting—the dearth of the offseason is finally over. Over the coming weeks, they will diligently prepare for the battles to come facing one of the NFL’s hardest schedules in 2026. Meinerz, entering his sixth season with the franchise, is eager to take the upcoming challenges head on. “I’m really excited about this season coming up. I would say this is the most excited I’ve ever been about camp. It’s been really good to reflect on all those things and come up with a better plan moving forward,” stated Meinerz. While the Broncos ended last year’s gridiron campaign short of reaching the ultimate goal, it was still an impressive season. The team broke numerous team records and led the league in sacks for the second year in a row. On top of that, they secured their first division title in a decade, cementing themselves as a true title contender and a force to be reckoned with inside the AFC West and beyond. Boasting continuity in scheme and bringing back high-quality starters at most positions, Denver is poised to compete for a Super Bowl again in 2026. They addressed significant needs this past April in the 2026 NFL Draft and made a big swing trading for Jaylen Waddle to help take their offense to the next level. For those reasons and more, Surtain spoke with the utmost confidence in this year’s group of players. “I think we have all of the right pieces and the right team. The coaches invest a lot into us and pour a lot into us, too. When you put all of that together, it makes for a great team. We have the right guys with the right mentality to start things off the right way. This team is great all across the board,” remarked Surtain. Just how great can the Broncos be? Only time will tell. Though one thing is for certain, every coach and player is eager to prove they have what it takes to be champions. The time to put in the work is now. “Our expectations are pretty high, but we are just going to take it week-by-week. Obviously, that’s the main goal, but it starts right here in training camp and it starts early on in the season. Our main focus is to start out fast and start out hot early. That way we can prepare ourselves to get to that stage.”

title: Blake Miller is on a mission to help fix the Lions offensive line
summary: The Detroit Lions made a huge investment in the offensive line this offseason. They signed Cade Mays to be their new center and drafted Blake Miller in the first round to become their future right tackle. Mays is essentially the unchallenged starter at center, but Miller has veteran Larry Borom to compete with at right […]
full_text: The Detroit Lions made a huge investment in the offensive line this offseason. They signed Cade Mays to be their new center and drafted Blake Miller in the first round to become their future right tackle. Mays is essentially the unchallenged starter at center, but Miller has veteran Larry Borom to compete with at right tackle. However, during the first day of training camp on Wednesday, Miller had already assumed the starting role, playing what appeared to be every first-team rep at right tackle, while Borom was reduced to reserve and jumbo formation roles. That’s a significant shift from the spring, where Miller and Borom split reps daily. And it could be a sign that Miller has already done enough to warrant the majority of the starting reps for training camp. “Definitely feel more comfortable. Things are coming a bit quicker,” Miller told media after the first day of practice. “That’s not to say that there’s still not more things to learn. I want to be able to just go out there, I want to be able to make the point in my head. Things just should be automatic. We’re still working to that point, but the guys that you have in that room, the veterans, and then coaches as well making themselves available, I have no doubt that I’ll be in a good spot.” Detroit’s investment in the offensive line was for a good reason. After a couple years of dominant football, the unit took a significant step back last year. Jared Goff suffered a career-high 38 sacks (eighth most in NFL) and Detroit’s rushing success rate plummeted from 44.9% in 2024 (seventh) to 40.7% (21st). Asking Miller to step in and immediately provide high-level play is a lot for a rookie, but the former Clemson Tiger comes to the NFL with far more experience than most. He started a whopping 54 games over four seasons. And beyond that experience, he’s also bringing an all-in mentality. When asked if he feels like there’s pressure on him to help the offensive line reclaim its standards, he showed a clear devotion to doing whatever it takes. “As any player, it’s a duty to your team, it’s a duty to God, a duty to your family—whoever it might be—you have a duty to be the best player that you can be for your teammates, for your family, for everybody, for the city of Detroit,” Miller said. “I have a duty to be the best player I can be.” It’s far too early to say that Miller’s play on the field indicates he’ll be ready for Week 1. The pads have yet to come on, and Miller is still picking up the playbook. But with upcoming daily bouts against the likes of Aidan Hutchinson, DJ Wonnum, and fellow rookie Derrick Moore, he’s certain to get a taste of the big challenges that await in the NFL.
author: Jeremy Reisman

title: Discussion: Should Lions fans be mad about Jahmyr Gibbs’ sit-in?
summary: Turns out the offseason rumors were right. The Detroit Lions opened training camp on Wednesday morning, and running back Jahmyr Gibbs wasn’t there on the practice field. He has officially reported to camp, as evidenced by a photo from the Lions’ media team, but at this point it’s pretty clear Gibbs doesn’t intend to actually […]
full_text: ALLEN PARK, MICHIGAN - JUNE 17: Jahmyr Gibbs #0 of the Detroit Lions works out at mandatory minicamp at Detroit Lions Meijer Performance Center on June 17, 2026 in Allen Park, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Turns out the offseason rumors were right. The Detroit Lions opened training camp on Wednesday morning, and running back Jahmyr Gibbs wasn’t there on the practice field. He has officially reported to camp, as evidenced by a photo from the Lions’ media team, but at this point it’s pretty clear Gibbs doesn’t intend to actually practice until there is some sort of new contract deal in place. While this isn’t the first time the Lions have found themselves in some contractual drama (remember Alex Anzalone last year?), this is the first time there has been a snag in extending a core player beyond their rookie contract while Brad Holmes has been in town. Typically, those deals have gotten done well ahead of time with literally no drama. Now, the Lions do still have a long runway with Gibbs. After exercising his fifth-year option earlier this offseason, the Lions have their star running back under contract through the 2027 season. But this is the time in which the Lions have typically given new deals to their best players still on rookie contract, so it’s somewhat reasonable for Gibbs to be making this negotiating tactic. So today’s Question of the Day is: Are you mad about Jahmyr Gibbs’ sit in? If so, who’s to blame? My answer: At this point, I don’t think there’s any valid reason to be mad. Gibbs has missed a single practice, and it appears there’s been at least some progress in contract talks , as evidenced by Adam Schefter’s relatively optimistic reporting on the situation. If this thing lingers several weeks into training camp, that’s the time to be annoyed. Don’t get me wrong. It would be nice to have Gibbs out there for the entirety of training camp. I’d love to see him out there getting used to Drew Petzing’s new scheme, preparing his body for a more full workload, and I’d rather him not set this sort of precedent for other players in similar situations. However, I can also recognize that Gibbs doesn’t want to risk any sort of injury before getting paid. An NFL career is so fragile and it can turn your fortune around completely in an instant. We saw how quickly the career outlook of Kerby Joseph changed last season, and there’s already been a handful of NFL players who have suffered season-ending injuries before the first week of training camp has ended. With running backs’ careers being especially short and fragile, I don’t fault for Gibbs trying to cash in when he can. It’s not an ideal situation, and I certainly understand those who are frustrated to see this happen after what has already been a pretty frustrating offseason. But until Gibbs actually misses significant time, I’m not too worried about it.

title: Lions OT Giovanni Manu oddly lands on NFI list after training camp practice
summary: In a very strange turn of events, just hours after taking part in the Detroit Lions’ first training camp practice of the year, reserve offensive tackle Giovanni Manu has been placed on the Non-Football Injury list. Manu didn’t appear to suffer an injury during Wednesday’s practice, and even if he had, it would not be […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - AUGUST 23: Giovanni Manu #59 of the Detroit Lions plays against the Houston Texans during a pre season game at Ford Field on August 23, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images In a very strange turn of events, just hours after taking part in the Detroit Lions’ first training camp practice of the year, reserve offensive tackle Giovanni Manu has been placed on the Non-Football Injury list. Manu didn’t appear to suffer an injury during Wednesday’s practice, and even if he had, it would not be considered a Non-Football Injury. So either Manu suffered an injury prior to practice and tried to fight through it on Wednesday or he suffered an injury after practice in a non-football setting. Either way, it’s highly irregular to see a player placed on the active/NFI list after participating in a training camp practice. It’s a tough development for Manu, who has an uphill battle to land a spot on the 53-man roster after Detroit drafted Blake Miller in the first round and signed free agent veteran Larry Borom as solid, experienced depth this offseason. Manu was repping with the second-team offense at left tackle on Wednesday. While Manu is out, the Lions will likely rely on Borom, Devin Cochran, and Colby Sorsdal to play with the reserves. The good news for Manu is that because he is now on the active/ Non-Football Injury list, he is still eligible to come off the list and return to practice at any time. Hopefully we’ll get some clarity on his situation during Dan Campbell’s morning press conference on Thursday.
