title: Las Vegas Raiders Summer Scouting: OG Rankings
summary: I broke down the 2027 scouting classes in my early summer scouting series, and the room has a ton of potential with a long list of potential standout players. I broke down the offense and defense in articles and I suggest reading those for a broad aspect of the room. The Raiders do have some […]
full_text: I broke down the 2027 scouting classes in my early summer scouting series, and the room has a ton of potential with a long list of potential standout players. I broke down the offense and defense in articles and I suggest reading those for a broad aspect of the room. The Raiders do have some talent on the interior OL, and I’d expect Las Vegas to add more in 2027 as John Spytek does. Las Vegas will likely see one, or both of Spencer Buford & Jordan Meredith depart after the 2026 season, and they’ll still have Jackson Powers-Johnson (2023 2nd), along with third rounders Caleb Rogers and Trey Zuhn. Ideally, Las Vegas can see development from at least 2, if not all, of these younger lineman, and they can all pivot to be core pieces of the Raiders offensive line going forward. These rankings are extremely early, and they will evolve over not only the summer but the next 8-10 months throughout the season, and into draft season. Some lists will feature 10, 15, 20, or more ranked prospects but I’ll include others on the list below to note. Note: A few of the Offensive Tackles, such as Carter Smith (Indiana), Greg Johnson (Minnesota), Anthony Donkoh (Penn State), McKale Boley (Virginia), and others could shift into T. Austin Siereveld, Ohio State – 6’5/325, R-Jr Siereveld has lined up 819 times at LT (all in 2025), and around 500 at both guard spots combined but he’s going to play guard in the NFL most likely. Siereveld allowed a 5% pressure rate in 2025 at tackle, but 0 sacks, largely off his natural raw strength and limited agility working laterally in his kickstep. Sierveld has a ton of initial movement skills, he’s powerful, long, and engages his lower body exceptionally well. As a run blocker, he’s a premium player, with a tough mindset, good power, and he engages his full body into the rep. Siereveld blends his power with good lower body athleticism, and while he’s not going to stick at tackle, he has more than enough athletic ability to move in the run game, he pulls well, and he’s a dangerous player at the 2nd level. Brandon Baker, Texas – 6’4/305, Jr Baker can play tackle, but he’s going to end up at guard this season for Texas. Baker allowed 0 sacks in 2025, with 23 pressures (4.8% rate) mainly at right tackle (950 snaps). Baker has good length, and he could stick at tackle as well. He shows decent athletic ability, but mainly wins with his natural raw power, grip strength, and leverage ability as a former wrestler. Baker keeps his pads low, fires off the line of scrimmage, and he’s able to pull in run concepts while quickly getting to the next level and delivering lethal hits. He’s a nasty offensive lineman, and he can be grabby, especially when facing twitchy quick pass rushers which was the largest struggle at tackle where he was flagged 20 times. Baker can move well, his feet are consistent, but limiting the penalties, adjusting to guard, and showing developed technique in pass protection will be crucial. Samson Okunlola, Miami – 6’6/300, R-So Okunlola plays very similar to Francis Mauioga, and the 6’6/330 guard has a ton of raw power, with good initial movement skills as well. Okunlola comes off the line quickly, he drives his full body through the rep, and Okunlola has immense lower body with good core strength. Oknlola grapples onto defenders well, his hip flexibility shows in short intermediate bursts, and there’s a ton of natural upside in his game as well with only 600 snaps. This is a bit of a projection, but Okunlola has the natural athleticism, power, and flashes of good technique to work as a starting G in the NFL. Alani Noa, USC – 6’3/315, Sr Noa has over 1500 snaps in his career, and he’s allowed 3 sacks & 37 pressures (5.7% pressure rate) across his time at USC. Noa is undersized, but he has good initial movement, fluid hips, and bends really well in the lower half. The USC product does a good job keeping his pads low, he fires off the line of scrimmage and quickly gets up and under defensive tackles with good leverage. Noa’s lower body power stands out, he anchors extremely well, and he has good core strength to engage and latch on. There’s a ton of upside in Noa’s game, and he’s highly experienced as well. Anthonie Knapp, Notre Dame – 6’4/305, Jr Knapp is kicking into guard for Notre Dame this season, and while he’s been a decent tackle, he should do better on the interior. He allowed 5 sacks and 45 pressures across 785 attempts the last two seasons, and his biggest struggle has been the ability to anchor against bull rushers where he’ll consistently get pushed backwards. A former Freshman All-American, Knapp has a ton of length, his lower body has decent athleticism, with his knees and hips working in unison. There’s a ton of upper body power in Knapp’s frame, and while the lower body tends to lag along, he’s not going to be out muscled in his upper body. Knapp is smart, he fires off the ball, and he shows a good ability to identify targets in the run game. Knapp may have a smaller ceiling than others, but he’s consistent, and can be a quality starter at guard, with the potential to stick at tackle. Cayden Green, Missouri – 6’5/325, R-Jr Beau Johnson, Vanderbilt – 6’6/305, Jr Johnson transferred to Vanderbilt from North Dakota State, and the 2x FCS All-American tackle will play LT for the Commodores in 2026. There’s a good chance he could stick there, but the natural athletic ability, paired with lower body strength projects him as a possible higher upside guard. Johnson’s core strength consistently engages, he’s long, and Johnson does a great job with his initial movement. In the run game, Johnson explodes off the line of scrimmage, has quick hips, and he can flip his movement to get to the second level quickly. The former North Dakota State standout is incredibly smart, has a great frame, but I’d like to see more power added into his upper body, while also improving the hand strength which doesn’t show a ton at times. Additionally, Johnson has just 368 career PBLK attempts with most coming in 2025 where he allowed 3 sacks and 17 pressures. Dave Iuli, Oregon – 6’3/332, R-Jr Iuli projects very similar to Noa, he’s lean, big, and powerful. There’s questions on his athleticism, but Iuli has a ton of power, drives defenders backwards, and he plays incredibly nasty. Iuli is a traditional zone blocker, though he may do best in a gap system as well to act into his pure power and limit his inconsistencies when moving laterally. Iuli has 627 career pass block attempts and has yet to allow a sack with just 14 pressures allowed. Malachi Breland, Akransas – 6’5/430, R-So Griffin Empey, North Dakota State – 6’3/315, Jr Empey turned down over half a million to return to North Dakota State, and he should have a chance to continue the Bisons’ NFL pipeline. Empey is undersized, but he’s an incredible athlete, and plays with a lot of natural raw power. Empey drives defenders backwards, he’s able to come off the ball quickly, and the North Dakota State standout also does an incredible job working with his hands showing great punch abilities while also using his core to shut down defenders. Empey is able to seal off the boundary, does well in the run game, and he may make a move to center for his longterm projection, but there’s a lot of traits to bank on. Empey may be nearing his ceiling, and there’s questions on his overall length, but the soon to be 22 year old has allowed just 4 sacks and 22 pressures (1 sack, 5 pressures in 2025) across nearly 800 attempts. Other Names To Watch: Knijeah Harris, Florida – 6’3/315, big physical player. Former Tackle, good movement off the LOS. Powerful Joe Brunner, Indiana – Former Wisconsin T, big frame, great length. Stiff lower body, struggles to move Luke Montgomery, Ohio State – Chance to rise heavily, just 575 snaps, good athlete, ton of hand skills Joe Cotton, Cincinnati – Tackle who will kick into guard, former FCS standout. Average length, powerful Eddy Pierre-Louis, Oklhoma Sonny Makasini, BYU…

title: Rookie versus rookie training camp battles on Las Vegas Raiders’ roster
summary: As the Las Vegas Raiders begin their full squad training camp practices today, while there will be plenty of position battles that pit veterans against first-year pros, including some of the players listed below, there are also set to be a handful of head-to-head competitions that pit two rookies against each other. That could be […]
full_text: Jun 3, 2026; Henderson, NV, USA; Las Vegas Raiders wide receiver Malik Benson (19) runs a drill during organized team activities at Intermountain Health Performance Center. Mandatory Credit: Candice Ward-Imagn Images | Candice Ward-Imagn Images As the Las Vegas Raiders begin their full squad training camp practices today, while there will be plenty of position battles that pit veterans against first-year pros, including some of the players listed below, there are also set to be a handful of head-to-head competitions that pit two rookies against each other. That could be for positioning on the depth chart or a spot on the 53-man roster at the end of camp. Malik Benson vs. UDFA WRs It’s no secret that the Raiders’ wide receiver room is wide open (no pun intended) heading into training camp, especially since Benson was taken in the sixth round and is the only receiver John Spytek drafted this spring. That’s good news for undrafted rookies E.J. Williams, Chase Roberts and Jonathan Brady. Whether it’s for a role in the offense or a roster spot, those four will likely be tied at the hip and competing with each other throughout the summer. Mike Washington Jr. vs. Roman Hemby It feels like Washington is destined to become the No. 2 running back behind Ashton Jeanty in Las Vegas, but the door should at least be slightly open for someone to take the job from the fourth-round pick. That gives Hemby some hope, especially since he was a productive receiver out of the backfield in college with nearly 130 catches and over 1,000 receiving yards over the last four years. Granted, Washington can catch passes too, hauling in 7 3 grabs for 470 yards during the same timeframe. Also, veterans Dylan Laube and Chris Collier will be vying for the RB2 role, too. Keyron Crawford vs. Cian Slone There isn’t a world where Slone makes the team and Crawford doesn’t this year, since the latter was a Top 75 pick in April. However, it isn’t out of the question that both make it and Slone has a bigger role on the defense or is slightly higher on the depth chart. Both players are projects as edge rushers, so if the UDFA proves to be more ready for NFL action, then there’s a chance he ends up getting more playing time than the third-rounder. Brandon Cleveland vs. Gary Smith III Like receiver, defensive tackle is another position group on the Raiders’ roster where just about every spot on the depth chart is up for grabs. Nose tackle is one battle that a lot of people will have eyes on since Spytek didn’t address the position until the seventh round of the draft with Cleveland. Since then, the general manager has inked deals with Smith and Benito Jones to add more competition in addition to defensive linemen like JJ Pegues, who were already on the roster. In other words, there are plenty of contenders to fill the void in the middle of Las Vegas’ defensive line, and these two rookies are among them. Also, with Cleveland’s alignment versatility , there is a chance that he and Smith have significant roles on the team in 2026. But of course, that’s highly unlikely. Jermod McCoy vs. Hezekiah Masses This matchup is saved for last because it’s the headliner on the rookie-versus-rookie training camp battles as the only competition that features two draft picks. While McCoy will be competing with Darien Porter for the second starting cornerback role opposite Eric Stokes, don’t sleep on Masses dropping in from the rafters and factoring into the mix. The Cal product has already taken advantage of McCoy being on a pitch count during OTAs and minicamp, reportedly rotating into the first-team defense with Porter by the end of the spring. The fifth-rounder might be a dark horse, but his excellent ball skills ( five interceptions and 13 PDs in 2025) could be hard to ignore during training camp. With a strong summer, he could move ahead of the Tennessee product on the depth chart, especially if the latter’s surgically repaired knee limits his practice time even more.

title: Miami Dolphins training camp 2026: Position battles to watch
summary: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Dolphins fans and fans across the country. Sign up here to participate in the weekly emailed surveys. The Miami Dolphins have opened their 2026 training camp, with the veterans reporting to the team […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 26: Storm Duck #36 of the Miami Dolphins lines up against the Atlanta Falcons during the second quarter of the game between the Miami Dolphins and Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 26, 2025 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Dolphins fans and fans across the country. Sign up here to participate in the weekly emailed surveys. The Miami Dolphins have opened their 2026 training camp, with the veterans reporting to the team facilities on Tuesday following last week’s reporting deadline for the rookies. Miami has undergone major changes this offseason, starting with a new general manager, Jon-Eric Sullivan, and head coach, Jeff Hafley, continuing through a massive turnover of the roster. Veterans were cut, traded, or allowed to leave in free agency as the team looked to reset its salary cap situation and turn to a rebuild focused on younger players who can grow together. While the focus is on build a winning team that can compete for years to come, it means the 2026 season might be one of growth, development, and overcoming struggles. The Dolphins are the youngest team in the NFL, based on average age, and there are a lot of positions on the roster just begging for someone to step up and take charge of the group. What are the biggest position group battles on the roster this year? We take a look at some of them, and let you decide which battle will be the most important to the team this year. Honorable Mention: Running back The running back position is headlined by De’Von Achane, a 2025 Pro Bowl selection who is only getting better as he plays more. The offense will be built around Achane this summer and he is expected to back up last year’s success with ease. There is no question about who will lead the group. But that does not mean there is not a position battle to watch this summer. While it did not land in our poll below, it is worth mentioning that there will be several players looking to claim the number two position behind Achane. Second year running back Ollie Gordon II would appear to be the easy answer for claiming the second option as he brings power to the ground attack, but he only averaged 2.8 yards per carry last year. He was asked to pick up the short yardage, and he did, but is there more to his game as he heads into year two? Jaylen Wright is coming into his third year and would appear to be more like Achane in terms of skill set. He and Gordon both carried the ball 70 times last year and played almost the same number of snaps. Wright averaged 4.1 yards per attempt in 2025. He could force himself ahead of Gordon as the primary backup to Achane, even if Gordon provides the better short yardage option. Behind them, Carlos Washington, Jr., Donovan Edwards, and undrafted free agent Anthony Hankerson could all factor into the equation. Special teams play could be a major factor in deciding the back end of the depth chart when it comes to the running backs group. Wide receivers Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle are gone. Who steps up to fill the top of the wide receiver depth chart. Malik Washington returns as the top incumbent for the position, with Tahj Washington, Theo Wease, Jr., and AJ Henning also coming back. Miami signed free agents Jalen Tolbert, Tutu Atwell, Terrace Marshall, Jr., and Jalen Reagor this year, along with drafting Caleb Douglas, Chris Bell, and Kevin Coleman, Jr. They also signed undrafted free agent Donavan McCulley. That throws a lot of names at a position group that feels like a giant question mark as training camp begins. Who will step forward and prove he is ready to be the number one, two, or even three target for quarterback Malik Willis? Offensive line The o-line may not be a full “position battle” under the typical definition, and there may not be many open position in the group, but it definitely should be a position to watch this summer and could include competition at key positions. Left tackle, center, and right tackle should be fairly well locked down. Patrick Paul enters his third season at left tackle, Aaron Brewer is coming off an All-Pro season, and Austin Jackson has proven a solid option at right tackle – assuming he can stay healthy. The guard positions will be keys to watch this summer. Rookie Kadyn Proctor was selected in the first round this year and will assume the starting left guard spot while second-year guard Jonah Savaiinaea will move from the left to his natural right position. Will they lock down their respective spots or could someone challenge for a starting spot? And who will claim the number two right tackle spot – and will it become a critical position at some point or will Jackson remain healthy this season? Edge Chop Robinson assumes the top spot at edge rusher, but there are a lot of question marks on the roster after that. Who will start opposite Robinson? Who will prove to be the key rotational player? Josh Uche, David Ojabo, Clelin Ferrell, Robert Beal, Jr., and Seth Coleman were all signed as free agents this year, while Max Llewellyn was drafted in the seventh round and Rodney McGraw and Mason Reiger were signed as undrafted free agents. There are a lot of names to throw at the position as camp begins. Who will jump out and will they do enough to make an impact for Miami this year? Cornerback Miami’s secondary was decimated by injury last year, exposing a desperate need for depth at the position. This year, they are heading into camp with JuJu Brents, Jason Marshall, Jr., and first-round rookie Chris Johnson set to headline the group, with Storm Duck, Ethan Bonner, Alex Austin, Ethan Robinson, Darrell Baker, Jr., A.J. Green III, Marco Wilson, and Miles Battle set to provide depth or fight for a starting role. Johnson is probably locked into one of the top spots, but everyone else could slide around on the final depth chart. Duck, who missed most of 2025 with an injury, could be someone to watch this year as he looks to return to the form that turned him from an undrafted free agent in 2024 to a starter by the end of the season. He is currently listed as physically unable to perform, but he could have a line to a starting role if he can get healthy and return to the same level of play. Safety Similarly to the cornerback position, safety is a position in flux for the Dolphins due to injuries last year – and add in the trade of Minkah Fitzpatrick clearing the top of the depth chart. There should be plenty of battles throughout camp as they work to fill out the depth chart. The team has Dante Trader, Jr., returning and signed free agents Zayne Anderson, Omar Brown, Major Burns, and Lonnie Johnson, Jr. They drafted Michael Taaffee and signed undrafted free agent Louis Moore. Anyone could claim a starting role this summer as camp battles play out. Which camp battle will prove to be the most important for the Dolphins in 2026? Our SB Nation Reacts poll for this week ties into the position battles expected during the summer. Which battle will prove to be the most important for the Dolphins this year? Vote below and head to the comments to let us know why you chose that position group.

title: Start of Training Camp Rundown
summary: The Minnesota Vikings start training camp this week and there are a bunch of news items that have coincided with that this week worth addressing. As a reminder, rookies and quarterbacks reported on Sunday, while veterans reported on Tuesday. Wednesday’s practice included the first press conferences of training camp. Jamal Adams Acquisition The Vikings acquired […]
full_text: The Minnesota Vikings start training camp this week and there are a bunch of news items that have coincided with that this week worth addressing. As a reminder, rookies and quarterbacks reported on Sunday, while veterans reported on Tuesday. Wednesday’s practice included the first press conferences of training camp. Jamal Adams Acquisition The Vikings acquired linebacker/safety Jamal Adams this week. Adams is a former 6th overall pick and Pro Bowler who has since had injury issues and bounced around a couple teams in recent years, including Seattle from 2020-2023 where he got to know Vikings’ GM Nolan Teasley. That relationship seemed to be a factor in his signing with the Vikings from his comments about the signing on Wednesday, but he’s also a good fit for Brian Flores’ scheme as a versatile defender. Jamal Adams on Decision to Sign with Vikings, Respect for Brian Flores, … https://t.co/dQt5XkSVJ1 via @YouTube — Warren Ludford (@wludford) July 30, 2026 He played around 450 snaps last season with the Raiders at linebacker (Adams was a safety previously) and was an above-average performer according to PFF. He’s listed on the Vikings’ website at 6’1”, 213 pounds- which is light for a linebacker. He looks a bit heavier than that though. He signed a league minimum deal last year with the Raiders and I wouldn’t be surprised if he signed a similar deal with the Vikings, although the terms of his contract have not yet been released. But I expect him to make the roster as a linebacker. I could see him replacing Josh Metellus’ reps in that role last season and also reducing some reps for Eric Wilson. After watching Adams’ tape last year at linebacker with the Raiders, my first impression is that he’s a decent linebacker. He may be the best option in coverage among linebackers on the roster. He is also very good at reading plays and always has his eyes in the backfield. He was either a hook zone or flat defender in coverage last season and he showed good awareness in that role. Occasionally he’d run with receivers, whether backs or tight ends or wide receivers and did alright in that role too, but he’s not a good matchup against top wide receivers to be sure. As a run defender, he’s not afraid of contact but sometimes he will be the sacrificial defender to absorb blocks or clog up one hole for others to make the tackle instead of trying to make the tackle himself. He doesn’t show the ability to shed blocks like a traditional linebacker, but he can work his way through the trash, as they say, to make a tackle. As a pass rusher he did okay but could improve by taking more direct routes to the quarterback and improving his ability to get by chip blockers. He’s not a blow-em-up blitzer when it comes to taking on running back blockers like Blake Cashman or Ivan Pace or Eric Wilson have been. He blitzes like a safety. Vikings’ defensive coordinator Brian Flores talked about Adams in his Wednesday press conference saying that Adams is a real football guy and that his role will be determined by what he can do well and be productive at. I’d be surprised if he played anything but linebacker, however, although you could say he’s a bit of a hybrid linebacker/strong safety. But I expect him to make the roster and play around half the defensive snaps, maybe more if there are injuries. His acquisition is good insurance against injury in the linebacker group, which is a significant risk with Blake Cashman having missed a few games every season that last few years and Eric Wilson at age 32. His role could decrease potentially if Jake Golday is able to ramp up over the course of the season. He could also end up playing more snaps than Eric Wilson if they lean on him more in coverage. He graded higher than Blake Cashman and Eric Wilson last season overall according to PFF- particularly in coverage- and could have similar quarterback pressures as Wilson last year if he earns enough playing time. Brian O’Neill Extension No surprise that the Vikings got a deal done extending Brian O’Neill prior to the start of training camp. That seemed like it was in the cards all summer. It was a well-deserved extension for O’Neill, who has been a captain and core player for many years now and one of the better right tackles in the league. It’s a four-year, $96 million deal ($24 million AAV) but further details have not yet become available. The length of the extension goes through O’Neill’s age 35, which makes it likely that O’Neill begins and ends his career in Minnesota. I wouldn’t be surprised if the deal was structured in such a way that the Vikings could pull out a year early without a big dead cap hit, but at this point O’Neill has not shown any signs of reduced performance. It varies by player, but some tackles can continue playing at a high level well into their 30s. But extending O’Neill means the Vikings will have their bookend tackles for four more seasons- Christian Darrisaw is signed through 2029 and O’Neill now through 2030. Gerald Alexander Suspension Vikings defensive backs coach Gerald Alexander was suspended for three weeks without pay for a DUI incident back in April. Terrible timing for a coach to serve a suspension for the first three weeks of training camp. Apparently defensive coordinator Brian Flores stepped in to coach the defensive backs at the beginning of Wednesday’s practice. Not sure what the plan is for the whole three weeks, but not a good time for a coach to miss. Harrison Smith Update Harrison Smith’s name was brought up on a couple occasions during Tuesday’s press conferences and judging by the comments from Kevin O’Connell it doesn’t appear that Smith signing on for another season is imminent nor do those discussions appear to be ramping up. I’d be surprised at this point if Smith came back before the start of the regular season, if he does at all. July 29th Training Camp Notes Kyler Murray took the first reps with the first team in team drills and alternated with J.J. McCarthy every four reps with Murray ultimately getting 16 reps to McCarthy’s 12, although I’ve seen slightly different rep counts. Kevin O’Connell said that reps between the two would not always be perfectly even every day for a variety of reasons, but the initial intension is to split reps roughly evenly between the two quarterbacks. Will have more in our @espn notebook of Vikings camp, but there was a relatively even split of snaps between the QBs on Day 1. Kyler Murray went first and I had him with 16 first-team snaps. Had J.J. McCarthy with 12. Timing of the end of practice likely cost him the final 4. — Kevin Seifert (@SeifertESPN) July 29, 2026 There doesn’t appear to be a clear winner of the day between the two quarterbacks according to reporters attending the practice. Some nice throws and misses by both quarterbacks. StarTribune reported an even split in reps: “Murray and quarterback J.J. McCarthy split first-team reps. Murray took the lead in two 11-on-11 periods and one 7-on-7 period within a roughly 90-minute practice. Both quarterbacks worked with the first- and second-team offenses, ending with an even split of total snaps: 16 each in full-team drills and another six snaps each in a 7-on-7 passing drill. It’s a work in progress. Neither quarterback connected consistently with receiver Justin Jefferson, who watched Murray miss him on a deep ball down the sideline and McCarthy throw a late pass over the middle deflected by safety Jay Ward. Jefferson finally caught a pass in team drills when Murray found him over safety Josh Metellus during Murray’s penultimate 11-on-11 rep. They each had a couple highlight throws: McCarthy had an arcing pass find receiver Jeshaun Jones along the sideline, while Murray threaded the needle to receiver Jordan Addison in a roughly 15 to 20-yard strike over the middle in heavy traffic. Kyler Murray reportedly went 10/17 with two drops and 1 interception while McCarthy went 13/15 with a lot of shorter throws and no real deep balls according to Will…

title: Craig Woodson-Kevin Byard relationship keeps getting forged in Patriots training camp
summary: The New England Patriots’ secondary was one of the best in the NFL in 2025, perhaps surprisingly given who they used as their starting safeties. Craig Woodson and Jaylinn Hawkins — a fourth-round rookie and a career backup — patrolled the team’s defensive backend, and they did a fine job. However, the Patriots still decided […]
full_text: Jul 28, 2026; Foxborough, MA, USA; New England Patriots safety Craig Woodson (4) looks on during training camp at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The New England Patriots’ secondary was one of the best in the NFL in 2025, perhaps surprisingly given who they used as their starting safeties. Craig Woodson and Jaylinn Hawkins — a fourth-round rookie and a career backup — patrolled the team’s defensive backend, and they did a fine job. However, the Patriots still decided to make a change by letting Hawkins leave in free agency and signing first-team All-Pro Kevin Byard to take his place. Four practices into their first training camp together, the pairing has looked solid. Like the rest of the secondary, it also has been feeding off each other to build its chemistry. “Feel really good about the secondary. We just got to continue to build and keep getting better,” said Byard. For the 33-year-old, training camp is business as usual despite being his first in New England. For his young comrade, meanwhile, it is a chance to get an up-close look at one of the best safeties of his era and a player who led the NFL in interceptions in 2025. That is particularly true off the field, where Woodson said he is watching everything from Byard’s film study to his training routine. “I’m just watching his routine. It’s pretty good. He does the contrast, does the sauna, does the massages and everything else. That’s stuff that I’ve been doing as well, so we’re pretty similar when it comes to that,” said Woodson. “In the film room, just hearing him break down things, what he’s seeing scheme-wise, and different coverages, and how he’s able to play stuff. Just hearing all that is just interesting to hear. I’m just trying to take it in as he keeps on spitting the game to me.“ For Byard, the process has been going well and he likes what he has seen from the second-year safety starting alongside him. “He had the first pick of training camp, made a really good diving play on a tipped pass,” he said about Woodson. “He’s mature beyond his years. I think he’s older, he’s 25. He’s a second-year guy, but he’s an older guy, very mature. I’m just looking forward to building with him and obviously having good discussions in meetings and things like that.”

title: Patriots training camp competitions, updated ahead of padded practices
summary: The New England Patriots’ 2026 training camp is underway, and the first four practices of the summer in the books. Even though those were effectively an extension of the offseason before the expected introduction of full pads on Thursday, they were still a first extensive glimpse into the team as it ramps up its preparation […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA- JUNE 11: Kenneth Harris #36 of the New England Patriots and Marcellas Dial Jr. #27 of the New England Patriots battle within a drill during New England Patriots Minicamp on June 11, 2026, at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Summer Lamont/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New England Patriots’ 2026 training camp is underway, and the first four practices of the summer in the books. Even though those were effectively an extension of the offseason before the expected introduction of full pads on Thursday, they were still a first extensive glimpse into the team as it ramps up its preparation for the upcoming season. This also means that some early trends have started to emerge. Players are trending up, players are trending down, and competitions are evolving. With the Patriots returning to practice off their first off-day, and with those aforementioned pads about to be introduced to the mix, we thought that now would be a good time to look at those competitions and find out where they presently stand. Obviously, there is a long way to go before the start of preseason and roster cutdowns, so consider this a first of what will be multiple snapshots this summer. Patriots camp competition update: July 29 Quarterback: Drake Maye is undisputed as the Patriots’ starter, but behind him a competition might be brewing. Seventh-round rookie Behren Morton has received his fair share of practice reps and performed on a decent level. He still finds himself behind Tommy DeVito on the depth chart as the third-string QB, but he actually had some moments when he looked better than the No. 2. DeVito still has the edge and is coming off a strong practice on Tuesday, but Morton is making a case to be included on the 53-man team as a third passer. Running back: Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson are unsurprisingly leading the way, with Lan Larison typically the next man up — one who also saw some reps with Drake Maye and the top offense at points. That said, seventh-round draft pick Jam Miller has had a solid start to his rookie training camp and from our point of view does not appear to be that far off the second-year man. The full-pads practices will help create a clearer picture in the RB3 competition. Wide receiver: Through four practices, A.J. Brown, Romeo Doubs and DeMario Douglas look like the starting receiver trio, with Kayshon Boutte and Mack Hollins rounding out the top five behind them. Among that group, Boutte has looked the best and Douglas like his oft-used spring self. Doubs, meanwhile, has been quiet, while Brown is still finding his connection with Drake Maye. Behind them, sophomores Kyle Williams and Efton Chism are fighting for the WR6 job. The battle is a close one, but based on the quality of reps Chism appears to have a marginal edge at the moment. Tight end: Hunter Henry is the clear top tight end on the roster. Third-rounder Eli Raridon, meanwhile, is the No. 2 despite some drops and maybe playing too quick for himself to anticipate throws on time; he looked smoother and more involved performance Tuesday. The real intrigue, however, starts behind the two. Based on the first four sessions, undrafted rookie Tanner Arkin is the top blocking specialist on the roster and is slowly expanding his role. Offensive tackle: Will Campbell, Morgan Moses and Caleb Lomu are the top three tackles on the roster, with the latter two swapping places in the starting lineup depending on Morgan’s presence and practice usage. The depth spots behind the trio are currently headlined by Marcus Bryant, a mainstay on the second-team line, and by James Hudson, who even saw some starter reps at right tackle on Tuesday. Interior offensive line: Caedan Wallace, Ben Brown and Andrew Rupcich are the names to watch when it comes to the backup jobs along the interior offensive line. The trio has consistently manned those spots in practice and appears to clearly be ahead of any competitors. Obviously, as is the case with the other line positions on both offense and defense, the full-pads portion of training camp will create a clearer picture. Interior defensive line: With Milton Williams and Christian Barmore as the starters, the next spots on the depth chart appear to be Cory Durden’s and Joshua Farmer’s to lose. Durden is the third member of the rotation and very much can be seen as a lock to make the team, while Farmer has repped extensively alongside him with the second-string defense. It remains to be seen how deep the Patriots elect to go, but if they went with five DTs, Leonard Taylor is the player to keep an eye on. Defensive edge: With Harold Landry and Gabe Jacas both sidelined to open camp, the Patriots have been without two of their projected top three edge defenders. This created opportunities for second-year men Bradyn Swinson and especially Elijah Ponder, who has run with the starters opposite Dre’Mont Jones during Landry’s absence. Both he and Swinson are in a good position, while undrafted rookie Xavier Holmes and free agency signing Jesse Luketa have also had a few positive moments. Still, the group as a whole is nowhere near its best. Linebacker: Unsurprisingly, Robert Spillane and Christian Elliss are hoarding the starter-level reps at linebacker. Behind them, K.J. Britt has been first off the bench at one point, with Chad Muma also involved in the mix. The two veterans might end up battling for one roster spot, depending on what the youngsters behind them are doing once the pads come on. Cornerback: The top of the Patriots’ cornerback room looks as expected, with Christian Gonzalez, Carlton Davis and Marcus Jones as the top three. Further down the depth chart, Charles Woods is the current CB4. When he left Tuesday’s practice due to injury, free agency pickup Kindle Vildor took his spot in the lineup. Vildor is part of a group also including Karon Prunty, Kobee Minor and Marcellas Dial Jr. — the latter of whom having gotten a run as a nickel/slot corner — competing for the fifth and sixth spots on the depth chart. Safety: With Kevin Byard and Craig Woodson firmly set as the starting safety duo, the Patriots opted to rotate the third man next to them so far in practice. Mike Brown, Dell Pettus and John Saunders Jr. all got a crack at the role so far. Basically, the only available safety — Brenden Schooler remains on the NFI list — not used in that fashion with the starters is undrafted rookie Peter Manuma. Special teams: Kicker Andy Borregales, punter Bryce Baringer and long snapper Julian Ashby have no competition in camp at their respective positions, so they are all locked into roster spots at the moment. Borregales has looked good, Baringer has not had to do any competitive punting yet, and Ashby was solid outside of one errant snap on Tuesday. The Patriots are scheduled to hold three practices this week, with one session each on Thursday, Friday and Saturday. For more info, please check out our Pats Pulpit Training Camp Guide .

title: Returning for Year 13 an easy choice for Patriots’ Morgan Moses
summary: Despite turning 35 years old in March, retirement was never an option for offensive tackle Morgan Moses. Instead, returning for his 13th NFL season was an easy choice.  “Come on. How can I turn down this opportunity to play football?” Moses said. “My three boys love this game, and they enjoy being out there and […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA - JULY 27: Morgan Moses #76 of the New England Patriots has a laugh after New England Patriots Training Camp on July 27, 2026, at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Fred Kfoury III/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Despite turning 35 years old in March, retirement was never an option for offensive tackle Morgan Moses. Instead, returning for his 13th NFL season was an easy choice. “Come on. How can I turn down this opportunity to play football?” Moses said. “My three boys love this game, and they enjoy being out there and me being out there with them and stuff. And so being able to just continue to wanting to be able to play and coming out here and knowing that there’s room for improvement, that’s what keeps you going.” After signing a three-year deal with the Patriots in free agency last offseason, New England helped keep the veteran fresh with maintenance days during training camp and the regular season. The plan worked, as Moses started all 21 games at right tackle while battling through injuries — allowing just two sacks in the process. To help keep Moses available this season, the team is taking a similar approach with his workload this summer. “We have to know that when he’s giving us a bone and taking care of our bodies,” Moses said. “But we have to have that mindset to know, ‘hey, when it’s time to go, it’s time to go.’ And I think that’s a part of having a veteran team and a veteran presence, but also the willing and the DNA of us just willing to go out there and work every day so we know what we’re getting into, what we want to be. And we have goals to achieve, and so we have to take those one day at a time.” Due to Moses’ age, the Patriots drafted offensive tackle Caleb Lomu in the first round of the NFL Draft this spring. Lomu projects as Moses’ eventual successor and has been repping at right tackle with the top offense on days where Moses’ workload has been managed . That included plenty of reps back in the spring as Moses left a practice early and did not participate in mandatory minicamp. “I’m just getting old, man. I’m 35,” Moses said. “Caleb’s been a big addition to our offensive line and just getting him comfortable and under, letting him understand that we’re going to work together. We’re going to work together, work on the field and in the film room, too.” Through the opening days of training camp, Moses says he is “feeling fantastic.” He has also enjoyed seeing the growth of fellow offensive lineman Will Campbell while reuniting with former teammate Alijah Vera-Tucker up front. It’s all part of what has him excited about the offense entering Year 2 in New England. “Just the evolution. Last year, we came into this thing, nobody kind of knew where we were at, and now we got the target on our back,” Moses said. “Everybody knows we got a MVP candidate quarterback and we got some guys that we can spread the ball out to, and we got the offensive line to do things. So, this is year two of the offense, and I think it’s more important to keep on looking at ourselves and not looking at the noise or hearing the noise outside of us. “I think when you’re one-on-one with yourself and you can look yourself in the mirror and say, ‘Hey, I got better every day.’ I think that’s the surprise in it all.”

title: ‘Unbelievable’ Kayshon Boutte unfazed by rumors about his Patriots future
summary: Between the Romeo Doubs signing and the A.J. Brown trade, no position on the New England Patriots’ roster has made more headlines this offseason than wide receiver. Of course, one other player is also responsible for that: Kayshon Boutte. The fourth-year wideout, who was among the Patriots’ most productive pass catchers in 2025, has been […]
full_text: Foxboro, MA - July 29 - Wide receiver Kayshon Boutte (9) of the New England Patriots makes a catch during Training Camp at Gillette Stadium. (Photo by Matt Stone/MediaNews Group/Boston Herald via Getty Images) | MediaNews Group via Getty Images Between the Romeo Doubs signing and the A.J. Brown trade, no position on the New England Patriots’ roster has made more headlines this offseason than wide receiver. Of course, one other player is also responsible for that: Kayshon Boutte. The fourth-year wideout, who was among the Patriots’ most productive pass catchers in 2025, has been the subject of trade rumors throughout the spring. And yet, with the first four days of training camp in the books, he remains in Foxborough — and not just that: seemingly unfazed by the speculation about his future, no other member of Drake Maye’s supporting cast has had a more notable impact on the practice fields so far. Boutte has made the biggest play of the day in all three of the competitive sessions, including a 40-yard back-shoulder touchdown catch over All-Pro safety Kevin Byard on Tuesday. “That dude is unbelievable,” fellow wideout Kyle Williams said after practice. “I’m super proud of him. Obviously, he’s picking up where he left off, and this is only the beginning for him.” Maye sees Boutte’s impact thus far in camp the same way. “It’s nothing new. I mean, you guys see it. All year last year and the year before, he just keeps doing things right,” the Patriots’ starting quarterback said on Saturday. “I’m proud of him for getting in there, jumping in there. And he understands if he’s got something down the sideline and a ball down the field, he’s got a chance it’s coming his way.” A sixth-round selection in the 2023 NFL Draft, Boutte’s arrow has been pointing up since his sophomore campaign. He quickly developed a chemistry with then-rookie Maye, and continued to enjoy his QB’s trust during their second season together. As a consequence, he finished 2025 with 42 catches in 18 games for 719 yards and seven touchdowns. While not a world-beater in terms of productivity or consistency, he still had an active hand in the Patriots’ offensive fortunes: the team’s starting X-receiver, he provided a deep element none of his teammates were able to duplicate. That was a problem from the team’s perspective, however, and the reason why it went out and brought in Doubs and Brown over the offseason. And with those in the fold, as well as DeMario Douglas, Mack Hollins, Efton Chism and the aforementioned Kyle Williams rounding out the depth chart, Boutte found himself as the potential odd man out. And yet, he continued to impress the coaching staff with his professionalism. “I have a lot of respect for Kayshon,” head coach Mike Vrabel said. “We went through this last offseason: he had a great offseason, he had a good training camp, and that played out during the season. He was a large part of our success. His communication through this offseason with Todd [Downing] and myself, he is a pro. He understands what his job is, and he has gotten off to a good start. I have a lot of respect for him for the way that he has handled all these different situations, the conversations outside of here, and the noise that does not affect his performance on the field.” Had New England gotten an attractive trade offer, the situation might have worked out differently. However, despite being willing to listen particularly around the draft, nothing concrete ever transpired. And so, the 24-year-old stays put. Based on the the first week of training camp, the Patriots offense is all the better for it.
author: Bernd Buchmasser

title: Denzel Ward contract extension raises floor for Christian Gonzalez deal
summary: While the contract negotiations between the New England Patriots and Christian Gonzalez are ongoing, the cornerback market in the NFL was reset. The Cleveland Browns and five-time Pro Bowler Denzel Ward reached an agreement on Tuesday that would reportedly pay him $62.2 million over two years, including $52.3 million in guarantees. While full details of […]
full_text: Jul 25, 2026; Foxborough, MA, USA; New England Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez (0) works out at training camp at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect While the contract negotiations between the New England Patriots and Christian Gonzalez are ongoing, the cornerback market in the NFL was reset. The Cleveland Browns and five-time Pro Bowler Denzel Ward reached an agreement on Tuesday that would reportedly pay him $62.2 million over two years , including $52.3 million in guarantees. While full details of the pact are not yet available, reports indicate that the 29-year-old is now indeed the highest-pair cornerback in football on the basis of annual average value. His $31.1 million AAV barely beats the previous record set by Trent McDuffie’s $31 million per-year deal signed with the Rams earlier this offseason. This is also something the Patriots and Gonzalez will have noticed. New England’s No. 1 cornerback, after all, is trying to become the top-compensated cornerback in the game himself. According to team owner Robert Kraft, the organization is willing to help him in that quest and has an offer on the table that would at least have put him above McDuffie. With Ward now signing a new deal, however, the floor has been raised ever so slightly. Ward’s $31.1 million per year is the new benchmark now, a minuscule increase in the grand scheme of things but one that nonetheless has reshaped the market. Gonzalez, after all, is not the only CB vying a new deal: Seattle and fellow 2023 first-round draft pick Devon Witherspoon are working on what will be a record-breaking pact themselves, and the belief is that the Patriots and Gonzalez are waiting for this one to drop first before committing. If so, and assuming Witherspoon also wants top-of-the-market money when he signs his own deal, we can now expect Gonzalez to make at least $32.3 million annually on a new pact. When that pact will be signed remains to be seen, but the 24-year-old fully participating in training camp can be seen as an encouraging sign. “It’s different, but at the end of the day, it’s business and I’m blessed to be able to do this as my job,” Gonzalez said following Tuesday’s practice at Gillette Stadium . “So, you know, can’t get too much into it. Get to wake up and come out here and play football for a job. So very blessed, just happy that I’m able to come out here, run around and do what I love for my living.”

title: Sean Payton set to present Drew Brees at Hall of Fame enshrinement
summary: Former San Diego Chargers and New Orleans Saints quarterback Drew Brees will officially be inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in Canton, OH, as a member of the class of 2026 on August 8. Sean Payton, former Saint and Brees’ longtime head coach in the Crescent City, was recently announced as the presenter […]
full_text: New Orleans Saints quarterback Drew Brees (9) and New Orleans Saints head coach Sean Payton embrace each other and the Vince Lombardi Trophy as the New Orleans Saints beat the Indianapolis Colts 31-17, Sunday, February 7, 2010 in Super Bowl XLIV at Sun Life Stadium in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Al Diaz/Miami Herald/Tribune News Service via Getty Images) Former San Diego Chargers and New Orleans Saints quarterback Drew Brees will officially be inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in Canton, OH, as a member of the class of 2026 on August 8. Sean Payton, former Saint and Brees’ longtime head coach in the Crescent City, was recently announced as the presenter for No. 9 at the enshrinement ceremony. @SeanPayton to present @drewbrees for Class of 2026 Enshrinement 🏈 https://t.co/VCKkIU7NAf pic.twitter.com/mXkZZhxgca — Pro Football Hall of Fame (@ProFootballHOF) July 30, 2026 Although Brees and Payton had their own backgrounds in the NFL before joining forces in New Orleans in 2006, the QB-HC combo cemented their professional legacies within the Superdome at the heart of the Big Easy, delivering a rebirth to Saints football and aiding in the rebuild of a then-broken city. Following a 3-13 season and a 2005 campaign that saw zero home games played inside of New Orleans following the aftermath of Hurricane Katrina, the city and team required a refresh and found just what Louisiana needed in a first-year head coach and a young gunslinger coming off of a brutal shoulder injury. These guys would grow, progress, and build what would become one of the most prolific offenses in modern league history. The partnership between Brees and Payton quickly sparked a fire for the black and gold while providing a sense of hope for those still suffering from the tragic natural disaster just a year removed. In the pairing’s inaugural season in New Orleans, the Saints finished with an 11-5 overall record and made a run to the NFC Conference Championship game. Although the team would ultimately fall short of reaching the ultimate goal of playing in and winning the city’s first Super Bowl, this season was simply a foreshadowing of greater things to come. New Orleans would go on to miss the postseason in both 2007 and 2008 before a magical year in which pigs learned to fly. Brees and Payton’s offensive prowess, in addition to a multitude of weapons on both sides of the football, allowed the Saints to simply dominate opponents during the 2009 regular season. Averaging nearly 40 points a game, New Orleans would end the year 13-3, not losing until the final three weeks of the year. Victories against the Arizona Cardinals and Minnesota Vikings would lead the Saints to Miami for a chance at a title. The AFC representative? A 14-2 Indianapolis Colts team led by QB Peyton Manning. Everyone remembers the iconic plays; everybody knows about the final result, but what many look over is just how immediate the impact Drew Brees and Sean Payton had on the New Orleans Saints and the Big Easy came to be. In less than five years, the two brought a franchise from the bottom of the barrel to the top of the world following a 31-17 Super Bowl XLIV win. Although Brees and Payton never managed to bring New Orleans back to the big game, their record-shattering, game-changing, everlasting effect on the sport continued for over a decade together. The two had more than 150 regular-season victories, six division titles, three conference championship appearances, and a SB ring for the cherry on top. Drew carried a chip on his shoulder in the way he played the game, leading to his first-ballot gold jacket. He finished his career with over 80,000 passing yards, 571 touchdowns, and an absurd completion rate of 67.7%. Brees was also selected for 13 Pro Bowls, named as an AP first-team All-Pro, a two-time Offensive Player of the Year award winner, and MVP of Super Bowl XLIV. Although times have changed, with Payton now at the helm of the Denver Broncos and Brees retired and enjoying time with his wife and kids, the professional success and legendary status for both started with a losing team in a city that did not have much to offer. Now, after giving everything they possibly could and then some, Payton will give Brees his flowers in what is sure to be a moving, emotional presentation for fans everywhere. I’m sure Drew is already looking forward to being in attendance when Sean has his name called in the near future.

title: Taysom Hill says thank you and goodbye to New Orleans
summary: It’s official, the New Orleans Saints’ Swiss Army Knife is bidding goodbye as Taysom Hill just released a statement on social media saying that after 9 years, his time in the black and gold is over. However, Hill stopped short of saying that he is retiring: “I’ve taken time this offseason to think carefully about […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - DECEMBER 21: Taysom Hill #7 of the New Orleans Saints warms up prior to the game against the New York Jets at Caesars Superdome on December 21, 2025 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Sean Gardner/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s official, the New Orleans Saints’ Swiss Army Knife is bidding goodbye as Taysom Hill just released a statement on social media saying that after 9 years, his time in the black and gold is over. However, Hill stopped short of saying that he is retiring: “I’ve taken time this offseason to think carefully about what comes next for my family and me. I still don’t have a clear answer about what the future holds, but I know that returning to New Orleans is not in the cards.” Thank you New Orleans ⚜️ pic.twitter.com/Q27EJAg4Xk — Taysom Hill (@T_Hill4) July 29, 2026 For the last nine years, New Orleans has been so much more than the city where I played. It’s where my family built a life, where our oldest son was born, and where we formed relationships and made memories that will stay with us forever. I’ve taken time this offseason to think carefully about what comes next for my family and me. I still don’t have a clear answer about what the future holds, but I know that returning to New Orleans is not in the cards. As training camp begins, I didn’t want my silence to be misinterpreted, and as hard as it is to put into words, I wanted to express my gratitude. To the city of New Orleans: thank you. I had always heard, “If you love New Orleans, New Orleans will love you back.” That could not have been more true. You exceeded every expectation I had of what it would be like to live and play in a city. The passion, loyalty, and support you showed my family and me over these nine seasons were truly one of a kind. We will always be grateful for the way you embraced us both on and off the field! Thank you to Mrs. Benson, my teammates, and the entire Saints organization. What I will remember most are the relationships I built with so many people throughout the organization. You helped make me a better player, but more importantly, a better person. I feel incredibly fortunate to have worked alongside so many great people, and I’m grateful for everything we experience together. I’m still working through what comes next, but I couldn’t move forward without taking the time to say thank you. New Orleans, you will always hold a special place in our hearts, and we will always be cheering you on. FOREVER A SAINT Taysom Hill Hill first signed with the Saints in 2017, and his unique versatility at quarterback, wide receiver, running back, and tight end made him a fan favorite. He also cemented his place in the NFL record books last season by becoming the only player in the Super Bowl era to accumulate at least 1,000 career passing, rushing, and receiving yards. Whatever comes next for Taysom Hill, we wish him nothing but the best. While his playing time with the Saints may be over, his legacy will live on, and he will no doubt be inducted into the Saints Hall of Fame.
author: Tina Howell

title: Breaking: Saints DT Bryan Bresee feared to be out for the season with a knee injury
summary: With a day that should have been filled with positives, some awful news has struck the New Orleans Saints. After picking up his 5th-year option this offseason, Bryan Bresee had a massive year ahead of him for contract discussions moving forward, but everything has changed. At practice today, Bresee left with a knee injury, and […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 02: Bryan Bresee #90 of the New Orleans Saints during the NFL 2025 game between New Orleans Saints and Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium on November 02, 2025 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Ronald Martinez/Getty Images) | Getty Images With a day that should have been filled with positives, some awful news has struck the New Orleans Saints. After picking up his 5th-year option this offseason, Bryan Bresee had a massive year ahead of him for contract discussions moving forward, but everything has changed. At practice today, Bresee left with a knee injury, and it seems it’s the worst-case scenario as the injury is believed to be significant, which would end his season before it even began. #Saints DT Bryan Bresee, one of the linchpins their defense and a rising star, is feared to have suffered a torn ACL, per me and @MikeGarafolo . While tests are ongoing, it’s likely the former first-rounder is done for the season. pic.twitter.com/qbuTBb7sZ4 — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) July 29, 2026 The future becomes different because of this news. Bresee was set for a big year with the Saints supporting him (shown by the 5th-year option being picked up) and improvements being made in his own game. The run defense improved last season, and he continued to pressure the QB. This was the year to show he can be the franchise’s star DT, but now that won’t happen. Also, an injury like this threatens to completely stunt the growth Bresee has made. Looking at this from a contract perspective, it puts his future in doubt. Bresee has dealt with injuries his entire career, and the Saints may be more hesitant to give him an extension in 2028. That is still far in the future, but it’s going to be a storyline to pay attention to. Then, we have to talk about this season. Young players like Vernon Broughton and Christen Miller will need to step up right away, and this injury may also open up the path for Zxavian Harris to make the roster. Also, edge rushers like Carl Granderson may be able to fill the vacancy left by Bresee because of how Brandon Staley’s defense is built. Still, this is a major roadblock that the Saints are going to need to figure out fast.

title: Saints star WR sits out of team drills on day one of practice
summary: Although training camp is back and the New Orleans Saints are finally on the field again, the business side of football always tends to creep in. While most were worried about rookie Jordyn Tyson’s availability for drills, which turned out to be full participation, maybe some attention should have been put on Chris Olave’s contract. […]
full_text: METAIRIE, LOUISIANA - JUNE 17: Chris Olave #12 of the New Orleans Saints takes part in drills during mandatory mini camp at Ochsner Sports Performance Center on June 17, 2026 in Metairie, Louisiana. (Photo by Tyler Kaufman/Getty Images) | Getty Images Although training camp is back and the New Orleans Saints are finally on the field again, the business side of football always tends to creep in. While most were worried about rookie Jordyn Tyson’s availability for drills, which turned out to be full participation, maybe some attention should have been put on Chris Olave’s contract. Yesterday, in Saints General manager Mickey Loomis’ press conference with Saints media, he spoke on the contract talks and had nothing negative to say. Olave was good to go for training camp, and his presence was never in question, but on the first day, he did sit out team drills due to the contract situation. #Saints HC Kellen Moore said that WR Chris Olave is not participating in team drills. Just business related but there's no animosity. — Tina Howell (@TinaM_Howell) July 29, 2026 Contract situations like these can often cause issues, but this one may be different. While other players around the NFL are fully sitting out, Olave just chose not to participate in team drills. This is similar to what Alvin Kamara did a few years ago when he was looking for a new contract, and it never caused issues. Instead of holding out, Olave is holding in, so he is still a participant, just not fully. This move puts just enough pressure on the front office to get this deal done quickly, and with what Loomis said about those negotiations, that should come sooner rather than later.

title: Saints 53-man roster prediction: Pre-training camp
summary: The New Orleans Saints begin training camp this week, which means football is back. Of course, it’s not yet game time, but fans and analysts are going to finally get some clarification on roster battles, and for the Saints, there are plenty to pay attention to. As a result, a 53-man roster prediction may look […]
full_text: METAIRIE, LOUISIANA - JUNE 03: Head coach Kellen Moore of the New Orleans Saints speaks to media during the OTA Offseason Workout at Ochsner Sports Performance Center on June 03, 2026 in Metairie, Louisiana. (Photo by Tyler Kaufman/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New Orleans Saints begin training camp this week, which means football is back. Of course, it’s not yet game time, but fans and analysts are going to finally get some clarification on roster battles, and for the Saints, there are plenty to pay attention to. As a result, a 53-man roster prediction may look very different by the deadline, which is August 30th. So, let’s take a look at who’s in and could be out. QB: Tyler Shough and Spencer Rattler Tyler Shough is a guarantee, so we don’t need to spend too much time there, but Spencer Rattler is another story. This offseason, Rattler will be in a competition against former first-round pick Zach Wilson, and although I do think it’s going to be closer than many expect, Rattler will likely win. He has experience with Moore, won the QB competition last season, still has two more years on his contract after this season, and could be a very good trade piece next offseason. If this battle is close, the winner should be Rattler. RB: Travis Etienne, Alvin Kamara, Devin Neal, and Audric Estime With Alvin Kamara back on the roster, the duo of him and Travis Etienne should lead New Orleans’ rushing attack this season. Behind them is where the battle begins, and the three favorites for those spots are Kendre Miller, Devin Neal, and Audric Estime. For me, the decision came down to availability, and although Neal is also dealing with injuries, I think the coaching staff will go with the guy that they drafted. Also, Miller is coming off of a much worse injury. WR: Chris Olave, Jordyn Tyson, Devaughn Vele, Bryce Lance, Ja’lynn Polk, and Barion Brown On the roster, the WR battle is the hardest to predict. So many players will be competing for that last spot, and although I really wanted to pick Brock Reichensteiner as the UDFA surprise that proves himself before the roster cuts, it’s too early to do that. So, Ja’lynn Polk is the obvious choice due to the chemistry he has already built and the potential he still has. TE: Juwan Johnson, Oscar Delp, and Noah Fant At TE, the Saints have a shockingly better room than they have in the past few seasons, and it’s going to be really exciting to see what this group brings to the offense. I would not be shocked if the Saints decide to bring 4 TEs here, but instead, for my prediction, I had only 3, and Moliki Matavao brought back to the practice squad. OL: Kelvin Banks Jr., David Edwards, Erik McCoy, Cesar Ruiz, Taliese Fuaga, Dillon Radunz, Jeremiah Wright, Torricelli Simpkins, and Alan Herron Most of this offensive line group is as expected, including most of the depth options, but Alan Herron is a bit of a longshot pick that I think happens. The young tackle is one of the UDFAs from this offseason, and the Saints gave him a significant amount for a UDFA. There’s a clear interest in his potential, and if the Saints want to take that bet, it could force them to move on from the veteran option of Asim Richards, who really didn’t do too well last season. DE/OLB: Chase Young, Carl Granderson, Cam Jordan, Anfernee Jennings, Tyree Wilson, and Michael Heldman As with the offensive line unit, the DE/OLBs are as expected, except for one spot. I would expect the Saints to bring in six players in the DE/OLB group, but if that happens, Fadil Diggs, Chris Rumph III, and Michael Heldman will all be fighting for the last available spot. Diggs and Rumph III should be the favorites, but I think the Saints go with the potential option here. Rumph III did not show enough last season to gaurentee anything in 2026, and Diggs is still developing. Heldman was extremely productive in college and has potential to be the next Saints UDFA star. DT: Bryan Bresee, Christen Miller, Vernon Broughton, Nathan Shepherd, Zxavian Harris, and John Ridgeway III Here’s the first big surprise of the prediction. I have the Saints moving on from Davon Godchaux. The veteran could be a good nose tackle for the Saints, but I think the lack of flexibility into 4-3 sets (if the Saints do switch throughout games), his age, and the small amount of cap space saved will help with the decision. John Ridgeway III would be the player to push him out, and after the Saints game, Ridgeway III signed a two-year contract in free agency; I think this outcome is likely. A bit of a surprise is that UDFA Zxavian Harris also makes the roster, but I truly believe the Saints will be unable to overlook his potential. LB: Kaden Elliss, Pete Werner, Danny Stutsman, and Isaiah Stalbird Next to the LBs, the Saints could bring 5 into the regular season, but this group of four should be enough. Elliss and Werner create a decent duo, while Stutsman and Stalbird will fight for snaps all season. CB: Kool-Aid McKinstry, Quincy Riley, Martin Emerson, TJ Hall, and Isaac Yiadom The CB group is very unproven, and it’s going to be interesting to see how they do this season, but for me, it’s pretty predictable. Kool-Aid McKinstry, Quincy Riley, and Martin Emerson should be the primary outside corners we see throughout the season; then TJ Hall can develop, and Isaac Yiadom can be the veteran presence in the room. S: Justin Reid, Jonas Sanker, Julian Blackmon, Jordan Howden, and Lorenzo Styles Jr. Last year, the Saints brought five safeties into the season, and I expect that to happen again. Justin Reid and Julian Blackmon would be the starting safeties, Jonas Sanker in the slot spot, Howden as the main backup, and Lorenzo Styles Jr. a top contributor on special teams. ST: Charlie Smyth, Ryan Wright, and Zach Wood Speaking of special teams, here is the group. Even with some competition at kicker, I do believe Charlie Smyth will end up winning the battle. What are your thoughts on my pre-camp edition of the Saints 53-man roster and what changes would you make?

summary: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know about after Day of Giants training camp. 5 QBs Highlight The NFL’s 12 Biggest Comeback Candidates For 2026 | FOX Sports 6. Malik Nabers, WR New York Giants. The Giants hope to have Nabers, who tore his ACL and meniscus in […]
full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know about after Day of Giants training camp. 5 QBs Highlight The NFL’s 12 Biggest Comeback Candidates For 2026 | FOX Sports 6. Malik Nabers, WR New York Giants. The Giants hope to have Nabers, who tore his ACL and meniscus in Week 4, ready for the start of the season. With a promising young quarterback in Jaxson Dart, the former LSU star receiver could put together a season that rivals or exceeds his standout rookie campaign in 2024 (109 catches, 1,204 yards, 7 TDs). Malik and OBJ Malik Nabers and Odell Beckham Jr. on the field together #giants pic.twitter.com/QKd9y5S6Us — Charlotte Carroll (@charlottecrrll) July 29, 2026 New York Giants’ Cam Skattebo ‘good to go’ as training camp opens | USAToday.com “Yeah, he’s good to go,” Schoen told reporters. “I’m sure you guys saw the video. Yeah, he’s been busting his tail. That video shows a little bit of how good his rehab’s been, that he’s able to not land it and still be okay. So yeah, he’ll be out here. He’ll be ready to go today, and he’ll be doing everything.” The video Schoen was referring to was from last week’s Fanatics Fest in New York, where Skattebo did a backflip on stage and nearly wiped out. “He’s a young man, and so he’s in the spotlight and in New York City, and you’ve got to be conscious of your actions, not only from a health standpoint but a perception standpoint,” Schoen said. “But he knows, I’d rather him not do that, especially this close to camp. But also a testament to, you know, how good of a job our training staff and medical staff did in terms of getting him back and ready to go here as we start camp.” There’s a subtle difference with ‘reenergized’ John Harbaugh as he begins new Giants chapter | New York Post Chris Horton has witnessed that for the past 12 years on Harbaugh’s staff, the past six as the Ravens special teams coordinator. It was wholly expected that Harbaugh would pluck Horton out of Baltimore and he did, adding the title of assistant head coach to his Giants job description. Horton, 41, always gets a kick out of watching and hearing Harbaugh at the annual introductory team meeting. This time around, standing in front of the Giants for the first time to open up the spring offseason workout program, Horton noticed a subtle difference. “Did I see a little more juice, more pop?’’ Horton said. “He’s excited. We’re excited. You know, we’re excited to be here. We’re the New York Football Giants. We’re all excited to be here. He was ready to go. He was fired up. It was an awesome team meeting.’’ Why the Giants are in West Virginia and how they turned a resort into a home away from home | The Athletic Largely, because The Greenbrier has proven up to the task many times before. In 2014, then-New Orleans Saints coach Sean Payton worked with the resort to establish a facility equipped for an NFL training camp. In the years since, the Denver Broncos, Houston Texans, Cleveland Browns, San Francisco 49ers, New England Patriots and Arizona Cardinals have used the facility for training camp or other parts of the NFL season. This year, the venue even hosted Iraq’s national soccer team as part of the World Cup. Rosburg spoke with Abir Chaudhry, the Browns’ director of team logistics and operations, to learn how the team got the most out of its time at The Greenbrier, from small details like outfitting player lounges and commute patterns to the big-picture planning of making the excursion as easy as possible. During training camp, the Giants will stay at The Greenbrier Hotel. But the main benefit isn’t the luxury lodging; it’s what’s down the road from the historic hotel. Not only do the Giants have access to two grass fields and a FieldTurf field, but also fully equipped meeting rooms, offices, a training room and an on-site weight room, which is a big change from the Giants’ Albany days, when team meetings were held in college classrooms. They also don’t have to bring lockers or weights to set up a weight room. 1 Reason Every NFL Team Shouldn’t Be Overlooked in 2026 | Bleacher Report New York Giants: Realizing Their Collective Talent. The New York Giants are ready to emerge as a legitimate Super Bowl threat on the heels of a transformative offseason. With John Harbaugh taking over as head coach, the stage is set for this potential-laden squad to put all its high-upside pieces together and make a run. The team has an enviable young offensive nucleus built around Jaxson Dart, Cam Skattebo and Malik Nabers, while the defense added a ton of veteran playmakers in free agency. The expectations for Big Blue may be unreasonably high for a program that hasn’t won more than six games since 2022, but there is every reason to trust Harbaugh can maximize the roster’s potential and get the Giants to live up to these lofty projections. title: Joe Schoen on Cam Skattebo’s backflip: ‘I’d rather him not do that’
summary: WHITE SULPHUR SPRINGS, W.Va. — New York Giants general manager Joe Schoen was having dinner with friends while on vacation when he learned of Cam Skattebo’s viral failed backflip. Needless to say, that interrupted his dinner. Briefly. “Fired off a quick text and confirmed he was alright so we were good,” Schoen said. Skattebo, of […]
full_text: Cam Skattebo | Getty Images WHITE SULPHUR SPRINGS, W.Va. — New York Giants general manager Joe Schoen was having dinner with friends while on vacation when he learned of Cam Skattebo’s viral failed backflip. Needless to say, that interrupted his dinner. Briefly. “Fired off a quick text and confirmed he was alright so we were good,” Schoen said. Skattebo, of course, is coming back from a dislocated ankle and the failed backflip drew plenty of criticism online. Schoen looked for the positive in the video, saying that Skattebo is “good to go,” and that “The video shows a little bit about how good his rehab’s been, that he’s able to not land it and still be okay.” Skattebo took team reps for the first time during mandatory minicamp. He was a full participant in Wednesday’s opening practice of training camp. Schoen admitted that the Giants have spoken to Skattebo about the backflip. “We have, but again, he’s a young man that’s still getting used to the spotlight and in New York City and you got to be conscious of your actions, not only from a health standpoint, but a perception standpoint,” Schoen said. “But he knows I’d rather him not do that, especially this close to camp.” Here are a few other takeaways from Schoen’s annual pre-training camp media availability. Why West Virginia? The Giants could have moved training camp to a number of different facilities closer to East Rutherford, N.J. They chose the Greenbrier, largely because of the many things that were already in place. “A lot of it was different general managers or clubs or teams that even travel in season from West to East will stay here,” Schoen said. “And again, once we did our research and talked to those coaches, and they talked about how easy it was to transition from plugging in your computer and you could watch the film, where they have a weight room, they have a training room, they have the space. The fields are excellent. The accommodations are great. So, for us, we looked locally at some places, and then we also looked down here, and this one just made the most sense for what our needs were.” ‘We’ll see’ about the run defense The Giants were the worst team in the league defending the run last season, giving up 5.3 yards per rushing attempt. Then, they traded star defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence. So, after trading Lawrence and bringing in a plethora of defensive tackles in an effort to build a deep defensive line rotation, will this defensive line be better against the run? “We’ll see,” said Schoen. The GM admitted the Gians will have to do handle defensive tackle “a little bit by committee.” “Signed D.J. Reader and Shelby (Harris) and then I feel like we turned over that inside linebacker position, bringing back the outside backers that we had before,” Schoen said. “So, again, Harbs has said it multiple times about stopping the run, it’s an emphasis. We talk about it all the time. And again, it’s day one here, we’re not in pads yet, but we’re going to continue to work on that and do whatever we can to be better than we have in the past.” John Harbaugh’s impact What difference can Harbaugh make in the Giants’ fortunes? “John’s record speaks for itself. He’s a tremendous leader, very organized, very detailed,” Schoen said. “His record speaks for itself, but we got to go out and still do it. We got to build the team. Every year’s different and today’s day one of building the 2026 New York Giants. “We had a really good offseason, really good spring, he also hired a really good coaching staff. We got a really qualified coaching staff that I’ve been impressed with. So, along with some of the young nucleus and the players that are here, again, we got to go out and do it and see how it all comes together but I like where we are right now, again, coming off the spring and where we are health-wise.”
