title: NY Giants QB Jaxson Dart ‘trying to continue to grow’ in Year 2
summary: The New York Giants 2026 training camp is underway. The Giants took the practice field for the first time Wednesday afternoon, and for their first training camp with Jaxson Dart as their starting quarterback. The media at large doesn’t think much of the Giants this year, with some feeling as though Big Blue is being […]
full_text: Jaxson Dart | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New York Giants 2026 training camp is underway. The Giants took the practice field for the first time Wednesday afternoon, and for their first training camp with Jaxson Dart as their starting quarterback. The media at large doesn’t think much of the Giants this year , with some feeling as though Big Blue is being disrespected. Whether or not those feelings are justified is a debate for another time. For his part, Dart is coming into training camp with a chip on his shoulder. “Because,” he said, “we didn’t have a good year last year. I can’t wait for this upcoming year. This whole offseason I’ve just been waiting to get back with the guys. I really like where we’re at. We’ve got to continue to grow.” Dart certainly also included himself in the collective “we”. He acknowledges that while there were great moments last year, he needs to build off of them. “There’s a lot that I’ve got to still learn,” he said. “There are reps of things that I haven’t really had a ton of experience doing. I’m taking it day by day. I’m trying to keep everything around me simple. From the things that I give my attention to, to my daily and study habits. That’s just me trying to continue to grow because I saw what it was like last year for a tough season. It was new for my career. I want to make sure that doesn’t happen again. So, just continuing to take the next steps and really pour myself into my teammates and my coaches.” “There are a few things mechanically that are different,” he added later, speaking about the parts of the offense that are played under center. “Probably just the biggest thing is a little bit of footwork landmarks in the pocket. But we’ve repped the hell out of it, I’m feeling really good with the track that we’re on and I’m feeling comfortable.” That comfort will likely be aided by the return of wide receiver Malik Nabers , who took part in the individual wide receiver drills . Dart didn’t have much time with Nabers last year, and he’s looking forward to having a more consistent explosive element as well as the return of running back Cam Skattebo . “It makes me really excited, that’s for sure,” Dart said. “In the short time that we had, as me and Skatt were rookies, there was a lot of energy, there were a lot of explosives, and that’s what kind of player he is. He brings a completely different element to an offense. So, I’m really looking forward to the future, getting him back healthy, because I think the sky is the limit for what we can do.” Dart also spoke glowingly of veteran wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. Not only has Dart acknowledged the presence that Beckham brings to the team, but also the veteran leadership and team-first mentality. “I’m definitely excited about O,” he said. “I think the big thing is you never know how somebody’s going to respond from having that time off coming back. I think that his ability to pour into his teammates – and you would think a lot of times when there’s a big comeback that it’s about the individual himself, but he’s really just about the teammates, the guys around him. I’ve loved having him here so far. He’s just a great guy. He’s a great leader. He’s had the ultimate experience of the highs and the lows, and I think that the more that you’re able to communicate with him, get perspectives from him, with him also being, obviously, a really good player, is huge for our team.” Dart mentioned “growth” multiple times speaking with the media. New head coach John Harbaugh will be the man tending to, and guiding, that growth. Dart helped to lure Harbaugh to East Rutherford, and the two have seemingly hit it off. “I love Harbs,” Dart said. “Just his intensity, his love for the game, his leadership. There are a lot of things that stand out as to why he’s been so successful in this league. All of us are just focused on buying in and taking the necessary steps for all of us to grow each and every day. Just super pumped for right now and continuing to move forward with him.” Experience and accolades aside, Harbaugh is a pretty significant departure from Brian Daboll. Where Daboll was an offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach at heart, Harbaugh truly tries to be a “head coach” who oversees the whole team. “Right now, he’s very observant,” Dart said. “He’s very observant from every single facet. From the offense, to the defense, the special teams. He has his hand in every single one of them, of his expectations. Things that he likes. I just think the really cool thing is he’s so open to communication, from the coaching staff to the players. I think that’s just been really cool to have that openness, no ego. Ultimately, he just wants to, obviously, win.” Everyone is hoping Harbaugh gets his desire, with the wins coming early and often.
author: Chris Pflum

title: NY Giants training camp, Day 1 takeaways: ‘We’re getting ready for the games’
summary: WHITE SULPHUR SPRINGS, W.VA. — The New York Giants know they are definitely not in East Rutherford, N.J. anymore. They have noticed the beauty of their surroundings, nestled snugly into the Allegheny Mountains. They have noticed the comfort of their accommodations at the ritzy Greenbrier Performance Center. They know, though, that they are not in […]
full_text: John Harbaugh | Getty Images WHITE SULPHUR SPRINGS, W.VA. — The New York Giants know they are definitely not in East Rutherford, N.J. anymore. They have noticed the beauty of their surroundings, nestled snugly into the Allegheny Mountains. They have noticed the comfort of their accommodations at the ritzy Greenbrier Performance Center. They know, though, that they are not in West Virginia to sightsee. They are not on vacation. They are on a business trip. The business of preparing to be the best football team they can be in 2026. New head coach John Harbaugh made that clear on Wednesday, the first day of training camp. He noted the “beautiful setting” and thanked everyone who made it happen. Harbaugh, though, quickly turned to the business at hand when asked what he was evaluating in the early practices. “We’re chasing execution,” Harbaugh said. “We’re at a stage now, we’re getting ready for the games. I mean, that’s what practice is for. We’re not here to practice. It’s not a training camp exercise. We’re here to prepare for the games that we’re going to play. “What plays we call, how we practice, all those things. We’re not just running plays out here to run plays. That’s why we want to keep our plays to ourselves when we’re doing them out here. So, that’s what we’re evaluating, is our execution.” Here are some of the things we saw from the sidelines on the first day of training camp. Differences for Dart It is clear watching the Giants practice that there are some differences in what is being required of second-year quarterback Jaxson Dart. He acknowledged as much Wednesday by saying “There’s reps of things that I haven’t really had a ton of experience doing.” One of those differences is the amount of work Dart is being asked to do under center. Roughly half of his 11-on-11 work Wednesday came from under center. “There’s a few things mechanically that are different,” Dart said. “Probably just like the biggest thing is a little bit of footwork, landmarks in the pocket, but we’ve repped the hell out of it. I’m feeling really good with the track that we’re on, and I’m feeling comfortable. “It’s not something out there when I’m on the field that I have to think extra about when I’m having a rep at a certain play. It’s more obviously just about readingthe rep from a conceptual standpoint, getting on time with all the guys, so, it’s been something that we’ve really, you know, pushed and really got a ton of reps out of this offseason.” Malik Nabers’ day Nabers did individual drills and ran a few pass routes on air at the beginning of practice. He played a few minutes of catch with Dart when practice ended. Dominic Zvada is human The placekicking competition, where undrafted free agent rookie Dominic Zvada was 13 of 13 in two practices witnessed by reporters and Ben Sauls struggled mightily, was a big story during the spring. Both kickers got opportunities on Wednesday. Sauls made 4 of 5 kicks from 33 to 51 yards, missing a 43-yarder. Sauls also missed a 61-yarder wide right, a ball that had plenty of distance. Zvada was 4 of 6 on the day, missing an extra point and a 43-yarder. Practice highlights Dart threw a beautiful short out to tight end Chris Manhertz, floating it nicely over a trailing Abdul Carter. Cornerback Tae Banks got his hands on two passes. He broke up a throw across the middle from quarterback Brandon Allen that was intended for Xavier Gipson. He also got a hand on an off-target sideline pass intended for rookie wide receiver Malachi Fields. Jameis Winston hit Braxton Berrios for a 40-ish-yard touchdown. Berrios was well behind Nic Jones, the closest defender. Kayvon Thibodeaux, working with the second unit, broke the line and batted down a Winston pass. During a two-minute end-of-game drill, Fields had a leaping 15-yard catch that put the offense into field goal position. The defense missed chances for two interceptions of Dart. Safety Jevon Holland dropped an overthrown ball across the middle. Paulson Adebo had a pass down the middle go right through his hands into the arms of tight end Isaiah Likely for a big play. The defense also missed an interception when linebacker Tremaine Edmunds batted a pass into the air, and Arvell Reese and Ar’Darius Washington collided trying to bring the ball in. Take me home, country roads Here are a handful of quotes from players and coaches about their West Virginia home away from home: Dart: “This is like old school. It’s like what you see in the movies, so I was stoked just to come out here with the team, and it’s a cool experience because in the league, there’s so many external factors … a lot of guys have families and things that they’ve got to take care of off the field, so I think that us just being able to come here for extended days and just being with one another, growing our personal relationships, but also having great communication from the football side, there’s not a ton of things to do around here, so it forces us to be together, and we love each other as a team, so I’m really excited about it.” GM Joe Schoen: “Talked to several general managers and head coaches that have been here, and it’s everything they said it would be. I mean, it’s beautiful. I think it was 60 degrees this morning when we woke up and came over here. So yeah, it’s a beautiful setting and again, they were ready for us and I’m thoroughly impressed with the facilities.” Brian Burns: NOTE: A railroad train was chugging by during most of Burns’ press conference, making it virtually impossible to hear him. Or, be heard by him. “It’s peaceful, a lot of mountains, trees, wildlife. So, you know what I’m saying, it’s a peaceful view, but there’s a lot of chaos on the field … it’s beautiful out here. There’s a couple cribs up there [in the mountains], it’s nice. I notice quite a bit of things, we’re trying to figure out something to do on the off day, maybe we’ll go fishing or something. It’s (not) a lot to do out here.” Injury notes Tight end Thomas Fidone and defensive tackle Sam Roberts, who were initially on the PUP list, passed their physicals on Tuesday. They were both removed from PUP and took part in Wednesday’s workout. Remaining Greenbrier practice schedule The fans are coming! The next three practices will be open to the public. The remaining schedule at the Greenbrier is below. Thursday, July 30 — 1:30-3:15 p.m. (Open to the public) Friday, July 31 — 1:30-3:30 p.m. (Open to the public) Saturday, August 1 — 1:30-3:30 p.m. (Open to the public) Sunday, August 2 — Players’ day off Monday, August 3 — 1:30-3:15 p.m. Tuesday, August 4 — 1:30-3:30 p.m. Wednesday, August 5 — 1:30-4 p.m. (Open to the public) Thursday, August 6 — 1:30-4 p.m. (Open to the public) Friday, August 7 — 1:30-4 p.m. (Open to the public) Saturday, August 8 — 10 a.m. – 12:30 p.m.

title: NY Giants ‘will take it one day at a time’ with recovering Malik Nabers
summary: WHITE SULPHUR SPRINGS, W.VA. — Malik Nabers did not do a lot on Wednesday during the first practice of New York Giants training camp. Nabers took part in some wide receiver agility drills, then ran a few routes. Every bit that that Nabers, coming back from a torn ACL that cost him most of last […]
full_text: Malik Nabers | Getty Images WHITE SULPHUR SPRINGS, W.VA. — Malik Nabers did not do a lot on Wednesday during the first practice of New York Giants training camp. Nabers took part in some wide receiver agility drills, then ran a few routes. Every bit that that Nabers, coming back from a torn ACL that cost him most of last season, did on the field was an encouraging sign for the Giants. Nabers, as has been well-documented, had two surgeries to repair the ACL. The fact that the Giants did not place the 23-year-old on the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list meant that he could get on the practice field at The Greenbrier Sports Performance Center from Day 1. Malik Nabers running drills at Giants training camp today. 🔥 pic.twitter.com/DQPScCfwiA — New York Post Sports (@nypostsports) July 29, 2026 Nabers was not wearing a knee brace during his time on the field Wednesday afternoon. “It was great,” head coach John Harbaugh said of having Nabers on the field. “He looked good.” Quarterback Jaxson Dart worked little with Nabers last season. Dart was the backup quarterback while Nabers worked almost exclusively with then-starter Russell Wilson. Dart said Wednesday that “it’s huge” to have Nabers on the field, even in a limited capacity. “I have a quarter, and one week, really, of reps with him last year,” Dart said. “So any time that we’re able to just have communication, have dialogue between each other, watch tape, which we’ve done a lot, just communication throughout this offseason, which I think has been really good for us. “Trying to get those reps before he’s 100%, and I think that that will help mold our relationship into what we want it to be. He’s obsessed with this game, and he’s attacking it the right way.” Dart and Nabers even spent a few minutes post-practice playing catch before Dart’s media session. Harbaugh said there is no exact plan for Nabers, who caught a franchise record 109 passes for 1,204 yards as a rookie in 2024. “Next will be tomorrow,” Harbaugh said. “We’ll see where he’s at … How it feels. How it responds … We’ll just take it one day at a time.” Harbaugh said there is no definitive date when the Giants think Nabers will be ready for game action. “We’ll take it one day at a time. We’ll meet the circumstances where we find him every single day. Maybe he’ll get way ahead. Maybe he won’t. You can’t really put a timetable on it exactly, I don’t think. “Just see where it goes. Because we want him to be at his best. So when he’s ready to be at his best, he’ll be at his best. If you work hard every day, the body’s amazing. He’s been doing it. That’s really what matters.” The only real play Harbaugh would offer for Nabers is that “I don’t think he’ll be scheduled for a full practice for a little while yet.” Dart said “it makes everybody happy” just to see Nabers on the field. “He definitely has a presence about him. There’s an aura that he has on the field that is exhilarating. It makes me happy,” Dart said. “I mean, it’s Leek. That’s it. It’s Leek. Every time he’s on the field, everybody knows where he’s at.” The best news, of course, is that Nabers is on a football field again. For now, that is enough for the Giants.

title: Fantasy Football 2026: Preliminary WR rankings and tiers
summary: Welcome to the final installment of my preliminary rankings and tiers for each major position for fantasy. Today I’m tackling the deepest position, and the one that’s likely to give your fantasy squads the most total points this season: Wide receiver. You can find all my preseason fantasy content, including my other rankings and tiers, […]
full_text: The dynamic duo | Getty Images Welcome to the final installment of my preliminary rankings and tiers for each major position for fantasy. Today I’m tackling the deepest position, and the one that’s likely to give your fantasy squads the most total points this season: Wide receiver. You can find all my preseason fantasy content, including my other rankings and tiers, here . I’ll update rankings in late August. Hopefully, these initial looks will help you to start thinking about player values and draft strategies. How you approach the receiver position depends on your league settings. In leagues that start three receivers and a flex, there’s still plenty of depth, but the top tiers vanish quickly. Full-point PPR (vs. Half) also can push receivers up boards in drafts. Before we get to the rankings, here are two quick observations on the position. Receiver injuries have been rough the past two seasons. I discussed this in the running backs rankings column, and it’s part of why the top running backs have had the upper hand over the best receivers the past two seasons. These high-end receivers all missed at least five games across 2024-2025: Puka Nacua, CeeDee Lamb, Nico Collins, A.J. Brown, Tyreek Hill, Drake London, Malik Nabers, Chris Olave, Mike Evans, Tee Higgins, Davante Adams, Terry McLaurin, and Christian Watson. Plenty of others in the tiers below them also saw extended absences. Yikes. That’s a lot of angst for fantasy managers. Hopefully that trend reverses this season. Rookie receivers are contributors — but it can take a minute. As college offenses continue to more closely resemble NFL units, we keep getting more and more receivers of all shapes, sizes, and skillsets who can contribute as rookies at the NFL level. I’ve got nine rookie receivers ranked in my Top-80 below, and there are several others on my waiver wire watch list. Trust me when I say that at least one rookie receiver — and probably two or three — will be very fantasy-relevant at some point this season. Landing spot is obviously key, and part of that equation is the opportunity to see the field. Nobody wants roster cloggers, and some of the rookie pass catchers won’t click at all. But if you do draft a rookie receiver, plan to be patient. Justin Jefferson and Amon-Ra St. Brown were both fantastic in their rookie seasons, but not immediately. Jefferson erupted fairly early while St. Brown exploded down the final stretch of the season. Christian Watson is another name that comes to mind – he scored seven TDs in a four-week stretch starting in Week 10 of his rookie campaign. Inhale. Exhale. I’ve organized the WRs into tiers, as I do at every position. You should do the same. To reiterate, everyone wants the best players, and a tiered approach allows fantasy managers to have a great view of (a) ranges of players who can be expected to have similar fantasy production, (b) where the drop-offs are between those ranges, and (c) how many players in a range remain available at any given time. Tiers really help when position runs come, and they facilitate more effective drafting, regardless of format. My receiver rankings and tiers are for Half-Point PPR. Season-long rankings shown are on a fantasy points per game (FPPG) basis and exclude the final week of the season. I’ve ranked 65 players. TIER I – The First Round Picks J. Chase P. Nacua J. Smith-Njigba A. St. Brown St. Brown has been among the most consistent players in fantasy this decade, and deserves to go late in Round 1. It’s not a sexy pick, but you know what’s sexy? Winning fantasy championships. Can JSN repeat his ridiculous success from 2025? I’m dubious, and the others in this tier (and many in Tiers II and III) have done it more than once. Chase is the clear WR1 for me, and especially with Nacua’s adventures this off-season. He just needs Joe Burrow to stay on the field. TIER II – Solid WR1s J. Jefferson A.J. Brown C. Lamb D. London G. Pickens N. Collins C. Olave R. Rice Was 2025 just a blip for Jefferson, or should we be worried? After what is arguably the greatest start to a career of any receiver, including four straight Top-5 WR finishes from 2021-2024, Jefferson was unplayable for much of last season, and finished as the WR37, at just 9.1 FPPG. I’ll bank on Kyler Murray being good enough, and motivated enough, to get J.J. close to his historical numbers, if not back up to elite status. The rest of the receivers in this group are all pretty safe picks, barring injury. I have A.J. Brown higher than most. Pairing one of the game’s best downfield threats with a QB who led the NFL in yards per competition and downfield accuracy last season feels like a no-brainer. Two Cowboys in the Top-10? Unusual, but not unheard of. TIER III – Borderline WR1s/2s T. Higgins D. Smith J. Waddle L. McConkey G. Wilson Z. Flowers T. McLaurin T. McMillan M. Nabers D. Adams C. Watson E. Egbuka M. Evans I like a lot of the receivers in this tier, and plan to pepper them in Rounds 3-5 and with decent dollars in auctions. I’m higher than most on Watson, and think the departures of Doubs and Wicks should open the door for him finally putting together a complete season as an alpha. McLaurin and McConkey also have my attention this season, as both are set up for a lot of volume, and are paired with a QB who can get them the ball. Has Nabers fallen too far? He’s a Round 2 pick when fully healthy. TIER IV – Back-end WR 2s L. Burden III J. Williams R. Odunze B. Thomas, Jr. D.J. Moore C. Sutton C. Tate (R) M. Harrison, Jr. C. Godwin, Jr. A. Pierce D.K. Metcalf M. Wilson J. Addison This tier features a lot of players with good upside, but uncertain floors. Questions abound, but there are players here who are going to help people win leagues. Thomas fell off a cliff after his brilliant rookie season. Which player are we getting in 2026? Has the Burden hype gone too far, and are we sleeping on Odunze? How good can Tate be as a rookie, in Cam Ward’s second season? If Harrison and Wilson are both healthy, who will be better? Can Metcalf return to alpha dog status, or is Aaron Rodgers just too old to wait for him to get open downfield? What happens when Moore is paired with Josh Allen? Pierce has led the NFL in yards per catch for two straight seasons. Can he do it again? TIER V – WR3/Flex Plays M. Pittman, Jr. J. Tyson (R) P. Washington Q. Johnston J. Reed R. Pearsall J. Downs W. Robinson K. Shakir X. Worthy M. Lemon (R) This tier is mostly a mix of slot merchants, who can definitely help you win weeks and especially in Full-point PPR, and younger players who haven’t quite proven it yet. While I don’t think anyone in this tier will finish as a Top-10 player at the position, history says that one of them will. I’m high on Reed this season, who like Watson should benefit from Green Bay finally not having a deep rotation at the position. TIER VI – More WR3s/4s J. Coker R. Doubs J. Meyers J. Nailor A. Mitchell M. Golden R. Shaheed J. McMillan J. Jennings K.C. Concepcion (R) M. Washington J. Jeudy T. Tucker D. Boston (R) R. Flournoy T. Harris Receiver is deep. It always is. And every year, there are players who come from this tier and lower who surprise. It can be rookies, or older vets, or anything in between. You can get most of these guys fairly late in drafts. Most won’t pan out into anything that helps you more than Bye week and injury fillers, but some will be weekly starters, at least for stretches. My favorites in this tier (at cost) are Nailor, McMillan, and Shaheed, who will hopefully be more fully incorporated into Seattle’s offense in his first full season with the team. TIER VII – WR Depth C. Ridley K. Boutte D. Wicks J. Noel R. Bateman I. TeSlaa S. Diggs T. Hunter D. Mooney D. Stribling (R) O. Cooper, Jr. (R) T. Franklin T. Dell A. Williams (R) Z. Branch (R) I could’ve easily listed 10-15 more guys who are just as likely as the guys in this tier to be fantasy contributors at some point this season. Keep an eye on Diggs, who will hopefully sign…

title: Vita Vea as a New York Giant sounds nice, but probably isn’t happening
summary: Vita Vea’s request to be traded by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers has New York Giants fans dreaming of putting the two-time Pro Bowl nose tackle in the middle of the defensive line alongside D.J. Reader. It is a nice dream. Tony DelGenio and I discussed the idea at length in our training camp preview podcast. […]
full_text: Vita Vea | Getty Images Vita Vea’s request to be traded by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers has New York Giants fans dreaming of putting the two-time Pro Bowl nose tackle in the middle of the defensive line alongside D.J. Reader . It is a nice dream. Tony DelGenio and I discussed the idea at length in our training camp preview podcast . Giants’ GM Joe Schoen should absolutely call Bucs’ GM Jason Licht to inquire about whether Vea is actully available and what the price tag might be. BBV’s Chris Pflum took the same stance a few days ago. After being forced to trade Dexter Lawrence to the Cincinnati Bengals, the Giants were fortunate to sign Reader, a quality run-defending nose tackle. The 32-year-old Reader isn’t Lawrence, though. He’s not Vea, either. Vea, 31, is a 6-foot-4, 347-pound monster in the middle who can both defend the run and get to the quarterback, something Lawrence could do but Reader cannot. Vea has 35 sacks in eight seasons, and has not had fewer than 4.0 in a season since 2021. Acquiring Vea sounds tantalizing. It would make the Giants better in 2026, no doubt. Is it smart, though, or even feasible? Probably not. The Giants have only five selections in the 2027 NFL Draft, one which is currently thought to be historically deep in available talent. Those selections are in the first, second, third, fith and sixth rounds. The Giants traded their fourth-round pick to the Cleveland Browns to select Malachi Fields in the 2026 NFL Draft, and sent their seventh-round pick to the Miami Dolphinsin the Darren Waller deal. They don’t have draft capital to give away. Vea likely has a few more good seasons left. Acquiring him, though, would mean giving him a lucrative long-term deal. That might not be smart with a player already on the wrong side of 30, especially since the Giants are not yet in position to contend for a championship. Vea as a Giant sounds nice. There are a lot of reasons why it should not, and probably will not, happen.

full_text: With New York Giants training camp beginning on Wednesday at The Greenbrier Resort in White Sulpher Springs, West Virginia, let’s look at where the Giants stand in pre-training camp power rankings. No one wants to give a timetable or talk about Week 1, which is usually a bad sign. The Athletic (No. 28) How good was Dexter Lawrence (who was traded to Cincinnati for the No. 10 pick, which turned into OT Francis Mauigoa)? So good that New York added seven new defensive linemen with a combined 48 years of NFL experience in hopes of filling his shoes. New Giants coach John Harbaugh also added first-round linebacker Arvell Reese to his defense. For The Win (No. 21) A possible surprising 4-1 start for New York being undone by a Jaxson Dart injury feels about right. Maybe John Harbaugh’s first miracle in New Jersey will be teaching him to slide. Sharp Football (No. 24) Super Bowl 61 Odds: +7000 I am sure the team would love it if Cam Skattebo would stop doing backflips and Malik Nabers shows he is 100% well before the season starts. Perhaps more importantly, the front office did a decent job rebuilding the defensive line, but that still looks like a worry spot. NFL Trade Rumors (No. 22) Valentine’s View These convinced me of a couple of things. The Giants still have a lot to prove to media writing about the NFL. Second, it seems like writers will never get tired of poking fun at Skattebo and Dart.

title: NY Giants news: Giants report to West Virginia for training camp
summary: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are your headlines for Wednesday, as we gear up for the beginning of training camp. Giants camp in W.Va.: Cool temps, plush grounds and some football | ESPN.com The Greenbrier boasts a state-of-the-art performance center, built in 2014, that has a locker room and multiple fields conducive to […]
full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are your headlines for Wednesday, as we gear up for the beginning of training camp. Giants camp in W.Va.: Cool temps, plush grounds and some football | ESPN.com The Greenbrier boasts a state-of-the-art performance center, built in 2014, that has a locker room and multiple fields conducive to hosting an NFL team for training camp. o, New York will take its training camp on the road for 12 days to West Virginia. It was a decision that was in the works before new coach John Harbaugh was hired. And the Greenbrier meets the Giants’ needs with two grass fields, a turf option (in case of rain), meeting rooms, offices, a weight room, player and coach locker rooms, a training room, a hydrotherapy room and an equipment room. The conditions are also conducive to a comfortable training camp. Temperatures usually range from the low 60s to around 80 degrees with low humidity in the mountains of West Virginia — cooler than the swamps of New Jersey. BBV’s Ed Valentine is on the scene Welcome to the Greenbrier practice facility. #NYG pic.twitter.com/9aNuiVvHIB — Big Blue View (@bigblueview) July 28, 2026 Vita Vea landing spots: Eight possible destinations for Buccaneers DT after trade request | NFL.com The need is clear after Big Blue traded Dexter Lawrence — perhaps the only current nose tackle better than Vea — this offseason. D.J. Reader is a solid veteran who can plug a hole, but he’s no Vea. It would take some work to fit Vea under the cap, but that shouldn’t be a prohibitor in the year of our Lord 2026 — of course, if the Giants didn’t want to pay Lawrence, they might balk at this scenario as well. Perhaps the Bucs would be interested in a Kayvon Thibodeaux swap? Vea playing alongside the likes of Brian Burns and Abdul Carter would provide a lethal front. Vea’s presence would also help clog the lanes for rookie Arvell Reese to torpedo in from the second level. Giants training camp preview: Why N.Y. decided to keep Malik Nabers off PUP list | The Athletic The Giants have been targeting a Week 1 return for Nabers, so they obviously didn’t prioritize the ability to potentially shift him to the reserve/PUP list. And even if Nabers isn’t ready for the opener, the Giants can evaluate him weekly rather than locking in a four-game absence. Of course, the Giants are hoping Nabers’ earlier start to practice this summer has him ready for Week 1. Avoiding the PUP list was a promising first step, but it’s not the final checkpoint. It will be a gradual process for Nabers and, barring any setbacks, it’s fair to be optimistic that he’ll be in the lineup against the Cowboys. 5 big questions as Giants open camp in West Virginia | New York Daily News Is Jaxson Dart The Guy? Everything about the Giants’ fortunes in the 2026 NFL season centers around the ability of second-year quarterback Jaxson Dart to grow as a pocket passer and a game manager and finisher. Dart, 23, has a lot on his plate to accomplish that. He is learning a new offense under a new coach and coordinator. He is in the public spotlight on the political side now after aligning with Donald Trump, which puts a different kind of spotlight on a young player who needs fewer distractions. Year 1 of Harbaugh’s program must be viewed as the beginning of a rebuild and turnaround that is not going to happen overnight. Dart, though, controls whether or not 2026 brings immediate promise in the team’s current core or if it demonstrates there is even more work to do than Harbaugh had hoped when he took the job. Exclusive: 2x Super Bowl champion Phil Simms on Jaxson Dart, John Harbaugh and the Giants prospects | Casino.org “It’s so huge to have that guy. I’ve been over there, and when John Harbaugh is in front of that group and they sit in that little theatre there with the lectern in front and Harbs comes in through that side door, trust me, everyone sits up straight and they’re a little bit nervous, because they know he’s the man and he is in charge. “But how he presents himself to the team, I’m just a big believer in him. He’s like Parcells. It didn’t matter if I had a great game or not; he’d come walk in that side door and he’d throw a pen on lectern and it was, not really fear, but he commanded your attention. What he’s creating there is a really good thing for that team.” Albert Breer’s Takeaways: With Fernando Mendoza Signed, the Raiders’ Positive Momentum Continues | SI..com Predictably, [John Harbaugh] got roasted on social media, because social media is a cynical place. But, again, this is in line with who Harbaugh is and what he built over 18 years in Baltimore. It reflected his reverence for the game’s history and, obviously, the Giants’ place in it—and that was indeed a real factor in why he picked New York over the other options he had in January. It also showed what he wants his players to establish, which is almost a college-like pride in the program they’re about to build. Bottom line, over 18 years, it wasn’t tough to identify what his Ravens were. My fourth-grader could spell it out. Big, tough, rugged, resourceful and smart. And it matches, in many ways, what the Giants’ best teams over the past half-century or so have been. So passing that mantle of Giants history on to the players in an effort to build a program that resembles the type he had in Baltimore makes all the sense in the world. Was the delivery of the message a little old-timey? Maybe. But that’s how the Harbaughs talk, and it’s genuine. And I’d bet, contrary to what people on X think, it works. Happy 23rd birthday, Malik! Jets transactions: * Placed Edge Joseph Ossai on the PUP list. * Moved WR Tim Patrick from PUP to active roster. #Jets — Rich Cimini (@RichCimini) July 28, 2026 A stint on the PUP list may sound daunting, but it only means the player is not ready to take the field for the first practice. title: Eagles News: Jalyx Hunt starts training camp strong
summary: Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Eagles 2026 training camp practice notes, Day 1: An initial look at Sean Mannion’s offense – PhillyVoiceJalyx Hunt had a great day. On one rep he had a 1-on-1 vs. Mailata, who was on an island. Hunt got Mailata leaning outside before jumping back inside […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - JANUARY 4: Jalyx Hunt #58 of the Philadelphia Eagles celebrates after an interception against the Washington Commanders at Lincoln Financial Field on January 4, 2026 in Philadelphia, United States. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Eagles 2026 training camp practice notes, Day 1: An initial look at Sean Mannion’s offense – PhillyVoice Jalyx Hunt had a great day. On one rep he had a 1-on-1 vs. Mailata, who was on an island. Hunt got Mailata leaning outside before jumping back inside with a free path to Hurts, and he got the “sack.” On the next play Hunt then beat Mailata to the outside for another “sack,” although that one was more of a coverage sack. Hunt also had a tackle for loss on Tank Bigsby, and he just generally he set the edge well against the run. 10 Eagles camp observations: Jonathan Greenard’s injury, Jalen Hurts’ new offense – The Athletic Two buzzworthy players who stood out in practice: Hunt and running back Tank Bigsby. Jalyx Hunt forced pressure against the Eagles’ first-team offensive line. Bigsby showed some juice catching the ball out of the backfield and could carve a role on offense. Eagles practice observations: Sean Mannion’s offense starts clicking; Jalen Hurts under center; Jalyx Hunt hunts – Inquirer Hunting season. Greenard’s absence pushed Jalyx Hunt into the starting spot at right outside linebacker opposite Nolan Smith Jr. Hunt will likely play as many snaps as the other two this season. There’s an argument to be made that he should get more playing time than Smith. Nevertheless, he took advantage of his opportunities with Greenard out. Hunt shot into the backfield unblocked and forced Hurts to check down to Cooper on one play-action pass that came from under center. He blew up tight end Dallas Goedert with an edge rush and Hurts had to hurry a dump to Bigsby that wasn’t caught. And he beat Mailata on back-to-back rushes — one with an inside move and the other from the outside — that blew up pass plays. Eagles Training Camp Practice Notes: Jalen Hurts and new offense show encouraging signs – BGN JALEN HURTS UPDATE: Just like the headline says, there were encouraging signs from the Eagles’ quarterback and the team’s new offense. Was it perfect? No, it wasn’t. There were drops. There were procedural penalties, as Lane Johnson brought up during his post-practice press conference. But this offense looked much more functional than the version that was largely dominated by Vic Fangio’s defense during the team’s spring practices. Training Camp Observations, Day 1: A Good, Boring Practice – Go Birds! Podcast Eliot Shorr-Parks is joined by Brandon Lee Gowton and Tucker Bagley to help break down the first day of 2026 Training Camp. The guys dive in to a solid day for Jalen Hurts, a slow day for the defense and express concern for a couple of the team’s rookies. Updated Roster Prediction – Iggles Blitz QB – 3 – Jalen Hurts, Tanner McKee, Cole Payton. The team has four QBs for now. Andy Dalton is the odd man out in my projection. The Eagles could look to trade him if some team wants a veteran this summer. They could also trade McKee, but only for a good return. The only way that happens is if another team loses a key QB due to injury and still wants to be competitive this season. I’m guessing McKee remains with the Eagles. Payton has to play his way onto the roster. Kyle McCord couldn’t do that last year. I think Payton is a better prospect and the team will do what they can to hold onto him because of his upside. Eagles training camp diary: The Sean Mannion era begins with a bang – PHLY Jalen Hurts has a new mantra. Listening to Nick Sirianni’s team address at the start of training camp, Jalen Hurts wrote down what will likely be his mantra for 2026: 100% alignment, 0% entitlement. Whether the phrase originated from Sirianni or if it was Hurts’ interpretation, Hurts opened his first press conference of the season emphasizing “discipline and unity” at the center of everything. Parse that how you choose, but it’s a message that underscores something Sirianni also harped on during the spring. When everyone is rowing in the same direction, this team has been more successful than just about anyone. Hurts seems to be acknowledging that from the jump this year. It’s fair to wonder if correlation doesn’t equal causation here. The 2024 Eagles had plenty of tension before going on to win Super Bowl LIX and the 2022 may have had the best “vibes” of any team I’ve covered, but it’s noteworthy nonetheless that Hurts and Sirianni are keying in on this so much at the start of the season in reflection of last year. 2026 Philadelphia Eagles training camp: Latest intel, updates – ESPN There were some encouraging signs from the Eagles’ new-look offense on Day 1 of camp. The learning curve they’re working through is obvious — there was one sequence where a pre-snap penalty was followed by a botched running play when Jalen Hurts and Saquon Barkley were on different pages. But there were also moments where things clicked, like on a hookup between Hurts and DeVonta Smith where Hurts dropped to his right and zipped a strike to his now-No. 1 receiver down the left seam with Quinyon Mitchell tight in coverage. Hurts worked primarily under center and targeted the middle of the field a good amount, departures from how he has generally operated to this point in the NFL. There was enough good mixed in to consider it a positive opening to the summer. Jalen Carter vows huge contract will only motivate him to work harder than ever – NBCSP He swears nothing will change. Nothing at all. Jalen Carter, $152 million wealthier than he was a couple days ago, promised Wednesday that becoming the highest-paid interior lineman in NFL history won’t change who he is or how he goes about his business. “I don’t really think the money is ever gonna change me,” Davis said after the first practice of training camp. When you get picked in the first round and you’re a top-10 pick, you kind of get a little bit of decent money. And that didn’t change me. I still came in, I had a goal, let the team know and the fans know that the goal was to get a championship. And it happened. But it’s a new contract and it’s time to get more championships for the city of Philly.” 2026 NFL All-Rookie Team projections: 25 impact newcomers on offense, defense and special teams – NFL.com TE Eli Stowers. In his four-year run with the Eagles, A.J. Brown averaged 130 targets per season. So, in the wake of Brown’s trade to New England, Philadelphia has an obvious pass-catching vacuum. Who will fill it? First-round receiver Makai Lemon certainly factors in as a slot machine to complement DeVonta Smith, but I wouldn’t overlook the potential impact of this second-round tight end. Truth be told, Stowers feels more like a supersized receiver at 6-4, 239 pounds. A converted quarterback who showcased rare athleticism at the NFL Scouting Combine, the reigning John Mackey Award winner (college football’s most outstanding tight end) wasn’t drafted to be an in-line blocker. But in an NFL that’s increasingly obsessed with multi-TE formations, new Eagles OC Sean Mannion could deploy the rookie in a playmaking role to complement veteran mainstay Dallas Goedert and recently inked blocking tight end Johnny Mundt. Players chirping. On a picture-perfect Wednesday at the Jefferson Health Training Complex, your favorite football team returned to the practice fields for Day 1 of the 2026 Training Camp and it was everything you’d hoped it would be. title: Eagles Training Camp Practice Notes: Jalen Hurts and new offense show encouraging signs
summary: Philadelphia Eagles training camp practice notes are back, baby! Today marked the Birds’ first summer practice ahead of the 2026 NFL season. It wasn’t padded and it lasted for about 70 minutes*. Here’s what I observed at the Jefferson Health Training Complex (formerly NovaCare). EAGLES PRACTICE NOTES UP NEXT: The Eagles practice again tomorrow starting […]
full_text: Jul 29, 2026; Philadelphia, PA, USA; Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts (1) walks out of a weight room for the start of training camp at Jefferson Health Training Complex. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Philadelphia Eagles training camp practice notes are back, baby! Today marked the Birds’ first summer practice ahead of the 2026 NFL season. It wasn’t padded and it lasted for about 70 minutes*. Here’s what I observed at the Jefferson Health Training Complex ( formerly NovaCare ). EAGLES PRACTICE NOTES JALEN HURTS UPDATE: Just like the headline says, there were encouraging signs from the Eagles’ quarterback and the team’s new offense. Was it perfect? No, it wasn’t. There were drops. There were procedural penalties, as Lane Johnson brought up during his post-practice press conference. But this offense looked much more functional than the version that was largely dominated by Vic Fangio’s defense during the team’s spring practices. There were a lot of under center play action looks. Hurts made some quality on-time completions in these situations. I wonder if under center play action helps Hurts’ timing because there’s more pressure to deliver the ball not knowing if a defender is bearing down on him while his back is turned to the defense, as opposed to him perhaps holding the ball too long while operating from shotgun and being able to see the defense at all times. Just a thought. Hurts made a good number of completions over the middle of the field, to which I saw a lot of “But I was told he couldn’t do that!” reactions. To that I’d say, the criticism hasn’t reasonably been about Hurts’ capability in that regard, though, as much as it has been about the frequency of his attempts between the numbers. Regardless, it was good to see him frequently target that portion of the field on Wednesday. Hurts had good back-to-back completions to Dontayvion Wicks and DeVonta Smith for moderate gains. The throw to Smith beat Quinyon Mitchell in coverage (update: see video below!) The highlight play of practice was Hurts hitting a diving Darius Cooper over the middle with an anticipatory throw against tight coverage. Not the first time I’ve said it this offseason and certainly not the first offseason I’ve said the following but it really does seem like Hurts is targeting running backs more often than usual. Answering a question about pass protection duties after practice, Saquon Barkley alluded to having a bigger role as a pass-catcher. So, maybe there’s really something to this?! Have to see it in the real games to fully believe it. I thought Hurts’ post-practice press conference was good. He included a line about “100 alignment, zero entitlement” in addition to speaking about an emphasis on “discipline and unity.” Was Hurts solely taking shots at A.J. Brown? I don’t believe that to be the case. But it’s probably more than zero percent about Brown. Hurts is very intentional and I think he’s preaching the right messages as he continues to take on a bigger leadership role every year. Stock up! Feels good to be seeing this again 🤌 pic.twitter.com/GdCUhyA6CP — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) July 29, 2026 Jalen Hurts said he’s emphasizing “discipline and unity” with his teammates as the Eagles begin training camp. pic.twitter.com/lNQ9dqYusg — Brandon Lee Gowton (@BrandonGowton) July 29, 2026 Jalen Hurts is rocking some bright cleats to start training camp. pic.twitter.com/J4DXxmR60J — Brandon Lee Gowton (@BrandonGowton) July 29, 2026 I am trying not to overreact to what we’ve seen in practice settings thus far but it’s hard not to buy the Eagles’ offense looking stylistically different under Sean Mannion this season. Obviously, we need to see it carry over to the real games, and it’s the results of those differences that matter most. Sean Mannion hands on working with the Eagles’ QBs. pic.twitter.com/D61ad6QBPk — Brandon Lee Gowton (@BrandonGowton) July 29, 2026 The general vibe of the team seems to be pretty positive! Which is somewhat to be expected at this time of year when optimism is abound. Still, things feel good, which is good! And therefore not bad. You can’t get this kind of high-level analysis anywhere else. EAGLES INJURY UPDATES: The Eagles officially placed Jonathan Greenard on the active/PUP list prior to practice. Howie Roseman revealed that the veteran edge rusher suffered a pectoral strain while lifting weights. He added that it is “not a long-term injury; nothing to be concerned about.” The rest of the roster is apparently healthy, which is huge! (Though I did not explicitly see Drew Kendall taking part in team drills, which was also the case at times in the spring. But maybe I just missed him being in there.) Jalen Carter, Makai Lemon, and Jihaad Campbell were notably back in action after missing time during OTAs/minicamp. Important to see. 2026 DRAFT CLASS UPDATES: Lemon made some short catches via Hurts passes, nothing flashy. Eli Stowers was invisible to me just like he was in the spring ( speaking together on a practice recap episode of the Go Birds! podcast , Eliot Shorr-Parks said he only noticed Stowers when he bobbled a short catch). Markel Bell continues to rep at second-team right tackle. Cole Payton made some good throws, more on that later. Micah Morris repped with the third-team offensive line. Didn’t really notice Cole Wisniewski, Uar Bernard, or Keyshawn James-Newby do much. All aboard the Tank Bigsby hype train. The Eagles’ No. 2 running back saw some run with the first-team offense (behind Saquon Barkley, of course) and stood out on two plays. The first was a long run up the middle where he fought through “contact” and looked explosive. The second was a catch-and-run that he set up by coming back to the ball and cutting upfield in a way that shook his defender to get yards after the catch. The dude clearly has juice. They’ve gotta find ways to get him involved. Dontayvion Wicks dropped a Hurts pass that Quinyon Mitchell may have gotten a hand on. Wicks has struggled with drops in the past, so, it would be good to see him avoid those issues in camp. Good to see the aforementioned Darius Cooper make some good catches. It was a quiet spring for him but, as I’ve said, he comes alive in the summer. Just like he did last year. SAFETY BATTLE: Marcus Epps took the first first-team safety reps in nickel defense (Cooper DeJean is the first-team safety next to Andrew Mukuba in base). But Michael Carter II also saw some time with the starters in place of Epps. BACKUP QUARTERBACK BATTLE: The QB2 competition we saw in the spring is rolling on to camp. Tanner McKee took the first set of second-team reps, including in the pre-practice walkthrough portion. But McKee and Andy Dalton frequently rotated with the backups. McKee didn’t do anything that made my notes while Dalton made some positive completions to a leaping Johnny Wilson and Hollywood Brown in stride on a quick slant. More on QB4, who saw limited action with the third-team offense. Cole Payton made a ballsy attempt over the middle to a contested Quez Watkins, who made the grab in 7-on-7. On the final play of practice, Payton completed a downfield pass to Britain Covey, who was able to find the end zone after the catch. Good to see that Payton doesn’t look scared to pull the trigger, as can be the case with some rookie quarterbacks. Payton is slowly but surely building the case for the Eagles to keep him as a developmental option. Dameon Pierce had a long run at one point. Could be the favorite to be RB4, likely on the practice squad, although the Eagles did keep four running backs last season. The second-team offensive line I saw: LT Fred Johnson, LG Michael Jordan, C Jake Majors, RG Myles Hinton, Markel Bell. Third-team offensive line: LT John Ojukwu, LG Hollin Pierce, C Willie Lampkin, RG Micah Morris, RT Cameron Williams. As you may have noticed, there wasn’t a ton to say about the defense today. The biggest standout from that…

title: Jalen Hurts prioritizes “discipline and unity” for the 2026 Eagles
summary: The Eagles finished their first training camp practice of the year on Wednesday, but before they went off to meetings, quarterback Jalen Hurts stopped to talk to reporters. He opened up talking about the summer and his focus as the team comes back together to continue building a new system. “I feel like it was […]
full_text: The Eagles finished their first training camp practice of the year on Wednesday, but before they went off to meetings, quarterback Jalen Hurts stopped to talk to reporters. He opened up talking about the summer and his focus as the team comes back together to continue building a new system. “I feel like it was a good summer — a really good summer. I’ve been able to spend time with the guys and really build toward everything we’ve transitioned to. Everybody’s very hungry and excited to go to work, and we’re really focused on that. I’d say one of my main points coming in, especially talking to my teammates and getting a sense of where we are throughout the summer and where we’re going, is the importance of discipline and unity. I can’t emphasize enough how important it is to carry and protect the intimacy of this team and what we do, because it takes all of us. And we know that there are challenges that come throughout the year, we’re not looking forward, we’re really just focused on where we are right now, and taking advantage of this training camp. So, to come out here, and have the conditioning test, have the first day be out here to get it in, it’s a good start, a good foundation. Just going to continue to progress forward and take it one day at a time.“ Here’s what else the QB had to say: On connecting with teammates Hurts said that he’s always intentional about trying to get the guys together away from the building, and feels like that works is reflected in the season. The QB talked about being able to get some of the younger guys together, which was something he did ahead of the 2024 season, and then also work with individual teammates, as well. “I think it was really good to have everybody all-in on it going into this offseason, and have everybody expressing and showing that hunger to build and kind of learn each other’s personalities a bit so we can go out there and thrive on the field. So, I was definitely excited about that, and I think it’ll pay forward — the work will show.” The quarterback said that the standard was set by head coach Nick Sirianni in his first words to the team to open training camp, and the commitment to being aligned. “Honestly, it starts with Coach Sirianni and his message. And, his first words in yesterday’s team meeting was about being together and being aligned, and when I was taking notes of it, I just thought about, 100 percent alignment and zero entitlement. So, as a team, that’s what everybody’s pushing.” On OC Sean Mannion “I think Coach [Mannion] is going to be just fine. He’s gotta lot of structure and a lot of intentionality behind what he does.” Hurts went on to say that he’s at a point now in his career, where he needs to step in and help Mannion in terms of keeping up his end of the deal — not necessarily be of service to the new OC, but to help bridge the old and the new. With the QB having a new OC annually, he noted that there’s really nothing different going into this season. On Jalen Carter’s new contract "I took that five-dollar bill, and I went and gave it to Jalen Carter, and I smacked it on his chest, and I said, 'Let me put five on top of that.'" 😂 pic.twitter.com/C9o7dzcUIi — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) July 29, 2026 Other notables Hurts said that the number one thing he’s seen from rookie WR Makai Lemon has been his heart, and his hunger for the game. The QB quipped that it’s a little different for him now, having been in the league so long that Lemon was actually in high school when Hurts was drafted to the Eagles. As for what constitutes as a good camp for the quarterback, he explained that it’s all about getting on the same page with his offensive coordinator heading into the year and then relaying everything to his teammates so they’re all on the same page. “I’m always seeking alignment, and then I think with different pieces that come and go, it can make that challenging or it can make it easier.” Hurts also talked about DeVonta Smith’s development over the years and said that the WR has always been really polished, but he’s really smooth at this point in his career. The QB recalled back to their college days at Alabama when all the other receivers declared for the draft, but Smith didn’t, so he’s someone who has had to take a backseat at times, but he’s always had that hunger to be the guy. He also commented on LeBron James joining the 76ers, and Hurts said that it’s huge for the city of Philadelphia and will be exciting to have such a dominant sports figure in the city.

title: Zack Baun is the latest Eagle named to the NFL Top 100 list
summary: The NFL has changed their roll-out of the Top 100 list, as voted by players, and it took several weeks before an Eagles player was named to the 2026 iteration — but now we’re up to three: There are still several Eagles expected to be revealed over the next few weeks, including guys like Cooper […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - DECEMBER 14: Zack Baun #53 of the Philadelphia Eagles carries the ball after an interception against the Las Vegas Raiders during the second quarter at Lincoln Financial Field on December 14, 2025 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL has changed their roll-out of the Top 100 list, as voted by players, and it took several weeks before an Eagles player was named to the 2026 iteration — but now we’re up to three: No. 45 — Zack Baun, LB No. 47 — Quinyon Mitchell, CB No. 56 — Jalen Hurts, QB There are still several Eagles expected to be revealed over the next few weeks, including guys like Cooper DeJean, Jalen Carter, and Saquon Barkley. The rest of the list will continue to be revealed two players per day, Monday through Friday, and then one player per day beginning Monday, August 24 through Friday, September 4. Here’s where Eagles players have ranked in the 2026 NFL Top 100 list up to this point: No. 45: Zack Baun, LB The Eagles signed their defensive leader to a big money contract last offseason and he went on to prove that he was worth the commitment. Baun continued to dominate in 2025, finishing with 123 total tackles, 64 solo, 7 pass breakups, 3.5 sacks, a career-high two interceptions, and one forced fumble. The LB is just as committed as he’s been since arriving in Philly, and should have an equally impressive season in 2026. No. 45 on the NFL Top 100 Players of 2026… @Eagles LB Zack Baun! @NFLFilms pic.twitter.com/VUd3Bketx6 — NFL (@NFL) July 29, 2026 No. 47: Quinyon Mitchell , CB Coming off his second season, Mitchell earned All-Pro and was immediately recognized as one of the best corners in the league. He finished the 2025 season with 17 pass breakups, allowed just 39 completions, and allowed only 94 total yards after the catch all season. The expectations for his third season have only grown, but there’s no doubt he’s capable of rising to the occasion. ESPN’s Top 100 list, as voted on by coaches and executives, knocked Mitchell for his lack of interceptions up to this point in his career, but Mitchell is consistently and reliably doing his job and locking down the best receivers in the game — his peers, at least, seem to recognize how dominant he is. No. 47 on the NFL Top 100 Players of 2026… @Eagles CB Quinyon Mitchell! @NFLFilms pic.twitter.com/bOQbShgDrv — NFL (@NFL) July 28, 2026 No. 56: Jalen Hurts, QB The former Super Bowl MVP dropped a bit in this year’s list, but still ranked higher than Lamar Jackson (No. 69), Jordan Love (No. 72), and Baker Mayfield (No. 77). Hurts has a lot on his shoulders this season as the Eagles embrace a new OC and scheme, but he has done nothing but prove time-after-time that he’s up for any challenge. He’s certainly spent the offseason focused on building a solid foundation with his offensive teammates, and every indication is he’s ready for another big season. NFL’s Jeremy Bergman explains Hurts’ ranking : “Hurts threw for a career-high 25 touchdowns and rushed for eight more en route to a third Pro Bowl bid in four years. The QB’s decreased completion percentage and use in the run game likely contributed to his 37-spot drop in this year’s list, his lowest ranking since before his 2023 debut at No. 3. But Hurts remains one of the NFL’s top dual-threat signal-callers entering his seventh NFL season, with or without the departed A.J. Brown.“ No. 56 on the NFL Top 100 Players of 2026… @Eagles QB Jalen Hurts! @NFLFilms pic.twitter.com/vkX3kqTfSI — NFL (@NFL) July 22, 2026 Former Eagles on the list: No. 61 — CB Kevin Byard (Patriots) No. 78 — LB Josh Sweat (Cardinals) No. 80 — WR A.J. Brown (Patriots)

full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 21: Head coach Nick Sirianni talks to Jalen Carter #98 of the Philadelphia Eagles look on against the Los Angeles Rams at Lincoln Financial Field on September 21, 2025 in Philadelphia, United States. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Eagles were back in the building on Wednesday and ahead of the team’s first training camp practice of the year, GM Howie Roseman and head coach Nick Sirianni spoke to reporters about Jalen Carter’s new contract extension . Roseman acknowledged that they typically like to get their deals done in March or April, but re-signing Carter — along with Jordan Davis — was always a priority and the DT market was in a bit of a transition with guys like Dexter Lawrence and Jeffery Simmons getting new deals. Both sides were kind of waiting to see where the market would land, but they were eager and excited to get something done before camp started. The GM said that it’s increasingly difficult to find talented defensive lineman ready to play Day 1 in college, and they felt like their DT room was really strong and wanted to keep it together. He also groused at any indication that the team had concerns about Carter’s off-field behavior, saying that the DT has had no issues since coming to Philly several years ago. ROSEMAN: “I don’t know what off-field concerns since Jalen [Carter]‘s been here. He’s put his head down, he’s worked hard. He’s made huge impactful plays for this organization, for this team. Last year, he wasn’t 100 percent. He was trying to fight through that, and play through that. We understand that. Like anyone, when you’re 25 years old, you’re still growing as a person and a player.“ Sirianni expressed his excitement for Carter and his family, pointing out how hard the DT has worked to get to this moment. SIRIANNI: “I’ve really enjoyed getting to know Jalen [Carter], and more-and-more each year. And the time that I’ve spent with him, he’s put his head down, he’s worked, he’s made impactful plays, and we look for that to continue. And he’s a heck of a football player that demands a lot of attention by the opposing offense, so to be able to have him locked up and we know what that creates for opposing offenses.” The head coach admitted that he’s happy that the new contract got done and isn’t something that they need to have lingering into training camp. He also gave a lot of credit to Carter for staying focused throughout the process. SIRIANNI: “I give [Jalen Carter] a lot of credit. He’s focused so much on football, he came back in phenomenal shape — with his weight, with his conditioning test. So even with that contract still looming, he worked his ass off, and I’m proud of him for that. And it shows you the type of guy he is, and he’ll continue to be, and excited for him to play ball.” Sirianni also said he isn’t worried that off-field issues will arise moving forward now that Carter earned the big-money deal. He explained that the team brings in players who fit their locker room culture, and he has yet to see someone earn a new contract and change their habits and approach to the game.
author: Alexis Chassen

summary: The Eagles are finally gearing up for their first training camp practice of 2026, but just ahead of the team taking the field, they announced that edge rusher Jonathan Greenard was placed on the active/Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list. The move was a bit of a surprise, but Eagles GM Howie Roseman spoke to […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - MAY 27: Jonathan Greenard #52 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on during OTA offseason workouts at Jefferson Health Training Complex on May 27, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Eagles are finally gearing up for their first training camp practice of 2026, but just ahead of the team taking the field, they announced that edge rusher Jonathan Greenard was placed on the active/Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list. The move was a bit of a surprise, but Eagles GM Howie Roseman spoke to reporters shortly after the news was announced and explained that Greenard suffered a pec strain while he was lifting. Roseman noted that they still expect him to be ready to go by Week 1, saying, “Not a long-term injury, nothing to be concerned about.” Greenard was the new veteran voice for a still-young group of edge rushers this offseason, and was brought in as a replacement of sorts for Jaelan Phillips. It’s unfortunate he’ll miss these training camp reps to build timing and instincts with his new teammates, but hopefully he’s back on the field soon — and thankfully he was able to participate in the rest of the team’s offseason program. Some have wondered if Greenard on PUP leaves an opening to get Brandon Graham back in the fold much earlier than they did last season, but Roseman wouldn’t talk about the conversations he has with his first-ever Eagles draft pick, only to say that they do and will continue to communicate. Note that Greenard still counts against the Eagles’ limit while on active/PUP. If he begins the regular season on reserve/PUP, he will automatically miss the first four games … but it sounds like Greenard will be activated before then.

title: Eagles training camp preview: 53-man roster prediction
summary: Philadelphia Eagles training camp is here! Players reported to the NovaCare Complex on Tuesday, July 28 ahead of the team’s first practice on Wednesday, July 29. Before the on-field action gets started, let’s run through everyone’s favorite summer activity: a 53-player roster prediction. The objective here is to get an early look at how the […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - DECEMBER 20: Will Shipley #28 of the Philadelphia Eagles carries the ball before the NFL game against the Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium on December 20, 2025 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images Philadelphia Eagles training camp is here! Players reported to the NovaCare Complex on Tuesday, July 28 ahead of the team’s first practice on Wednesday, July 29. Before the on-field action gets started, let’s run through everyone’s favorite summer activity: a 53-player roster prediction. The objective here is to get an early look at how the Eagles’ initial depth chart could play out. We’ll certainly update these projections throughout the summer to reflect meaningful developments from practices and preseason games. ( For fun, take a look at my last 53-man roster projection from exactly one month ago .) OFFENSE QUARTERBACK: Jalen Hurts, Tanner McKee, Cole Payton (3) [3] This feels like an especially important camp for Hurts as he adjusts to a new offense under Sean Mannion. It’ll be really interesting to monitor his progress. McKee is the Eagles’ second-best quarterback. He’s shown promise in small sample sizes. Andy Dalton, who turns 39 in October, seemed to be QB2 in spring practices based on how the reps were divvied up but he just didn’t look very good. At this point in time, I struggle to see how Dalton belongs on this roster meritoriously. Payton has enough potential to warrant a third quarterback role. RUNNING BACK: Saquon Barkley, Tank Bigsby, Will Shipley (3) [6] If the Eagles’ offensive line is healthy, there’s no reason Barkley shouldn’t have another big year. Bigsby is simply too good to go underutilized but it’s not like the coaching staff is going to be eager to take touches away from Barkley. Shipley isn’t a player that excites fans but he’s going to have a role as a kick returner/special teams contributor/two-minute drill back/etc. Dameon Pierce and Elijah Mitchell are likely competing for a fourth running back spot but the Eagles can probably just keep at least one of them around on the practice squad. WIDE RECEIVER: DeVonta Smith, Makai Lemon, Dontayvion Wicks, Hollywood Brown, Johnny Wilson , Darius Cooper (6) [12] DeVonta is going to have a huge year. How good do you feel about the receivers behind Smitty? The Eagles are counting on Lemon to make significant contributions as a rookie. It’s possible he’ll be really good from the jump; we’ll see if that’s the case or not in camp. Nick Sirianni has framed Wicks as a top three receiver on this team and even compared aspects of his game to Keenan Allen. Brown is probably being slept on and it’s possible he could be WR3 but for now he’s WR4. Wilson currently seems to have the inside track on being the “dirty work” wide receiver over Cooper. Don’t forget that Cooper really came alive last summer, though, and he could do it again here. I do think DC might make sense as a trade candidate for more depth at a different position, something akin to the Thomas Booker for Jakorian Bennett deal last year. Elijah Moore is a name to watch here, though I tend to think he could stay around on the practice squad, which is where he finished the 2025 season as a member of the Denver Broncos. Britain Covey could begin the season on the practice squad as the Eagles’ primary punt returner. TIGHT END: Dallas Goedert, Johnny Mundt, Eli Stowers, Cameron Latu (4) [16] Goedert is the clear top tight end and he could see more volume than he did last year in the aftermath of A.J. Brown’s departure. The front office might prefer Stowers to play more than Mundt but the coaching staff could be inclined to better trust the latter. Stowers was a part-time player in college and could need more seasoning before he’s ready to contribute in the NFL. Mundt is expected to at least be a good blocker. Latu could contribute as a fullback in addition to being a stud on special teams. OFFENSIVE LINE: Jordan Mailata, Landon Dickerson, Cam Jurgens, Tyler Steen, Lane Johnson, Fred Johnson, Markel Bell, Drew Kendall, Myles Hinton, Micah Morris (10) [26] The starting offensive line should be one of the best in the NFL … if healthy. And that’s a big “if.” It’ll be very encouraging if Dickerson and Jurgens can make it through camp without any issues. Big Fred could be a surprise cut candidate if the Eagles feel like Bell is ready to be the swing tackle as a rookie but I tend to think they’ll lean towards keeping him. Kendall is unproven but the Eagles are seemingly counting on him to be the top interior option, just like Brett Toth was last season. Hinton is training at left guard after spending his rookie season at tackle; demonstrating versatility could help him make the roster. The Eagles might not want to cut Morris as a rookie. Cameron Williams and Willie Lampkin are tough cuts here but the Eagles might be able to stash them on injured reserve or something. Veteran journeyman Michael Jordan could also push for a roster spot. DEFENSE EDGE DEFENDER: Jonathan Greenard, Nolan Smith, Jalyx Hunt, Arnold Ebiketie, A.J. Epenesa (5) [31] Mark my words: barring injury, Greenard will get back to being a double-digit sacker this season. He’s going to be a real nice addition to this defense. It’ll be interesting to see how the Eagles split snaps between Smith and Hunt. It’s easier to be bullish about the latter at this point in time but I think some are forgetting just how good Smith was for a large portion of the Eagles’ Super Bowl LIX-winning season. The 2023 first-round pick could bounce back after a lost year in 2025. Ebiketie is a fine fit as a fourth or fifth edge rusher. Epenesa’s medical situation bears monitoring after he failed a physical earlier this year but he should be able to make the roster if he’s healthy. Brandon Graham can still play but it doesn’t seem like the Eagles are rushing to bring him back for one last ride. And BG said he would like to have a camp under his belt if he’s going to come back for 2026. DEFENSIVE TACKLE: Jalen Carter, Jordan Davis, Moro Ojomo, Byron Young, Gabe Hall (5) [36] Carter won’t be holding out nor holding in after receiving a big-time contract extension . The Eagles are counting on him to be healthier and much more effective this season. If Carter lives up to his potential, he can be the engine of the NFL’s very best defense. The Eagles also paid big money to Davis because they believe his best football is ahead of him. Ojomo is on the Milton Williams path to have a big contract year before getting handsomely rewarded by a new team in free agency. Vic Fangio clearly likes “BY,” so, he’s DT4. Hall was lining up next to Young on the second-team defensive line in the spring. He’s also just about four months older than Ty Robinson, who really struggled as a rookie. The Eagles probably don’t want to risk exposing Uar Bernard to waivers but he’s clearly not ready to play at all in 2026. They might be able to stash him away. LINEBACKER: Zack Baun, Jihaad Campbell, Jeremiah Trotter Jr., Smael Mondon Jr. (4) [40] Baun is a stud. Campbell has flashed serious potential. One would hope he’ll be full go in camp after he missed spring practices due to his shoulder recovery. Trot Jr. isn’t realistically going to beat out Campbell but he’s going to try his hardest to make it close; Trot’s a good player. Mondon Jr. has showed enough potential on defense in addition to being a special teams guy. The Eagles could feasibly keep five at this position with Chance Campbell making the team. He could force the team’s hand by having a strong summer. CORNERBACK: Quinyon Mitchell, Riq Woolen, Cooper DeJean, Jonathan Jones, Kelee Ringo (5) [45] No one will be surprised when Q has another All-Pro season. Would be nice to see him get his first career regular season interception in 2026. There might be some volatility with Woolen but I’m bullish on the good outweighing the bad with him. DeJean is an elite slot defender who will also be playing at safety in the…
