title: Eagles News: Jalen Carter contract extension draws praise
summary: Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Jalen Carter and the Eagles struck a deal. What’s next for the franchise and NFL’s highest-paid DT? – The AthleticBerman: This was a smart move for the Eagles. Carter is a premium player — a true blue-chip talent with the upside to be the defensive […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 23: Jalen Carter #98 of the Philadelphia Eagles works against Cooper Beebe #56 of the Dallas Cowboys during a game at AT&T Stadium on November 23, 2025 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Jalen Carter and the Eagles struck a deal. What’s next for the franchise and NFL’s highest-paid DT? – The Athletic Berman: This was a smart move for the Eagles. Carter is a premium player — a true blue-chip talent with the upside to be the defensive player of the year, and those players are hard to find. He’s a building block for the Eagles. It’s a steep price, but it wasn’t going to go down. I was surprised that it stretched this far, but it was still his first offseason as an offseason-eligible player for a new deal. That’s how the Eagles have operated with their foundational players drafted in recent years, from Jalen Hurts to DeVonta Smith to Landon Dickerson to Cam Jurgens. His influence on the defense cannot be measured by his statistics. When Carter is at his best, he can change a game. (Sean McVay might have another Super Bowl if not for the way Carter played against the Rams on the final drive in the NFC divisional round playoff game in 2025.) The Eagles can and should expect more from him — whether it’s consistency or maturity — and my guess is that was part of the calculation in the investment. It’s incumbent upon Carter to understand as much. The Eagles made clear how much they valued him with this record-breaking deal. Carter is one of the best players in the league. The Eagles were smart to be aggressive. Jalen Carter Extended – Iggles Blitz Carter’s best football is ahead of him, which is good news for the Eagles and bad news for the guys who have to block him. He’s still putting all the pieces together. If he stays healthy this season, he could have a breakout year. There is the possibility that the money will have a negative effect on him, but I think playing for Clint Hurtt and Vic Fangio will be enough to keep him on the right path. At his best, this is a guy you want in the middle of your defense. Jalen Carter, Eagles agree to record-breaking contract extension – BGN Jalen Carter will neither be holding out nor holding in for a new contract this summer. With Philadelphia Eagles players reporting to the Jefferson Health Training Complex for training camp on Tuesday, the team officially announced they’ve reached a new deal with their two-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle. Carter and the Eagles have reportedly agreed to a four-year, $152 million extension that could end up being worth $160 million, including $106 million guaranteed. This keeps the defensive tackle in Philly through 2031, right alongside Jordan Davis — who signed his own three-year, $78 million extension earlier this offseason. With Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis signing long-term deals with the Eagles, who’s next? – PhillyVoice Likely gone next offseason: iDL Moro Ojomo. During training camp, Ojomo was by far the top “stock up” vote getter in our annual “stock up / stock down” training camp media poll. And sure enough, he had a breakout season, collecting 38 tackles, six sacks, and 12 QB hits while playing 66 percent of the team’s defensive snaps. The Eagles were hopeful that he could capably fill in for Milton Williams, who had departed in free agency last offseason, and Ojomo delivered. JimmyVerdict: The Eagles would undoubtedly love to keep Ojomo, but after signing Carter and Davis to massive long-term deals — and the aforementioned deals for Mitchell, DeJean, and Hunt on the horizon — it’s going to be hard for the Eagles to afford him. The very obvious play from Ojomo’s camp is to wait until free agency next offseason, and cash in, like Williams did. Enjoy Moro for one last season. Eagles training camp preview: Reacting to Jalen Carter’s extension, previewing top position battles – PHLY Player I’ll be watching on Day 1, offense edition: Makai Lemon. Makai Lemon seems to be ready for camp after being sidelined with a hamstring injury during spring workouts, setting up a pivotal few weeks for the first-round rookie to acclimate to Mannion’s system and build a rapport with Jalen Hurts. He’s the type of player who should look good in training camp, so there’s reason for cautious optimism there. The Eagles need him to look good, too. Of the options at receiver around him, there isn’t one that projects as cleanly into the No. 2 role behind Smith as a featured member of the passing game and possibly the third-highest target getter behind Dallas Goedert. Eagles coach Nick Sirianni has been bullish on Dontayvion Wicks since the team traded for the 25-year-old, but projecting him into the No. 2 receiver spot is, well, a projection. Smith was second on the team with 113 targets last year and Goedert had the third-highest total at 82. Wicks’ most prolific season was two years ago, when he had 76 targets, 39 catches, and 415 receiving yards. Even more staggering, Wicks’ catch rate that year was just 51.3% compared to Smith’s 68.1% and Goedert’s 73.2%. Wicks caught 65.2% of his 46 targets last season, though, and the Eagles will be banking on that upward trend continuing. Hollywood Brown’s career history has more evidence of him being capable of handling heavy usage, although his numbers have been trending down some in recent years. He’s had triple-digit targets in four consecutive seasons between 2020-2023, but would probably be better suited as a horizontal/vertical stretch role player for this receiving corps rather than a true mainstay at the top of the depth chart. For that reason, it’ll likely come down mostly to whether Lemon can hit the ground running this summer. NFL position battles in 2026: Picks to win 12 notable training camp competitions – NFL.com EDGE RUSHER OPPOSITE JONATHAN GREENARD: Jalyx Hunt vs. Nolan Smith Jr. Given how many defensive backs and defensive linemen teams rotate onto the field, there are not a ton of camp battles of consequence on defense. Even if a player doesn’t earn a starting gig, he’ll likely play a significant role. That’s true in Philly, but I wanted to highlight the edge battle between Hunt and Smith. The trade for Greenard underscored the Eagles’ need at pass rusher. Smith was pivotal during the Super Bowl run of 2024, but the triceps injury suffered in the Lombardi-lifting game seemed to take some of his bite away last season. Will he return to form? Hunt flashed upside while getting more reps in 2025, and feels like a smoother fit in Vic Fangio’s defense. Hunt has the upside to take his game to an even higher level after leading the club with 6.5 sacks last season. The outcome of this battle could play a big role in deciding which player gets paid to stay in Philly long-term. THE PICK: Hunt. Did he already break out or is there another level for the third-year pro to hit? I’m buying the latter. The six biggest roster battles as Eagles training camp gets underway – Inquirer Safety: Will Marcus Epps hold off the field? It’s worth starting with safety because it’s one of the few spots on the field where a starter is written in pencil and not pen. If you’ve been paying any attention to the Eagles since the spring, you know that Cooper DeJean is slated to move from nickel to safety in base defense. But the Eagles, like most NFL defenses, use nickel and dime packages much more often than base. So the spot next to Andrew Mukuba mostly will be manned by someone not named DeJean. Vic Fangio indicated that Marcus Epps is in the pole position for the job to replace Reed Blankenship, but the 30-year-old will have to earn it. There will be competition from converted nickel Michael Carter II, seventh-round pick Cole Wisniewski, veteran special teamer J.T. Gray, and long shots like Andre’ Sam, Kapena Gushiken, and Maximus Pulley. Don’t count out another roster addition, too, if Howie Roseman decides the Eagles need to upgrade the safety spot.…

full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 27: Jordan Whitehead #3 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers warms up prior to an NFL football game against the Atlanta Falcons at Raymond James Stadium on October 27, 2024 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Steelers reported to training camp on Tuesday and took the field for the first official practice on Wednesday afternoon. It’s a homecoming for the franchise, going back to Latrobe for the 59th training camp at St. Vincent College. The Steelers may also be eying a Pittsburgh native defensive back for a homecoming of his own. According to Noah Strackbein of Sports Illustrated , the Steelers are discussing a contract with free-agent safety Jordan Whitehead. “According to sources, the Steelers and free agent defensive back Jordan Whitehead are discussing the possibility of a deal, and there’s believed to be mutual interest between the two sides in getting something done,” Strackbein writes. A Central Valley and University of Pittsburgh alum, Whitehead missed the entire 2025 season after suffering a severe neck injury during a car accident in 2024. A seven-year veteran who won Super Bowl LV with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2020, Whitehead was a dependable starter before injury. He was drafted in the fourth round of the 2018 NFL Draft and played four seasons in Tampa Bay before joining the New York Jets for two years. He re-joined the Bucs in 2024 and made 79 tackles in 12 games. Over the course of his NFL career, Whitehead has started 101 of 105 games and recorded a career-best four interceptions in 2023. He owns 557 combined tackles, 31 tackles for loss, 45 passes defended, two forced fumbles, two fumble recoveries, 2.5 sacks, and 11 interceptions in seven years. The Steelers signed Gateway and Penn State alum Jaquan Brisker to join the safety room on a one-year deal, and retained DeShon Elliott and Jalen Ramsey on the roster. Whitehead could become the second WPIAL safety in recent history to play a meaningful role for the Steelers and join North Allegheny and Penn State’s Joey Porter Jr. in the defensive back room. summary: LATROBE— It was a picture-perfect overcast day at Saint Vincent College for the first training camp practice of 2026. Practice only lasted a little over an hour, and pads don’t go on until Monday, but there are still plenty of things to take away from the Steelers’ first training camp practice under Mike McCarthy. full_text: Jul 29, 2026; Latrobe, PA, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Drew Allar (16) throws a pass following a practice session at Saint Vincent College. Mandatory Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect LATROBE— It was a picture-perfect overcast day at Saint Vincent College for the first training camp practice of 2026. Practice only lasted a little over an hour, and pads don’t go on until Monday, but there are still plenty of things to take away from the Steelers’ first training camp practice under Mike McCarthy. Here are some guys who helped their stock, and others who are hoping for a better Day 2. Stock up: QB Drew Allar We got to see the full Drew Allar experience today in Latrobe. Although it is tough to differentiate between who is doing well or not while nobody is tackling or wearing pads, it’s tough to argue that Allar didn’t have the best moments of any quarterback today. The third-rounder fired a ball over the middle of the field to wide receiver Max Hurleman in seven-on-sevens that, for what it’s worth, would have gone for a touchdown. Allar then followed that throw up with an interception on a deflected ball and two more that defenders batted down. On the final play of practice, Allar fired a 25-yard rope to tight end Robert Tonyan in the back of the end zone for a touchdown. We all know Allar is a work in progress, but it was encouraging to see some exciting throws from him on day 1. CB Asante Samuel Jr With Joey Porter Jr. and Jalen Ramsey on the PUP list to start camp, Samuel Jr. went against the first team for many of his reps today in practice. During team periods, quarterback Aaron Rodgers tried to hit DK Metcalf on a streak down the right sideline, but Samuel ran stride for stride with Metcalf and tipped the ball away. LB Patrick Queen Queen and Cole Holcomb handled the first team linebacker reps today as Queen stood out. The linebacker has several quality reps in coverage in red zone drills and in 7-on-7’s. Queen admitted after practice that last year was a bit of a “down year” for him, but he is working to do everything he can to be better this season. Today was a great start for him in that regard. Stock down: OT Broderick Jones It was great to see that Jones has been activated and will be available to participate for the start of camp after suffering a neck injury last November in Chicago against the Bears. After the team drafted Max Iheanachor, many assumed that Jones would not be able to participate for the start of camp. Jones ran with the second team at left tackle and looked noticeably thinner than he has in recent years. Jones then worked with the third and fourth teams later in practice. Dylan Cook took the first team reps at right tackle as expected. The Steelers are going to ease Jones along as he recovers from injury, but it’s tough to see Jones having a legitimate shot to earn his starting spot back barring injury. QB Aaron Rodgers It was a slow first practice for Rodgers and the first team offense, who failed to score during a two-minute drill opportunity and were also held scoreless in red zone shots at the end of practice. Rodgers was throwing early and often underneath to Roman Wilson, but the pair also seemed to have had a miscommunication downfield. Rodgers and rookie receiver Germie Bernard also had a moment where it seemed like they weren’t on the same page. Head coach Mike McCarthy also noted before practice that Rodgers would be on a bit of a pitch count this week, likely in preparation for fully padded practices next week. This week will have a heavy emphasis on ironing out those miscommunications between Rodgers and his receivers. Let us know what you think in the comments . title: Steelers training camp: Drew Allar’s touchdown, Roman Wilson highlight first practice
summary: LATROBE — Training camp is officially underway in Latrobe for the Pittsburgh Steelers as they officially begin their 2026 season. While the first handful of practices are padless, there were still plenty of takeaways from Day One, including a big performance from Drew Allar, and a cornerback making the most of his increased reps. Roman […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - JUNE 11: Drew Allar #16 of the Pittsburgh Steelers in action at UPMC Rooney Sports Complex on June 11, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images LATROBE — Training camp is officially underway in Latrobe for the Pittsburgh Steelers as they officially begin their 2026 season. While the first handful of practices are padless, there were still plenty of takeaways from Day One, including a big performance from Drew Allar, and a cornerback making the most of his increased reps. Roman Wilson and his usage in the offense When the Steelers trotted out their starting 11 personnel, the receivers were DK Metcalf, Michael Pittman, and Roman Wilson. This may have surprised some who expected second-round pick Germie Bernard to get that spot – and there is a very good chance it will be his – but Wilson was a focal point in team drills throughout the first practice. It was hard to count how many times he was targeted, but I would say he was thrown to more than any other pass-catcher during team periods. Now, these were the same things we were seeing in camp this time last year, so do with that information what you will. In individual drills, though, his footwork looked clean, he was agile in his cuts and breaks, and he genuinely looked like a player that has been working to improve and earn real snaps in 2026. Considering where he was drafted two years ago, he will be a name that will be circled during exhibition play. Steelers get the full Drew Allar experience Fans in attendance got the first taste of the quarterback battle between Will Howard and Drew Allar to kickoff camp, and Day One would go to Allar in terms of big plays. The rookie out of Penn State had the two best throws of any quarterback during team drills, ripping a seam shot to Max Hurleman in seven-on-sevens and closing practice with a touchdown pass down the middle to Robert Tonyan from 15 yards out. There were, however, a few throws Allar would have liked to have back. A check down in seven-on-sevens was tipped by Cole Holcomb and picked off by Payton Wilson. Another sideline shot on a corner route was thrown into a tight window and nearly picked. It was admirable seeing him take some chances when others would simply throw three-yard check downs or easy pitches-and-catches to the flat, but you would also like to see a bit more precision on the tight-window throws. Overall, though, it’s a practice he can walk away happy with his performance. Edge rusher deployment and movement T.J. Watt said he and the pass rushers would be moving around, and he wasn’t kidding. He, Alex Highsmith, and Nick Herbig all lined up at multiple spots throughout practice, and were all on the field at the same time at one point. If that is a sign of things to come, fans will be very pleased with Patrick Graham and his usage of the three edge rushers. Big day for Asante Samuel Jr With Jalen Ramsey and Joey Porter Jr both on the PUP list, that opened up opportunities for other defensive backs to shine, and Asante Samuel Jr. took advantage of the extra reps. The Florida State product was the best defensive back on the field, breaking up a pair of passes during team drills. The first was a pass from Rodgers to Pittman on the sideline where Samuel read the play, broke on the ball, and batted it away. The second came on a go ball to DK Metcalf from Rodgers. Samuel stayed with Metaled step for step and broke up the pass at the catch point. Other notes Broderick Jones looks very light. It was good to see him on the field, but he’ll need to bulk up to get to playing weight Brandin Echols picked off Aaron Rodgers in the end zone on a tipped pass that was intended for Darnell Washington The first-team offensive line was from left to right: Troy Fautanu, Mason McCormick, Zach Frazier, Spencer Anderson, Dylan Cook. Jones rotated in at left tackle with Max Iheanachor playing right. Nothing too notable for Germie Bernard, but he did look fast. Aaron Rodgers had a nice tight-window throw to Pat Freiermuth in team drills. Jamel Dean had a nice PBU on a Rodgers pass to Pittman. Let us know what you think in the comments . title: Leonard Williams confirms Seahawks have opened extension talks
summary: One of the Seattle Seahawks’ biggest remaining contract questions may already be moving toward a resolution. Defensive lineman Leonard Williams confirmed during training camp that his representatives and the Seahawks have opened discussions on a contract extension. While the 12-year veteran declined to discuss specifics, he made it clear that both sides are talking. “There’s […]
full_text: One of the Seattle Seahawks’ biggest remaining contract questions may already be moving toward a resolution. Defensive lineman Leonard Williams confirmed during training camp that his representatives and the Seahawks have opened discussions on a contract extension. While the 12-year veteran declined to discuss specifics, he made it clear that both sides are talking. “There’s been few conversations, but nothing set in stone,” Williams said on Tuesday. “We’re all focused on the season starting right now, and we know that that’s towards the end of the season. We have time to figure that out when the time comes.” Williams is entering the final year of the three-year extension he signed after Seattle acquired him from the New York Giants during the 2023 season. Although there is still plenty of time before he would reach free agency, the fact that talks are already underway suggests the Seahawks would prefer to avoid another key player entering the final months of his contract. The timing of those discussions is anything but coincidental. Just days before Williams acknowledged negotiations, the Philadelphia Eagles reset the defensive tackle market by signing Jalen Carter to a four-year, $152 million extension worth $38 million per season , making him the highest-paid interior defensive lineman in NFL history. While Williams is eight years older than Carter and isn’t expected to command a deal anywhere near that figure, elite contracts have a ripple effect across the market. Every new extension is negotiated against the latest benchmark, and Carter’s deal effectively raised the asking price for every high-end defensive tackle seeking a new contract. That creates an interesting challenge for general manager John Schneider. Seattle has already committed significant money to Leonard Williams, Devon Witherspoon, Derick Hall and other core pieces, while Byron Murphy II is going to be extension-eligible next offseason. Locking up Williams now could provide some long-term cost certainty before the market climbs even higher. Despite turning 32 this season, Williams has shown few signs of slowing down and was just named the top defensive tackle in an ESPN survey . He remains one of the NFL’s most complete defensive linemen, capable of generating interior pressure while consistently disrupting the run game. His ability to occupy double teams also creates opportunities for teammates such as Murphy, Hall and the rest of Mike Macdonald’s defensive front. Beyond the production, Williams has become one of Seattle’s most respected veterans since arriving from New York. His leadership and consistency have helped stabilize the defensive line, and his presence was instrumental during the Seahawks’ Super Bowl-winning campaign. Nothing appears imminent, and Williams emphasized that his attention remains on football rather than contract negotiations. Still, confirmation that discussions have already begun is significant. The Seahawks have made it clear they want to keep one of the pillars of their championship defense in Seattle, but after Jalen Carter’s historic extension, doing so may now be considerably more expensive.

title: Seahawks stars Cooper Kupp, Leonard Williams advocate for grass surface at Lumen Field
summary: In the yearly survey run by the NFL Players Association, the Seattle Seahawks received an eyebrow-raising F grade for their home playing surface, the artificial turf at Lumen Field. That’s a grade that stars Leonard Williams and Cooper Kupp want to see changed. Both were asked about the possibility of seeing natural grass return to […]
full_text: In the yearly survey run by the NFL Players Association, the Seattle Seahawks received an eyebrow-raising F grade for their home playing surface, the artificial turf at Lumen Field. That’s a grade that stars Leonard Williams and Cooper Kupp want to see changed. Both were asked about the possibility of seeing natural grass return to Lumen Field after it was used for the 2026 FIFA World Cup, and advocated for the shift on Tuesday. Kupp was the more vocal of the duo, adding that playing on grass makes his body feel significantly better than playing on turf. “It makes a huge difference,” Kupp said. “I know all the metrics and all the data that say the injury rates of this, but I don’t know. I know how I feel. You ask a lot of players who will say the same thing. Whether injury rates change or not, I know how my body feels, everything on turf versus grass. You can ask coaches how their backs feel after standing on the turf versus grass. Coaches have a lot of other issues. But it does make a difference.” Williams echoed a similar sentiment and said he feels that grass lessens the impact on his body when going to the ground. “I understand there’s a lot of things that go into having grass in the stadium that I don’t fully understand yet, but if it was up to a player and it just came down to grass or turf, we obviously prefer grass,” Williams said. The Seahawks players join a growing list of NFL stars who have continued their push for grass fields across the league after several NFL stadiums, including Lumen Field, installed grass fields for the World Cup this summer. Players from across the league, including San Francisco 49ers tight end George Kittle and Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams, have begun a push backed by the NFLPA to institute grass playing surfaces league-wide. However, this advocacy is not new for Kupp or the Seahawks. Back in 2022, Kupp was asked about the same item during his time with the Los Angeles Rams, who play on turf at SoFi Stadium. “We should be on grass,” Kupp said at the time. “That’s all I’m gonna say.” In that same season, former Seahawks safety Quandre Diggs pushed back on turf fields following several non-contact injuries taking place at SoFi. Then Seahawks head coach Pete Carroll helped the push by backing Diggs, saying he’d like to see the debate reevaluated in the offseason, which never happened publicly. Though with the Seahawks in the midst of being sold to a new owner, who clearly has some deep pockets , now could be the perfect time for Seattle’s core players to rally behind the cause and see change, at least in their own stadium.

title: Seahawks’ DeMarcus Lawrence explains why he returned after he was ‘very close’ to retiring
summary: When the Seattle Seahawks hoisted the Lombardi Trophy in February, there was a legitimate possibility that DeMarcus Lawrence had just played the final game of his NFL career. After all, what else was left? The 34-year-old had spent more than a decade chasing a championship, made multiple Pro Bowls, established himself as one of the […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - FEBRUARY 08: QB Drake Maye (10) of the New England Patriots is hit by LB DeMarcus Lawrence (0) of the Seattle Seahawks as he throws during the Seattle Seahawks versus the New England Patriots Super Bowl LX game on February 8, 2026, at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, CA. (Photo by Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images When the Seattle Seahawks hoisted the Lombardi Trophy in February , there was a legitimate possibility that DeMarcus Lawrence had just played the final game of his NFL career. After all, what else was left? The 34-year-old had spent more than a decade chasing a championship, made multiple Pro Bowls, established himself as one of the league’s most respected edge defenders, and finally won the Super Bowl in his first season away from the Dallas Cowboys. Walking away on top would have made perfect sense. As it turns out, Lawrence seriously considered doing exactly that. Speaking with Seattle Sports’ Stacy Rost and Michael Bumpus during training camp, Lawrence admitted that retirement wasn’t simply speculation from the outside—it was a decision he wrestled with throughout the offseason. “I was very close,” Lawrence said during his interview with Seattle Sports’ Bump and Stacy. “Went through a long offseason of going back and forth – am I going to retire, am I not? “I think the one thing that held me steady is… it’s easy to take over a kingdom. But the hard part is when you’ve got the kingdom and now it’s time to defend it. Are you going to sit back and eat the fruits of your labor? Or are you gonna start building up your walls and making sure everything is structurally prepared to defend it? I didn’t want to go out on an easy way. I wanted to make sure I go out on top with a bang to let the whole world know this wasn’t some facade – this was something real.” For Seahawks fans, that’s a remarkable admission considering how confident Mike Macdonald appeared earlier this year that Lawrence would be back. While there were reports shortly after the Super Bowl suggesting retirement was a legitimate possibility , the organization never publicly behaved as though it expected to lose one of its defensive leaders. Ultimately, Lawrence decided he still had enough football left in him. The explanation is as simple as it is important: winning one championship didn’t eliminate his competitive drive. Rather than viewing the Super Bowl as the perfect ending, he saw another opportunity to help Seattle defend its title and continue playing alongside a roster he clearly enjoys being part of. That decision matters for reasons that extend well beyond the stat sheet. Lawrence isn’t expected to carry Seattle’s pass rush by himself. Byron Murphy II, Leonard Williams, Derick Hall, Dante Fowler Jr, and the rest of the defensive front will generate plenty of attention on their own. What Lawrence brings is something that becomes increasingly valuable for a championship team: stability. Last season, the veteran finished with six sacks (with another two in the playoffs) while continuing to be one of Seattle’s most physical run defenders. More importantly, he became an emotional leader inside Mike Macdonald’s defense, setting the tone with his relentless playing style and veteran presence. Younger players consistently pointed toward his preparation and professionalism as examples worth following. That’s difficult to replace, regardless of who might be available on the open market. His comments also serve as a reminder that the Seahawks are operating year-to-year with one of their most respected veterans; Lawrence’s contract expires at the end of the 2027 season. The fact that Lawrence chose to return is great news for Seattle, but it also reinforces that every additional season from this point forward should probably be viewed as a bonus rather than a guarantee. For at least one more year, though, the Seahawks will have one of the defense’s emotional anchors back on the field. And for a team trying to repeat, that’s exactly the decision they were hoping he’d make.

This appealed to McCaffrey as he searched for a new layer to his training and recovery regimen. “It’s almost too much to even give you an answer with words,” McCaffrey said, “but it was a heck of an experience. … He’s a brilliant mind when it comes to movement, the body, the mind, everything.” 49ers’ Kyle Shanahan built a career on quick decisions. A concussion makes lunch feel impossible (paywall) “Shanahan occasionally closed his eyes when he spoke because doing so, he said, felt better when there was too much stimulus. It can be disorienting when multiple people speak to him, and he said the music that pulsates when he observes part of practice was “killing” him. He’s dealing with regular headaches and fatigue and, of course, there’s his indecisiveness: His lunch decisions can require as much thought as how to plan the 49ers’ schedule in the week before their regular-season opener in Melbourne, Australia. The team’s doctors have told Shanahan his injured brain needs to push through pain — to a point. He has a numerical scale to judge the intensity of his headaches — from 1 to 6 — and that’s served as a guide as he’s watched practice film and tackled other duties before leaving the facility far earlier than he’s accustomed. “The whole thing that I used to think was you lay in a dark room and rest — and that’s not it,” Shanahan said. “When your pain’s a 2, they want you to do something to bring it up to a 4. But as soon as it gets there, you’re supposed to stop and let it come down. And then just keep building that muscle. “(On Monday), I was able to watch all the film and I felt like I never got to a 4. And it really excited me. I didn’t have as bad of a headache. And then I got home, and my head started hurting because I just get fatigued. … But it’s so much better. I know I’m going to be all right.” Albert Breer Empties His 49ers Notebook From Training Camp Stop in Santa Clara “This isn’t a faux absence. Shanahan’s not disconnected. But offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak has the walkie talkie that goes to Brock Purdy’s helmet, and the head coach is watching like a personnel guy might at training camp. For now, the Niners are encouraged with Shanahan’s progress, with the caveat that it hasn’t been, and won’t be, linear. There’ll be ups and downs. He’s contributing where he can. His body is healing nicely. The concussion is lingering a bit. The hope is he’s back soon. And as for what the team is missing most at the moment, everyone I asked brought up the absence of his team meetings. Rather than try and replicate them, the Niners have put those on ice for now, breaking into offensive and defensive meetings with the coordinators for the time they’re scheduled. We’ve got more coming on all that tomorrow.” Ricky Pearsall misses 49ers training camp practice with concerning knee flare-up “Tight end Jake Tonges, who could play a big role with George Kittle’s status uncertain early in the season, is having a good camp. He caught a pair of passes from Jones on Wednesday.” The Good and Not So Good from Day 3 of 49ers Camp: Ricky Pearsall Injures Knee Again “Intercepted his second pass in three days of camp. Today, he intercepted a pass that was intended for Jacob Cowing and thrown by Mac Jones (more on him in a minute). Jack Jones takes lots of risks and gets burned occasionally, but he’s also a playmaker, arguably the biggest one in the secondary. Renardo Green is good as well, but he’s not a playmaker….[Stout] gave up a 10-yard catch to Robinson on 3rd and 7, but also broke up two short passes that were intended for Stribling. Stout is having an outstanding training camp, but he hasn’t faced any elite wide receivers yet. He’ll have a tougher task when the season starts and he has to face Puka Nacua.” 49ers injuries (including to Ricky Pearsall) mounting again, while Brock Purdy rebounds (paywall) “Following a Monday practice in which aggressive defensive backs got their hands on a lot of passes, Purdy and the other quarterbacks had a measure of revenge. Purdy was 14-of-18 during the team portion of practice, including on a crisp crossing-route throw to Demarcus Robinson that was just beyond the reach of linebacker Fred Warner.” 49ers offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak shares training camp updates “San Francisco 49ers offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak spoke with reporters after Wednesday’s training camp practice. Here’s everything he had to say.” 49ers work out 3 wide receivers after the Ricky Pearsall injury news “Bachman, listed at 6’, 190 pounds, was with the Raiders in 2025. The 30-year-old caught two passes for 12 yards with Vegas last year and had three receptions for 31 yards in 2024. Bachman was an undrafted free agent out of the 2019 NFL Draft. Eskridge is a name that should sound familiar. He was a second-round draft pick by the Seahawks back in 2021. Eskridge spent the previous two seasons in Mike McDaniel’s offense. title: How one free agent’s ‘presence’ has taken over the 49ers locker room
summary: The San Francisco 49ers were lauded for their moves in free agency this offseason, which catapulted them up many power rankings ahead of the season. While the major move that the team made was landing wide receiver Mike Evans, another impactful addition came on the defensive side of the ball with the return of linebacker […]
full_text: The San Francisco 49ers were lauded for their moves in free agency this offseason, which catapulted them up many power rankings ahead of the season. While the major move that the team made was landing wide receiver Mike Evans, another impactful addition came on the defensive side of the ball with the return of linebacker Dre Greenlaw. Greenlaw had been an ascending dominant force through his six-year career in San Francisco before leaving for the Denver Broncos last season. But after only playing in eight games last year before being released, Greenlaw is now back as the LB2 in San Francisco alongside Fred Warner. While he’s looking to prove himself again, the veteran linebacker has already made his presence known in the 49ers locker room. “It’s huge,” Brock Purdy said of having Greenlaw’s presence around. “Obviously when he came back, it was like one of our brothers that came back. It’s almost like let’s pick up where we left off after that season when he left. Just his presence. The dawg that he has when he steps on the field, it’s like everybody feeds off that kind of energy. “Being on offense, I’ll look across the ball and be like, ‘oh shoot’, you got Dre Greenlaw next to Fred [Warner] again, and they’re flying around, and they’re filling the gaps like you can feel them. Just having him in our locker room and his presence, man, it’s a real thing. He looks out for all the young guys too; he’s a real brother. The minute that dude steps on the field, you got to be ready. And we all just want to go to war with him. I think it was a huge addition to get him back.” Cornerback Deommodore Lenoir was also hyped up to play with Greenlaw again, noting the linebacker’s mentality and intensity. “He’s the bully. We got our bully back,” Lenoir chuckled. “I was mad when he left cause I know the intensity he plays with. He’s gonna go 110 percent every game, every practice. I know that he’s gonna give it his all.” But of course, no player is happier to have Greenlaw back than his running partner Fred Warner. “It’s just been special from the moment he gave me that phone call telling me he was coming back,” Warner said of Greenlaw. “It’s been super special. Then today, kind of met every expectation. Even days leading up to today, I’ve been having to tell him like, ‘Hey bro, relax,’ because he’s been amped up and ready to go. It’s just great having him back. “Like I’ve always talked about, he’s one of the best football players I’ve ever played with, and his passion for the game, his mentality, having a guy like that beside you just gives you so much confidence as a player to go out there and rock out. It’s great having him back.” Reports from the first two days of training camp indicated that Greenlaw has been flying around to start camp, picking up where he left off with the 49ers. If that’s the case, it’s a great sign for the 49ers, who are looking for better results defensively after injuries hit the unit last season.
author: Rohan Chakravarthi

And then they said the visor really gashed me. … I took my eyes off the road looking for my phone, and my car veered into someone. “It’s one of those roads where there’s no forgiveness. … When I hit her, the impact was just so, I’ll just never forget how violent it was.” …..While Shanahan is healing well, he does not yet have a timeline for when he expects to return to coaching full time. He cites fatigue as one of his biggest obstacles, noting he had a good day Monday but was feeling a bit worse Tuesday. But Shanahan also wanted to clarify that while his concussion was serious, he did not have amnesia and never lost consciousness. Most of all, the coach said he wanted to make sure that someone else wasn’t getting the blame for something he did. “It just crushed me hearing the girl get blamed for it,” Shanahan said. “I’m just lucky that I survived, that she didn’t get hurt and that I didn’t lose my eye.” 49ers signing LB Quinton Bell to a one-year deal “The then-Oakland Raiders selected Bell out of Prairie View A&M in the seventh round (No. 230 overall) of the 2019 NFL Draft. title: Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles isn’t worried about ‘distractions’ heading into camp
summary: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers opened training camp with two contract situations hanging over the organization, but head coach Todd Bowles does not expect either to derail the team’s preparation. full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - JULY 29: Vita Vea #50 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers talks with head coach Todd Bowles during training camp at AdventHealth Training Center on July 29, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tampa Bay Buccaneers opened training camp with two contract situations hanging over the organization, but head coach Todd Bowles does not expect either to derail the team’s preparation. Quarterback Baker Mayfield is entering the final year of his contract after extension talks failed to produce an agreement. Meanwhile, defensive tackle Vita Vea has reportedly requested a trade following his unsuccessful push for a new deal. But Bowles is focused on what goes on at the practice facility for now. “Well, there [are] players every year [that] you’re going to have them [with]. These happen to be two of our biggest players,” Bowles said . “We haven’t had two of our biggest in a while, but we’ve had players every year. It just hasn’t been of that magnitude. But, it’s always about football. There [are] always going to be distractions just like there are on game day. There are going to be sudden changes and there are going to be sudden changes on the field. We have a very professional and mature group with a lot of leadership there, starting with Baker. So, he makes sure that’s separate. He makes sure the team knows that’s separate. Like I said, we’re not going to make this training camp about what he signed or what he didn’t sign or it being his contract year. We’re just going to play ball.” Bowles acknowledging that Mayfield and Vea are two of Tampa Bay’s most important players, he’s also acknowledging the circumstances are larger than the typical training-camp issue. Still, he expressed confidence in the professionalism and leadership inside the locker room. For Bowles, the message is clear: negotiations may continue away from the field, but the Buccaneers will not allow them to define their camp.

Head coach Todd Bowles said Wirfs is considered day-to-day, though the team is still determining the severity of the injury. Wirfs did not participate in Tampa Bay’s first practice, leaving the Buccaneers to proceed cautiously with the veteran cornerstone of their offensive line. “He tweaked [his hamstring] in the running test, so we left him inside to get treatment,” said Bowles . “Right now, I’m not sure (when he’ll return). I’ll know more today. I would hope it’s not long, but we’ll see.” Any absence for Wirfs is undoubtedly significant. The five-time Pro Bowler remains Baker Mayfield’s premier blindside protector and one of the NFL’s elite offensive tackles. Tampa Bay already experienced life without him last season after a knee procedure forced Wirfs to miss the first three games. There is no indication yet that the hamstring issue will threaten his availability for the regular season. Still, after injuries disrupted his 2025 campaign, the Buccaneers will prioritize getting Wirfs fully healthy rather than rushing him back during the opening weeks of camp.

Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images | Steve Roberts-Imagn Images The Tennessee Titans have their first training camp practice on Wednesday. One of the big storylines is the new-look wide receiver room. Sophomore Elic Ayomanor is tasked with navigating how he fits in Brian Daboll’s offense. The Titans signed Wan’Dale Robinson to a four-year, $70 million contract in free agency. Mike Borgonzi doubled down on Cam Ward’s development by drafting Carnell Tate with the fourth overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft. Like Chimere Dike, Ayomanor is a sophomore trying to navigate all the newness. Last season, the Titans were overly reliant on Ayomanor, the third of three fourth-round picks they made in 2025. Ayomanor finished second on the Titans in receiving yards (515) and tied for first in touchdowns (4, with fellow rookie Dike). The former Stanford standout placed fifth in receptions with 41. Ayomanor and Dike unexpectedly ended up in starring roles. Calvin Ridley suffered a season-ending injury during the first half of the campaign. Veteran Tyler Lockett was released after proving to be ineffective. Ayomanor and Dike were asked to pick up the slack. By adding Robinson and Tate, and retaining Ridley, the Titans are far better prepared at receiver. The assumption is that Tate will be the starting X receiver. Robinson is a slot, and both Ridley and Dike can play the Z position. Ayomanor is a throwback X receiver. He’s obviously not going to beat-out Tate for that role. The Titans could move personnel around, with Tate, Robinson, and Dike all being flexible enough to play different positions. Ayomanor could find himself at X in certain packages. Ayomanor was a useful receiver as a rookie throughout the 2025 season. The Titans desperately needed to get better at the pass-catching spots though, and that’s precisely what they did this offseason, to better support Ward. Ayomanor must navigate those challenges and compete for reps.

title: Washington Commanders already have quality offensive weapons entering camp
summary: The Commanders need more weapons. This is all we have been hearing from the national and local media and, of course, the fans. Much of the offseason focus was trying to get a true complement opposite receiver Terry McLaurin in an attempt to get quarterback Jayden Daniels more weapons. Although those efforts went largely unrewarded, […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - JANUARY 18: Jayden Daniels #5 of the Washington Commanders celebrates with Terry McLaurin #17 after defeating the Detroit Lions 45-31 in the NFC Divisional Playoff at Ford Field on January 18, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Commanders need more weapons. This is all we have been hearing from the national and local media and, of course, the fans. Much of the offseason focus was trying to get a true complement opposite receiver Terry McLaurin in an attempt to get quarterback Jayden Daniels more weapons. Although those efforts went largely unrewarded, there is some reason for fans to be optimistic about what Washington currently has on the team. Training camp started this week and the talk still centers around Washington adding another offensive weapon to the roster — and there is a chance they very well may. The national media is projecting veteran Stefon Diggs to Washington , while Brandon Aiyuk is projecting himself as a Commander. But what if the offensive weapons fans so desperately desire are staring us right in the face? Weapons, you say? I’ll give you weapons! Before we dive head-first into the offensive weapons Washington currently has, let’s first talk a bit about scheme. This new offense that coordinator David Blough is set to roll out projects to be run-focused, with multiple tight end sets. This could mean heavy doses of 12 personnel (one running back, two tight ends), and even some three tight end looks. With each tight end added, you can essentially assume a wide receiver is subtracted. If Blough uses a heavy dose of 12 personnel, that means just two wide receivers would be on the field. I’m not pointing this out to try and diminish the need for more playmakers at the wide receiver position, however It’s definitely something that has to be factored in when accounting for weapons in this new-look offense. Now, onto the fun part… Weapons Quarterback: Washington has one of the best dual-threat quarterbacks in the league in Jayden Daniels . Only Lamar Jackson may be considered more lethal as a runner, either by design or when the defense turns their back on him in the passing game. Getting a true weapon more weapons is a fun problem to have! Running back: Bill Croskey-Merritt was a bit one-dimensional as a rookie, catching just nine passes for 68 yards . So, what did Adam Peters do? He signed veteran Rachaad White . The 27-year-old has averaged 51 receptions, 363 receiving yards and three touchdowns per season over his four-year career. Cannot wait to see Rachaad White take plays like this to the house in the Burgundy & Gold #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/jvy3V3j6iP — brandon (@JayDanielsMVP) June 28, 2026 Don’t forget, both of these backs are capable of toting the rock as well, with Croskey-Merritt collecting 805 yards and eight touchdowns as a rookie, while White had a 990-yard, six-touchdown year his second season in Tampa Bay. Bill has home-run speed, while White, who is not quite as fast, is no slouch in that department either. Tight end: This is where things begin to get fun… Adam Peters needed more from the tight end room in an offense that is projected to feature a lot of underneath routes designed to produce chunks of YAC. He went out and signed the 6’3” 238-pound Chig Okonkwo to act as Blough’s new JUMBO receiver. Yes, you are reading this right – I did say JUMBO receiver! I don't think people realize how close Trey Burks and Chig Okonkwo profile athletically. Chig is an undersized TE. Burks is an oversized WR. Chig is faster and in the 96th percentile for TEs. Most sites have Chig at 238lbs too. Chig is basically a glorified WR. #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/OaLIBXqeMh — George Carmi (@Gcarmi21) July 25, 2026 Chig is a 4.5-second 40-yard-dash guy who excels with the ball in his hands after the catch. He offers very little as a blocker, so calling him a true tight end is a bit of a stretch, however, he forced 13 missed tackles (4th best among tight ends in the NFL) while his 345 yards after the catch were ninth best last year in Tennessee, so he’s very capable of creating yards with the ball in his hands. Aside from Chig, Washington also has third-year pro Ben Sinnott . He was the No. 53 overall pick in the 2024 NFL draft, but was used sparingly by former offensive coordinator Kliff Kingsbury during his first two seasons. He can double as an H-back operating out of the backfield but, athletically, he profiles like today’s Move-TEs, with a 4.68 40, a 40-inch vertical and a 6.82 3-cone drill. When he has been targeted, he has produced! Driscoll hits Sinnott down the seam for BIG gain. Watch Ben fight for extra yardage at the end 💪🏻💪🏻💪🏻 pic.twitter.com/drAEwU0q0q — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) August 10, 2024 Receiver: Terry McLaurin is coming off a down, injury-plagued season which saw him play in just 9.5 games, posting career lows in receptions (38), yards (582) and touchdowns (3). At 31, Terry may not be the same explosive athlete he was early in his career but make no doubt about it – he’s still a weapon on the outside. Peters swung for the fences in free agency, reportedly prepared to offer Colts WR Alec Pierce a massive deal. Ultimately, Pierce wound up re-signing in Indy. Peters was also in on Packers free agent receiver Romeo Doubs, who would up in New England. Peters was forced to settle on veterans Dyami Brown and Van Jefferson, with the draft just around the corner. There were definitely eyes on Carnell Tate (fourth overall to the Titans) and Jordyn Tyson (eighth overall to the Saints) in the draft, but Peters sat tight and landed what he felt was a first-round talent in Antonio Williams at pick 71. At a tad under 6-0 and now around 190 pounds, Williams ran a 4.41 40 at the combine , while posting nearly 40” in the vertical. He’s known as a savvy route runner who can operate on the outside or from the slot and is dangerous with the ball in his hands after the catch. He had a down year in 2025 on a Clemson offense that certainly wasn’t clicking on all cylinders, but if you look at his 2024 season, you’ll see the talent the young man possesses (75 receptions, 904 receiving yards, 11 touchdowns). Jayden Daniels has a new weapon in Antonio Williams 🔥 pic.twitter.com/l7McFBp7Lu — SleeperNFL (@SleeperNFL) April 25, 2026 Some others to watch are: Dyami Brown – deep threat who has some rapport with Jayden Luke McCaffrey – big-bodied receiver who has inside/outside versatility and good speed/quickness Treylon Burks – former first rounder who can win with play strength Jaylin Lane – blazer who is still learning the nuances of the position *As of this writing, there is still a chance Washington adds another player to the wide receiver room. 12/21 Personnel Scenario: QB: Jayden Daniels RB: Rachaad White TE/Jumbo WR: Chig Okonkwo TE: Ben Sinnott WR: Terry McLaurin WR: Antonio Williams With the above lineup, you don’t know what Washington is going to do. With two TEs (one who does well as a blocker), and a capable runner in the backfield in White, Blough could choose to run outside zone if Jayden sees a six-man front. If the defense chooses to stack the box, Washington has two outside threats in McLaurin and Williams, a mismatch threat against a safety or linebacker in Okonkwo and a dangerous weapon out of the backfield in White who can beat most linebackers in this league in the open field. The beautiful part of this look is playaction. Washington can line up under center with Sinnott in the HIP and show OZ left, only to have Jayden pull and have Terry, Antonio and Chig on a high-to-low vertical read (backside post, bang 9-route to clear and deep out). If Jayden likes what he sees, he can pull the trigger. If he sees open field, he can tuck it and run. In this scenario, who does the defense give the attention to? Who may be the guy who gets bracketed? 11 Personnel Scenario : QB: Jayden Daniels RB: Bill Croskey-Merritt TE: Ben Sinnott WR: Terry McLaurin WR: Antonio…

title: Commanders ‘tired of losing,’ fueled by 2025 entering new training camp
summary: The Commanders did not enjoy their 2025 experience. A 5-12 record, on the heels of an NFC title game appearance, will create such sentiment.   The page has been turned toward a 2026 campaign full of optimism after hiring new offensive and defensive coordinators and adding tons of talent via free agency and the draft. […]
full_text: The Commanders did not enjoy their 2025 experience. A 5-12 record , on the heels of an NFC title game appearance , will create such sentiment. The page has been turned toward a 2026 campaign full of optimism after hiring new offensive and defensive coordinators and adding tons of talent via free agency and the draft. That said, the Commanders have been asked at the start of this training camp how they compartmentalized last season and let it impact this go-round. Head coach Dan Quinn has promised an ultra-competitive camp. He has demanded players start camp in tip-top shape. The players are willing to try new things to get right after last year’s disappointment. “(We’re) tried of losing,” defensive back Jeremy Reaves said after Wednesday’s practice, via 7News-DC’s Scott Abraham . “Last year – it sucked. Nobody likes losing games, especially when you had the year we had the year before. It’s frustrating.” Jeremy Reaves “we are tired of losing” pic.twitter.com/YyUJIi1R2r — Scott Abraham (@Scott7news) July 29, 2026 The Commanders are confident in a quick turnaround, because of the upgraded talent and schematics now in place. “It’d be crazy not to say you wouldn’t take that lesson and pull it forward and apply it, but it is about the here, the now,” Quinn said in a Tuesday press conference . “I’m excited for you guys to feel the energy of the team. Their readiness, their swagger. So, as we get started into this, I’m excited for you guys to feel that.” There are several Commanders from that 12-5 2024 regular season and playoff run who know what it takes to win. They’re hungry for a return to glory. While quarterback Jayden Daniels has vowed to put 2025 in the past, he said it had an impact on his offseason prep for this training camp. “It left a bitter taste in my mouth,” Daniels said. “You kind of move forward and go out and get better and get back at it. You can’t really rush the days until the season gets back, but you attack it with a different mindset, a different approach to things.”
author: Scott Bair

title: What newcomer Rasul Douglas can bring to Commanders cornerback corps
summary: Rasul Douglas reported to Commanders training camp on Tuesday as the new student in class. The veteran cornerback reportedly agreed on terms of a contract on July 6 – the team announced the deal on July 9 – during the NFL dead period. He was officially signed to the roster on Monday after Nick Bellore retired. […]
full_text: Rasul Douglas reported to Commanders training camp on Tuesday as the new student in class. The veteran cornerback reportedly agreed on terms of a contract on July 6 – the team announced the deal on July 9 – during the NFL dead period. He was officially signed to the roster on Monday after Nick Bellore retired. Douglas wasn’t around for the offseason program and therefore didn’t get the scheme knowledge or the team bonding time typically gleaned during the spring. He had, however, previously played with fellow corner Amik Robertson during the 2021 offseason and camp and trained with Antonio Hamilton Sr. and Nick Cross. That was the extent of his Commanders familiarity. That’s not the first time the journeyman has been in such a predicament. It happened in Miami last year, so Douglas has learned to adapt quickly. “Just be ready,” Douglas said during a Wednesday press conference. “I’ve been a lot of places. Last year I came in to Miami two days before the first game, and then in the 10th play of the game I’m out there. I didn’t know what’s going on, but the coach told me he let me know before every play. It’s different, but you have to make sure you’re ready when the opportunities come.” Douglas said he’s trying to learn the system and the Commanders culture on the fly, with the goal of immersing himself in it more every day. He doesn’t enter the situation needing to be a top player right away. There’s quality in the cornerback room, even with Trey Amos remaining on active/PUP , dealing with soft-tissue soreness. Mike Sainristil and Robertson have been defensive leaders early on, and Antonio Hamilton is back with Washington , so adding Douglas was a luxury signing meant to bolster the position group. “We’re always looking to add really good players, and Rasul’s been a really good player in this league for a long time,” general manager Adam Peters said in a Tuesday presser . “He’s played at a high level. He’s started a lot of games. He started a lot of games recently, and he always performs. So, when you have an opportunity to add to that room, it’s not a deficiency in the room at all. You just want to make each room as strong as it can be. So, getting him in, we’re really excited about that. And we just got a chance to meet him yesterday. He’s big, and he’s played a lot of good ball.” Peters is right on all counts. While Douglas has bounced around, he has 93 starts over 135 games during his nine NFL seasons , including essentially every-down work with four teams over the past six seasons. Douglas is known as a ballhawk and promised to be a turnover generator in Washington. That’s warranted, considering he has 21 career interceptions and three pick sixes. If the Commanders need Douglas to step into a starting role at some point in 2026, or if he earns a spot outright through competition, he’ll be ready. “A player who’s going to give his all,” Douglas said. “I’m going to be passionate about the game. I like celebrating. I just like making plays, honestly. That’s all I think about is making plays and helping the team win as best I can.”
author: Scott Bair

title: Commanders morning briefing: Terry McLaurin’s ‘joy,’ Laremy Tunsil
summary: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn spoke to the media on Wednesday morning before Washington’s first training camp practice, something he’ll do regularly this summer. He hit on a number of topics before the practice session, which we’ll highlight here. — Quinn was asked about receiver Terry McLaurin, and whether his presence during the offseason program […]
full_text: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn spoke to the media on Wednesday morning before Washington’s first training camp practice, something he’ll do regularly this summer. He hit on a number of topics before the practice session, which we’ll highlight here. — Quinn was asked about receiver Terry McLaurin, and whether his presence during the offseason program and camp was quantifiable after he held-in during most of the 2025 season prep dealing with a contract dispute. While numbers may not support the impact, McLaurin’s presence can be felt. The anecdote below shows how McLaurin is making an impact beyond his talent. Dan Quinn gives a great example of how Terry McLaurin is playing with joy. (Video courtesy @wusa9 on YouTube) pic.twitter.com/pwgDViCV65 — COMMANDERS FOOTBALL (@HogsHaven) July 29, 2026 — Left tackle Laremy Tunsil is ready for another season anchoring the offensive line, and Quinn can tell he’s already at his best. “He has a really high standard,” Quinn said. “That’s what I see. He’s rarely out of position. He has a good way of asking questions. He’s the superstar player who’s not afraid to get coached or corrected or to ask something. The thing I have been most impressed by is how cool a teammate he has been. The guys here love spending time with him and going down to where he’s training to spend time. Those are the small markers that you think of, that guys are going to seek him out. “I remember last year, he told Josh (Conerly Jr.), ‘just get on a plane and come see me. Moments like that go unnoticed, about the teammate he is. The skill is there. He’s in fantastic shape coming in. … It’s incredible. He has a presence. He’s fit. He’s strong. He’s ready. He has been a really good teammate. That doesn’t show up on a stat sheet or when you’re looking into free agency and trades — there was more there than I even thought about the impact on other people he makes. I feel really fortunate that he’s here. — Quinn said that Dorance Armstrong (knee) and Deatrich Wise Jr. (quad) are making progress while remaining on the active/PUP list. They’ll continue to work on the side during practice, and Quinn said both guys have “turned corners” and hit markers in the rehab process. That doesn’t mean a return for either player is imminent, though Armstrong is getting closer. — The Commanders are in the middle of a required ramp up period to start camp, and Quinn said the Commanders will use it to work heavily on red-zone situations. He also said that the camp will be separated into blocks and install sections, all with an emphasis on creating a super competitive camp with stakes.
author: Scott Bair

full_text: The Daily Slop – 29 July 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles Bullock’s Film Room (subscription) Camp Battle: Leo Chenal vs Frankie Luvu at ILB [T]he Commanders also have some interesting battles for starting positions this year too. Earlier in the offseason I broke down the camp battle that is set to take place for the starting left guard position between Chris Paul and Brandon Coleman . Today though, I’m flipping to the defensive side of the ball to look at one of the most intriguing battles this year, at least in my opinion. The Commanders completely turned over their inside linebacker position this offseason. Leo Chenal was signed in free agency and then Washington drafted Sonny Styles with the seventh overall pick. We’re anticipating Daronte Jones to switch the Commanders to a 3-4 base defense, which is what Jones coached with the Vikings over the last few years. If that is the case, then the Commanders only have two inside linebacker positions available and multiple options to fill them. I think it’s fair to assume that Styles will ultimately start at one spot, at least the team will expect him to win the job given they took him so high in the draft. But who starts next to him? Leo Chenal was just signed in free agency but Frankie Luvu looks to be an excellent fit in the new scheme. Who wears the green dot? I asked #Commanders HC Dan Quinn what are the factors in ultimately deciding who wears the green dot. Take a watch/listen. @BowieTVSports pic.twitter.com/R9eRecxDvN — CWallSports (@cwallse) July 29, 2026 Dan Quinn RE: the green dot: "Sonny (Styles) is more than capable of doing that. Frankie (Luvu) as well. … Learning that command is part of the position. Quinn said they could have a safety wear the green dot, but it'll likely be a linebacker. — Nicki Jhabvala (@NickiJhabvala) July 28, 2026 I’ll caveat this piece by saying there are numerous ways the Commanders could get all three of Styles, Chenal and Luvu on the field at the same time and I’ve written about that previously . But I suspect there will be times where one of them has to sit on the bench and again, I doubt it will be the guy they drafted seventh overall. So that means Chenal and Luvu will be battling in camp for the starting spot next to Styles in the base 3-4 defense. Both are good football players with a lot of talent and the competition should drive both to improve and become even better players. But who will win out, the newly added free agent or the veteran tone setter? One of the most intriguing camp battles to watch in Washington will be who starts next to Sonny Styles. Frankie Luvu and Leo Chenal both have strong cases to make. I broke down the Commanders ILB battle: https://t.co/55qai4v9hs pic.twitter.com/xMuB8y2VRi — Mark Bullock (@MarkBullockNFL) July 28, 2026 Commanders Roundtable With Tress Way injured, Commanders add another punter to roster With Way now absent, the Commanders made a move to fill the immediate vacancy after the agent of longtime NFL punter Matt Haack announced his signing with the Commanders. Congratulations to former @ASUFootball and NFL vet, Matt Haack on signing with the @Commanders ! In 7 games with the @AZCardinals in 2025, he averaged 51.3 yards per punt with 40% of his punts Inside the 20! LET'S GO! pic.twitter.com/CMvfcg6Yxo — Paul Sheehy (@ProStarSports) July 28, 2026 An undrafted free agent out of Arizona State from the 2017 NFL Draft, Haack spent his first four seasons of his NFL career with the Miami Dolphins before stints with the Buffalo Bills, Indianapolis Colts, Arizona Cardinals, Cleveland Browns, Buffalo Bills, New York Giants and Jacksonville Jaguars. In 2025, Haack began the season on the practice squad of the Denver Broncos before heading to the Arizona Cardinals in November where he appeared in seven games. The Washington Commanders have signed veteran punter Matt Haack as Tress Way recovers from a pectoral injury. Way, a three-time Pro Bowler, is expected to miss time during training camp but is not anticipated to be sidelined long term. Haack provides an experienced replacement… pic.twitter.com/ANJw0P8iJw — Green 19 Football (@Green19Football) July 28, 2026 Through his nine seasons and 110 games in the NFL, Haack owns a 45 yard punt average and a 39.9 yard net punt with 179 punts pinned inside the 20 and 26 touchbacks. How much he’s able to capitalize on the opportunity will be a question for the ensuing weeks to answer given the lack of any question about the long-term status at the position. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Commanders.com 5 takeaways from Adam Peters and Dan Quinn’s training camp opening press conference The Commanders’ biggest challenge with the position is figuring out how roles will be divided among the players. Players like Mike Sainristil and Robertson have experience playing on the outside and in the slot, which should serve them well considering how much emphasis the Commanders’ new scheme places on versatility. There are other players, like Amos, who have more specific skill sets, and the Commanders want to take their time deciding where players can make the biggest impact. “I think that in itself is going to be some intrigue, and it’ll take a few weeks for us to get to that space,” Quinn said. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Sports Illustrated Why the Commanders Believe Nick Allegretti Can Win Their Starting Center Job Dan Quinn noted that he has consistently practiced across the interior. He’s played center, he’s played guard, even though you may not have seen him in some of the games; like, every week he was, you know, repping inside to go. So, that was a big piece of it. We’ve got a lot of faith and confidence in him. It’s another one of the positions that we do have competition that we’re going for.Commanders Head Coach Dan Quinn If Nick was playing on defense, he’d be a green dot. This is one of the smartest guys on our team now. Like, we talk about putting it under control; that’s part of playing center. And he has that targeting. ‘Who’s this? Where’s the protection going?’ So, we’ve got a lot of confidence in him. He is one hell of a competitor. And so, he’s one of those guys, man, you don’t bet against that. You know? Might be new, but you don’t do that with everybody, but somebody for him, you no doubt you do it .Commanders Head Coach Dan Quinn Clearly, Quinn likes Allegretti a great deal. That said, Quinn likely meant Allegretti processes information quickly, communicates clearly, and is trusted to make decisions when things become chaotic. While Dan Quinn loves Allegretti’s intelligence, Adam Peters stressed his leadership qualities , including Allegretti’s ability to command the situation. What stands out to me with Nick is just his leadership, his command, his confidence. The way the guys gravitate and listen to him. And so, that’s a big part of it. Knowing what to do, knowing where to go, knowing where to direct the guys. Just the calling up in the huddle. It’s a big deal. So, have a ton of confidence in him, have a ton of confidence in [C] Julian [Good-Jones] and [C] Matt [Gulbin] too. So, it’ll be a great competition. But, you know, for Nick, just, you know, I think the world of him. And so, we all have confidence in him.Commanders GM Adam Peters To read more of this article, CLICK HERE The Athletic (paywall) Pre-training camp NFL Power Rankings 23. title: Commanders injury news: Punter signed for camp with Tress Way sidelined
summary: UPDATE July 29, 4 p.m.: The Commanders placed P Tress Way on the active/non-football injury list and LB Kain Medrano on the active physically unable to perform list. Both guys will count against Washington’s roster limit and can participate in team activities outside of practice. This is merely a procedural move, so they can be […]
full_text: UPDATE July 29, 4 p.m.: The Commanders placed P Tress Way on the active/non-football injury list and LB Kain Medrano on the active physically unable to perform list. Both guys will count against Washington’s roster limit and can participate in team activities outside of practice. This is merely a procedural move, so they can be placed on regular-season NFI/PUP lists should they incur unexpected setbacks. The Commanders made a series of roster moves on Wednesday morning, before their first practice of this 2026 training camp. They signed receiver River Cracraft and punter Matt Haack (more on that later), released edge rusher Andre Carter and tight end Anthony Firkser and activated cornerback Fred Davis II off the non-football injury list. We have made the following roster moves: – Signed WR River Cracraft and P Matt Haack – Released OLB Andre Carter and TE Anthony Firkser – Activated CB Fred Davis II off the Active/Non-Football Illness List pic.twitter.com/RqKA74jvrj — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) July 29, 2026 Washington Commanders general manager Adam Peters and head coach Dan Quinn spoke to the media on Tuesday and said punter Tress Way is dealing with a pectoral injury and won’t be practicing to start camp. Peters said the injury isn’t expected to keep the Pro Bowler sidelined for too long, and he will be working on the side field. GM Adam Peters shares an update on P Tress Way and LB Kain Medrano pic.twitter.com/Ir5E5u1f1G — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) July 28, 2026 Haack will likely be the team’s punter until Way is cleared. Way is also one of the best holders in the league, a job that Haack will inherit, and one that will be important in the kicking battle between incumbent Jake Moody and UDFA rookie Drew Stevens. Peters also mentioned that second-year LB Kain Medrano is dealing with a hamstring injury from offseason training. The Commanders placed three players on the active/PUP list on Saturday, and they aren’t expected to be ready to start camp on the practice fields with the rest of the team. Adam Peters said that Trey Amos is still sidelined due to some soft tissue soreness. The second-year CB suffered a fractured fibula during a loss to the Lions on Nov. 9, ending his rookie campaign. Washington signed veteran Rasul Douglas last week, and added veterans Amik Robertson and Akhello Witherspoon earlier this year in free agency. Adam Peters says CB Trey Amos (fractured fibula) remains sidelined because he felt some soft tissue soreness this offseason. Added that the staff is being cautious here but Amos is in a good position overall. — Ben Standig (@BenStandig) July 28, 2026 Quinn said in a Wednesday morning press conference that Dorance Armstrong and Deatrich Wise Jr., with Amost on PUP, will be working on the side during practices and are making solid progress. Quinn also said that Armstrong is getting closer to a return from a torn ACL that occurred last season. While Dorance Armstrong and Deatrich Wise remain on PUP, Dan Quinn said this morning that they'll be working on the side during practice. "They've turned corners" and "hit markers" in rehab. DQ said that Armstrong is "super close in that space." No exact return timetable. — COMMANDERS FOOTBALL (@HogsHaven) July 29, 2026
